author.name: Beomsik Cho, Jinhyeong Kim, Dongseok Lee, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Shows that confidence-based response scoring imported from text LLMs barely changes when the input image is removed, meaning such scores track textual plausibility rather than visual grounding. LookBack is a training-free scorer that instead measures how much a response actually uses visual references, improving detection of image-ungrounded hallucinations.

entry.title: Do You See What You Draw? A Semantic Closed-Loop Framework for Holistic Evaluation of Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Hao Zhang, Jiaxin Qi, Zhijiang Tang, Jianqiang Huang

entry.summary: Introduces an annotation-free evaluation loop for unified multimodal models: the model generates an image from a description and then must answer questions about its own output, closing a semantic loop between generation and understanding. This probes whether unification in a single parameter space actually produces consistent capability rather than two separate skills.

entry.title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability

author.name: Long Hoang Nguyen, Eva Sp\"athe, Sebastian Lins, Ali Sunyaev

entry.summary: Argues that some configurations of actors, systems, and institutions make AI accountability conceptually impossible rather than merely difficult, introducing the notion of constitutive unaccountability. Built from a literature analysis plus secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews spanning technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds.

entry.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

author.name: Zile Zhou, Huining Yuan, Weichen Zhang, Xinlei Chen, Xiao-ping Zhang

entry.summary: SCOUT combines a structured chain-of-thought that explicitly models 3D perception including depth with a process-supervised RL algorithm using multi-objective rewards, targeting poor credit assignment across intermediate spatial reasoning steps. Aims to improve robustness of vision-language spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Redistribution-based Cost Inference Improves Sparse Safe Offline RL

author.name: Ebenezer Gelo (University of the Witwatersrand), Geraud Nangue Tasse (University of the Witwatersrand), Steven James (University of the Witwatersrand), Benjamin Rosman (University of the Witwatersrand)

entry.summary: Addresses safe offline RL when supervisors only provide trajectory-level stop-feedback at the first unsafe transition rather than dense per-step costs, framing it as temporal credit assignment. Return-equivalent redistribution converts the sparse signal into dense per-step costs, which the authors show preserves the feasible policy set and optimal Lagrangian while improving cost critic conditioning.

entry.title: Orientation, not magnitude: the causal structure of task-vector interference in merged language models

author.name: Chencheng Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzes why task-arithmetic model merging fails, tracking the exact layerwise cross-term and finding that magnitude-based diagnostics are insufficient and inconsistent across model families. Interference is dominated by amplifying transport of the cross-term, which is rebuilt by propagation unless intervention happens near the output, pointing to orientation rather than magnitude as the causal axis.

entry.title: SoftWater: Class-Aware Rate Allocation for Softmax Quantization

author.name: Joao V. Cavalcanti, Ashia C. Wilson

entry.summary: SoftWater treats quantization of the softmax output layer as a rate-distortion problem under KL divergence, exploiting a class-aware geometry in which error is weighted by feature covariance and per-class softmax curvature. This matters because in small LLMs with large vocabularies the unquantized head can hold 15 to 30 percent of parameters and dominate the true bit budget.

entry.title: Tight Nonasymptotic Local Convergence of Sinkhorn-Knopp

author.name: Wenzhi Gao, Zhaonan Qu, Yinyu Ye, Madeleine Odell

entry.summary: Provides the first nonasymptotic local linear convergence analysis of the Sinkhorn-Knopp matrix scaling algorithm matching known asymptotic Jacobian rates, shows polynomial-time guarantees under connectivity conditions, exposes local suboptimality, and gives accelerated variants plus improved dense-matrix complexity. Sinkhorn underpins entropic optimal transport used widely in ML.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Embodied Agents via Skill-Harness Evolution

author.name: Peidong Wang, Zhiming Ma, Ying Chang, Xufang Luo, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Yuqing Yang, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: SHAPER is a train-free self-evolving framework for embodied agents that keeps model weights frozen and instead evolves reusable skills plus a context-and-code execution harness against target environments, aimed at fixed-interface settings without programmable robot APIs. Positions agent improvement as harness engineering rather than fine-tuning. Includes Microsoft Research affiliated authors.

entry.title: Hybrid Gated Attention

author.name: Zekun Zhou, Ruobing Xie, Lanrui Wang, Weixuan Sun

entry.summary: Hybrid Gated Attention combines three gating strategies drawing on information from multiple attention stages to build element-wise and head-wise gates that capture intra-head and cross-head interactions, extending the effectiveness-efficiency frontier of gated attention. Motivated by mitigating attention sinks and increasing representational capacity. Architecture-level contribution from industry-affiliated authors.

entry.title: Map-Det3D: Metric Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction Prior for Multi-view 3D Object Detection from Streaming Inputs

author.name: Yung-Hsu Yang, Luigi Piccinelli, Samuel Rota Bul\`o, Sunghwan Hong, Denis Rozumny, Johannes Sch\"onberger, Zuria Bauer, Hermann Blum, Peter Kontschieder, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Map-Det3D performs online multi-view 3D object detection by grounding detection in a metric feed-forward 3D reconstruction prior rather than predicting 3D attributes from 2D boxes, tackling the absolute-scale ambiguity of monocular pipelines. Designed for streaming inputs on embodied agents without depth sensors.

entry.title: GenFAR: A generalized representation of brain structure, derived from 49,246 multi-cohort MRIs via deep learning

author.name: Vishnu M. Bashyam, Guray Erus, Junhao Wen, Pratik Chaudhari, Randa Melhem, Sindhuja Govindarajan Tirumalai, Gareth Harman, Yong Fan, Colin L. Masters, Paul Maruff, Sterling C. Johnson, Jurgen Fripp, Duygu Tosun, John C. Morris, Daniel S. Marcus, Pamela LaMontagne, Tammie Benzinger, Susan R. Heckbert, Mark Espeland, Marilyn S. Albert, Andrew J. Saykin, Paul M. Thompson, Timothy J. Hohman, Susan M. Resnick, R. Nick Bryan, Murat Bilgel, Yang An, David A. Wolk, Li Shen, Haochang Shou, Ilya M. Nasrallah, Christos Davatzikos

entry.summary: GenFAR trains a modular deep learning framework on brain MRIs from 49,246 individuals across 11 cohorts and 17 clinical, cognitive, demographic and biomarker tasks, using sequential learning where tasks build on prior representations. Yields general, clinically informed brain representations transferable across neuroimaging applications, with 5,000 task-sequence orderings analyzed.

entry.title: Agent Safety Should Be a Runtime Contract

author.name: Albus W. Ng, Yi Han, Jusheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: A position paper contending that training-time alignment techniques are structurally insufficient for agents that execute code and mutate state, and that safety should instead be a runtime contract enforced by the harness. It splits the contract into a preventive face of sandboxes, permission gates, and trajectory monitors, and an evidential face requiring verifiable proof such as test runs, diffs, and citations before task submission.

entry.title: Reinforcing Step-level Reasoning for Effective Self-Correction in LLMs

author.name: Vu Duc Anh, Nhat M. Hoang, Do Xuan Long, Cong-Duy Nguyen, Ponhvoan Srey, Luu Anh Tuan

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage preference optimization recipe where the first stage sharpens step-level reasoning through step-wise DPO and the second explicitly trains the model to verify and repair its own intermediate errors, plus a teacher-assisted variant that supplies error rationales. Evaluations span multiple models in and out of domain.

entry.title: Low-Interaction-Rank Learning: Unifying Multiplicative Dual-Encoder Heads

author.name: Zijian Zhao, Sen Li

entry.summary: Provides a unifying theory for multiplicative dual-encoder architectures, which compute pairwise scores as inner products of separate encodings and recur across operator learning, retrieval, matching, and contrastive vision-language models. It introduces low-interaction-rank function classes with an interaction spectrum, decomposing approximation error into spectral truncation and encoder realization terms and indicating when the architecture should be avoided.

entry.title: Benchmarking Trustworthiness of SLMs: Pre-trained vs. Compressed

author.name: Haokun Lin, Kaijie Zhu, Haobo Xu, Yichen Wu, Zhichao Lu, Qingfu Zhang, Zhenan Sun

entry.summary: Comprehensively benchmarks trustworthiness of small language models along fairness, robustness, privacy, and related dimensions, comparing models trained compactly from scratch against ones obtained by pruning, quantizing, or distilling larger models. Asks whether the path to a small model changes its safety profile, not just its accuracy. Useful guidance for edge and on-device deployment.

entry.title: How Can Driving World Models Do Counterfactual Prediction?

author.name: Jiaru Zhang, Can Cui, Yi Xu, Xin Ye, Ruqi Zhang, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a fundamental mismatch between treating driving world models as counterfactual simulators and their actual action-conditioned prediction: direct prediction uses shared history and the alternative action but ignores the observed factual continuation, so it can produce plausible futures that discard what really happened. Formalizes the gap with the abduction-action-prediction causal recipe and studies it over short horizons. Conceptually important for how world models are evaluated and used in autonomous driving.

entry.title: LinearKV: One Cached State Suffices for Position-Independent Caching in Hybrid LLMs

author.name: Yirui Liu, Ruoling Qi, Longwen Wang, Xuaner Wu, Jian Chen, Yuxin Jin, Jiawei Shao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: LinearKV brings position-independent prefix caching to hybrid attention plus linear-recurrence LLMs, where fixed-size recurrent states cannot be concatenated or locally repaired like token-indexed KV caches. The training-free framework uses decoupled initialization so that a single cached state suffices for chunk reuse.

entry.title: Agent Skills Can Be Harmful: An Empirical Study of Skill-Induced Failures in LLM Agents

author.name: Gen Dong, Yanjie Gao, Liqun Li, Tianyin Xu, Yu Hua, Fan Yang

entry.summary: Empirically analyzes how reusable agent skills, the de facto extension mechanism for LLM agents, can actively cause failures and cost regressions, using a differential framework that compares skill-guided runs against no-skill or semantically matched references. Attributes specific failures and token or latency regressions to particular loaded skills.

entry.title: Gaze Target Estimation Anywhere with Concepts

author.name: Xu Cao, Houze Yang, Vipin Gunda, Zhongyi Zhou, Tianyu Xu, Adarsh Kowdle, Inki Kim, James M. Rehg

entry.summary: Defines promptable gaze target estimation, an end-to-end task where the subject of gaze analysis is specified by natural language concepts instead of brittle upstream head boxes and pose detectors. Removing the multi-stage pipeline avoids cascading detection errors and adds prompting flexibility.

entry.title: HyperFix: Combinatorial Nonlinear Correction for Task Vector Merging

author.name: Hyo Seo Kim, Ren Wang

entry.summary: Frames model merging across varying subsets of task vectors as a combinatorial correction problem and trains a hypernetwork once on singleton, pair, and triple subsets to predict subset-conditioned nonlinear weight-space corrections that generalize to larger subsets. A local perturbation analysis bounds the residual beyond linear merging.

entry.title: Accuracy and Order Sensitivity Diverge Under Label-Free Strategies

author.name: Karl Hanna, Chen Feng

entry.summary: Tests whether hiding option labels from a model, via generate-then-match or scoring options in isolation, removes multiple-choice position bias and improves accuracy. Neither strategy reliably helps: accuracy and order sensitivity move independently, and the bottleneck is withholding the options rather than the matching step.

entry.title: QV-PIC: Query-Aware Visual Position-Independent Caching for Efficient RAG Serving

author.name: Yilin Liu, Rui Meng, Wangze Ni, Jianxin Yan, Heng Cao, Libin Zheng, Peng Cheng, Jinfei Liu

entry.summary: QV-PIC improves position-independent KV cache reuse for retrieval-augmented generation by rendering text chunks as images to compress token counts, then repairing the resulting quality loss with query-aware recovery of fine-grained textual evidence. Targets the redundant prefill cost of repeatedly serving the same chunks.

entry.title: NetlistBench: Evaluating LLM Reliability in SPICE Netlist Recognition and Manipulation

author.name: Jiarui Ma, Jianghan Wang, Yuheng Ma, Ziyi Zhuang, Xiaoguang Liu

entry.summary: NetlistBench provides 2,342 structure-verified cases across 24 task families to test whether LLMs can reliably read and edit SPICE netlists, including hierarchical operations, equivalence judgment, and long-horizon compound edits. Outputs are graded by a deterministic structure-aware oracle rather than text matching.

entry.title: Unmasking Toxic Mimicry in Medical Offline Reinforcement Learning for ICU Sepsis Management via Counterfactual Clinical Audits

author.name: Hangqi Ren, Junyi Liao

entry.summary: Shows that standard offline RL evaluation metrics measure imitation of clinician behavior and therefore miss toxic mimicry, where an agent reproduces harmful patterns such as treatment withdrawal during comfort-care transitions. Proposes a counterfactual clinical audit that perturbs physiology according to sepsis guidelines and applies it to two clinical decision transformer agents on MIMIC-III.

entry.title: Distillation of Foundation Models for Time-dependent PDEs

author.name: Daniel Musekamp, Boshra Ariguib, Andrei Manolache, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: TREX distills large PDE foundation models into compact students by having a fine-tuned teacher generate long synthetic rollout trajectories that augment scarce downstream data. The goal is retaining foundation-model accuracy while achieving surrogate-grade inference speed.

entry.title: Reducing Symmetry Increase in Equivariant Neural Networks

author.name: Ning Lin, Jiacheng Cen, Anyi Li, Wenbing Huang, Hao Sun

entry.summary: Characterizes why equivariant neural networks lose expressivity on symmetric inputs, namely that equivariant maps can only increase output symmetry beyond the input's own symmetry group, and proposes general strategies to reduce this symmetry inflation. Prior work only documented the phenomenon in special cases.

entry.title: An Efficient Near-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial $m$-Set Bandits

author.name: Francesco Bacchiocchi, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni

entry.summary: Gives a computationally efficient algorithm for adversarial combinatorial bandits with m-set actions that achieves high-probability regret matching the known rate without enumerating the exponentially large action set. It handles adaptive non-anticipating adversaries under semi-bandit-free aggregate feedback.

entry.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing

author.name: Minhan Cho, Jimin Kweon

entry.summary: An independent reproduction and stress test of two recent LLM reasoning reliability methods: test-time probability aggregation with self-consistency, and training projectors that split hidden states into content and logic components for editing. The authors re-run one method across four new domains and reimplement the other, which shipped no public code, across four 7 to 8 billion parameter models.

entry.title: Generative Learning for Quantum Measurement Design

author.name: Jun Dai, Olivier Nahman-L\'{e}vesque, Guillaume Rabusseau, Hong-Ye Hu, Cunlu Zhou

entry.summary: FlowMeas recasts resource-constrained quantum measurement design as a generative modeling problem, using a generative flow network to sample measurement schemes that trade statistical efficiency against circuit depth, connectivity, and entangling gate count. It interpolates between hardware-friendly product measurements and deep fully commuting schemes.

entry.title: A Quantum/Classical Example Oracle Separation for Making Things Up

author.name: Kenny Chen

entry.summary: Proves an oracle separation showing there exist distribution-generation learning tasks solvable efficiently by a quantum learner given quantum examples but not by a quantum learner limited to classical examples. Makes progress on a previously open question in quantum PAC learning. Theoretical contribution with no near-term practical use.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Code-with-Image Reasoning

author.name: Tianze Yang, Liang Wu, Ruitong Sun, Yucheng Shi, Yanqiao Wang, Mayank Darbari, Ninghao Liu, Jin Sun, Liangjie Hong

entry.summary: Argues that some visual questions are not perception-bottlenecked but require executing a multi-step visual algorithm over pixels, which language-only reasoning cannot do even when the model names the correct algorithm, and proposes a self-evolving code-with-image paradigm where the model writes and runs Python over the image. Extends thinking-with-images from evidence exposure to actual computation. Conceptually clarifying for multimodal tool use.

entry.title: Fingerprinting Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Collapsed Generation

author.name: Yuanmin Huang, Chen Chen, Geng Hong, Xiaoyu You, Hui Xue, Zhenxing Qian, Mi Zhang, Min Yang

entry.summary: Proposes non-invasive fingerprinting of text-to-image diffusion models by exploiting collapsed generation, where certain input conditions yield nearly identical images across random seeds, forming a model-specific behavioral signature. Ownership can then be verified without embedding watermarks or modifying the model.

entry.title: Language-Conditional Dequantization: Recovering What Quantization Steals from Non-English Languages

author.name: Nirmal Thomas

entry.summary: Documents that aggressive INT3 quantization degrades non-English perplexity two to four times more than English in sub-4B models, then proposes Language-Conditional Dequantization, per-language rank-2 LoRA corrections added post hoc for about 0.12 percent extra parameters and under 20 minutes of GPU training. Recovers a large share of the multilingual perplexity gap and part of the GlobalMMLU accuracy gap on Qwen2.5-3B and Llama-3.2-3B. Equity-relevant efficiency finding.

entry.title: VLMs Win a Systematic Evaluation of Underwater Image Reconstruction

author.name: Sara Aghajanzadeh, Yingxue Wang, Ieva Bagdonaviciute, David Forsyth

entry.summary: Builds a systematic evaluation pipeline for underwater image restoration measuring accuracy, consistency across camera motion, and sensitivity to water parameters, then finds that vision-language models substantially outperform methods based on explicit physical scattering models. Attributes the win to the strength of learned image priors over approximate physics. Includes a well-known computer vision senior author.

entry.title: When (and when not) LLMs can verbalize awareness of J-Space concept injections - Initial results

author.name: Ethan Garcia

entry.summary: An empirical introspection study injecting single-token Jacobian-lens concept vectors into the existing Qwen 3.6-27B model across layer bands and strengths while it answers simple factual questions, then asking it to report whether an injection occurred. Steering succeeded at similar rates in both response orders, roughly 450 of 1,560 trials each, but verbalized detection of the injection differed sharply depending on whether the model reported before or after producing its answer, suggesting reports partly reflect self-observation of the output rather than direct access to internal state.

entry.title: AutoWorldModel-Bench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Automated World-Model Research

author.name: Marjan Moodi, Xuankang Zhu, Fernando De Mesentier Silva, Harold Chaput, Mohammad Reza Taesiri

entry.summary: AutoWorldModel-Bench is a closed-loop benchmark where frontier coding agents must autonomously improve a world-model starter codebase across eight game environments under a fixed compute budget. Unlike engineering-to-spec agent benchmarks, the improvement direction is open-ended, making it a test of research-style autonomy.

entry.title: InfraBench: Evaluating Infrastructure Agents Across Layers, Lifecycle, and Risk

author.name: Yuan Gao (Wanxiang), Zeren Yang (Wanxiang), Junnan Li (Wanxiang), Shawn (Wanxiang), Zhong, Ahmed Dajani, Mai Zheng, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau

entry.summary: InfraBench evaluates AI agents on realistic infrastructure management tasks spanning the full system stack and operational lifecycle, with fine-grained risk assessment. Across 15 agent-model configurations no agent scores fully, with mean effective scores between roughly 40 and 88 percent.

entry.title: Chemically Meaningful Textualization Enables Explainable Validation of Metal-Organic Frameworks by Large Language Models

author.name: Guobin Zhao, Xiao-Yan Li

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs can act as interpretable validators of metal-organic framework crystal structures when crystallographic data is converted into chemically meaningful text, and finds that success hinges on whether local coordination environments are made explicit rather than on sheer information volume. Nine textual descriptors are benchmarked to isolate what representation matters.

entry.title: Herding End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guards

author.name: Sim\'on Pati\~no Idarraga, Erick Silva, Rehana Yasmin, Ali Shoker

entry.summary: Attaches a lightweight neuro-symbolic guard to the command interface of an already-trained end-to-end driving agent, checking each command against explicit traffic and physical safety rules and substituting the nearest safe alternative when needed. Every intervention is traceable to the rule that fired, adding auditability without retraining.

entry.title: Motion-as-Prompt: Enhancing Motion Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via Motion-Guided Cross-Frame Visual Prompting

author.name: Xikai Sun, Kebin Liu, Haotian Wang, Li Liu, Xu Wang, Yunhao Liu

entry.summary: Improves motion reasoning in multimodal LLMs by recovering dense point trajectories from video, selecting motion-informative frames, and drawing accumulated trajectories directly onto the sampled frames as visual prompts. This surfaces transitions that uniform sparse sampling would otherwise discard, without increasing token budget much.

entry.title: JieZi: A Large-Scale Expert-Audited Dataset and Benchmark for Ancient Chinese Character Exegesis

author.name: Ran Li, Huiguo He, Jiahuan Cao, Junle Liu, Hiuyi Cheng, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Defines ancient Chinese character exegesis as a four-level vision-language QA task spanning identification, glyph-form analysis, meaning interpretation, and diachronic evolution, and releases a large expert-audited dataset plus benchmark. It aims to move computational paleography beyond isolated recognition and retrieval subtasks.

entry.title: TELLME: Test-Enhanced Learning for Language Model Enrichment

author.name: Minjun Kim, Inho Won, Hyeonseok Lim, MinKyu Kim, Junghun Yuk, Wooyoung Go, Jongyoul Park, Jungyeul Park, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: TELLME injects quiz-style test items into continual pre-training so that domain knowledge is acquired with less data and compute, borrowing the testing effect from learning science. Reported gains over standard continual pre-training on domain adaptation benchmarks.

entry.title: Benchmark-Based Comparative Assessment of Publicly Benchmarked Indian Foundation Models: A Capability and Evaluation-Maturity Framework

author.name: Avinash Agarwal, Vridhi Jain

entry.summary: Compares publicly benchmarked Indian sovereign foundation models against global frontier and similar-size models across eight capability domains, and proposes an evaluation-maturity framework to handle inconsistent public reporting. Aims to give governments a way to track national AI ecosystem progress.

entry.title: Learning-Based Behavior Planning for Automated Driving: Real-World Integration and Deployment

author.name: Jean-Pierre Busch, Guido Linden, Jan Bergmann, Lutz Eckstein

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid automated-driving behavior planner where a neural network proposes maneuvers from complex traffic scenes and an optimization-based supervision layer verifies drivability and safety constraints before execution. Emphasizes real-vehicle integration and deployment rather than simulation only.

entry.title: Convergence Guarantees of Gradient Descent for Neural Networks via Generalized Lipschitz Smoothness

author.name: Siqiao Mu, Diego Klabjan

entry.summary: Establishes gradient-descent convergence guarantees for feedforward networks of arbitrary width and depth under only mild assumptions on activations (Lipschitz smooth, Lipschitz continuous, linearly bounded), with no special initialization or dataset conditions. The key idea is a generalized Lipschitz smoothness condition preserved through composition.

entry.title: Large-scale AI-Ready Data for Anti-Cancer Drug Response Modeling

author.name: Vincent Lavelle, Yitan Zhu, Kaitlyn Marlor, Thomas Brettin, Rick Stevens

entry.summary: Substantially expands standardized AI-ready training data for anticancer drug response prediction within the IMPROVE benchmarking framework, increasing coverage of cancer and chemical space. The motivation is that model generalizability is currently limited by dataset scale and inconsistent benchmarking practice.

entry.title: Forward Trajectory Steering for Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Analysis

author.name: Sungje Park, Stephen Tu

entry.summary: STEER2REACH is a physics-informed neural solver for Hamilton-Jacobi reachability that steers forward trajectories to generate informative collocation points, removing the need for complex training pipelines and auxiliary supervision used by prior PINN-based safety solvers. Reachability value functions underpin rigorous safe control in high dimensions.

entry.title: Direct Acceleration of Stochastic Root-Finding Without Variance Reduction and Regularization

author.name: TaeHo Yoon, Nicolas Loizou

entry.summary: Shows that the dual-anchor acceleration mechanism extends to stochastic root-finding without variance reduction, regularization, or growing batch sizes, achieving order epsilon-to-the-minus-three complexity with iteration-independent batch size. Contrasts with anchor-based Halpern methods that suffer error accumulation. A clean theoretical improvement for stochastic monotone inclusion problems.

entry.title: Avatar-Forever: Decoupled Parallel Training for High-Quality Real-Time Infinite Avatars

author.name: Ruibin Li, Tao Yang, Zhiyuan Ma, Fangzhou Ai, Shilei Wen, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Avatar-Forever replaces sequential distillation pipelines for real-time long-video avatar generation with a decoupled parallel training framework, separating few-step generation efficiency from long-horizon autoregressive robustness. Aims to avoid error accumulation and cascading failures across training stages for infinite interactive avatars.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM Generated Detection Rules in Cybersecurity

author.name: Anna Bertiger, Bobby Filar, Aryan Luthra, Stefano Meschiari, Aiden Mitchell, Sam Scholten, Vivek Sharath

entry.summary: Presents an open-source benchmark and three expert-inspired metrics for judging whether LLM-generated cybersecurity detection rules are actually effective, using a holdout methodology against a corpus of human-written rules from a commercial detection team. It gives security practitioners a concrete way to measure trust in LLM rule generators.

entry.title: RoadWeaver: Large-Scale Lane-Level HD Map Generation from Scratch for Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Yueyuan Li, Zexi Chen, Weijie Xi, Mingyang Jiang, Songan Zhang, Hanyang Zhuang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: Presents a coarse-to-fine generator that synthesizes large-scale lane-level HD maps from scratch, first laying out a global road network then producing topologically consistent lane geometry, reporting high reachability and small endpoint alignment error. The goal is scalable diverse map supply for long-horizon autonomous driving simulation.

entry.title: When the API Speaks the Wrong Language: Revisiting Post-Training for Multilingual Tool Use

author.name: Siddharth Chauhan, Thomas Butler, Abhishek Singhania, Pankaj Porwal, Honey Gupta

entry.summary: Names and measures argument language mismatch, a multilingual tool-calling failure where a model picks the right API but fills arguments in the wrong language, producing semantically sensible yet operationally invalid calls that standard metrics miss. Comparing post-training strategies, supervised fine-tuning proves a strong baseline that matches or beats more complex reinforcement learning approaches under consistent model selection.

entry.title: HCGRec: Hint-Conditioned Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs

author.name: Kangning Zhang, Haotian Fang, Xukun Luo, Hao Yin, Yang Gao, Peng Yan, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

entry.summary: Identifies a structural failure in reward-based post-training of semantic-ID generative recommenders: if an early token picks the wrong branch, all rollouts get zero reward and group-relative optimization yields no learning signal. HCGRec conditions rollouts on hints to recover gradient signal on hard items.

entry.title: Drift and Dependence: Layer-wise Information-Theoretic Bounds for Replay-Based Continual Learning

author.name: Tieliang Gong, Zhongbo Zhang, Wen Wen, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: Develops layer-wise information-theoretic generalization bounds for replay-based continual learning, decomposing the generalization gap into replay-induced representation drift and optimization-induced dependence between the buffer, current data, and final hypothesis. This separates two effects previous analyses conflated.

entry.title: The Advective Fisher-Rao Geometry of Deterministic Measure Transport

author.name: Benjamin Gess, Johannes M\"uller

entry.summary: Introduces an advective Fisher-Rao metric for optimizing over paths of probability measures governed by the continuity equation, showing it arises equivalently as a zero-noise limit of Fisher-Rao on path measures, the expected second variation of the Freidlin-Wentzell rate functional, and the Hessian of the Benamou-Brenier action. Provides optimal descent directions with supporting experiments. Foundational geometry for training flow and transport models.

entry.title: CT-$\Delta$Bench: A Benchmark for Longitudinal 3D Medical Imaging Difference Reporting with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kegeng Tang, Jingbo Wang, Shaogang Ren, Zihao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CT-DeltaBench, a benchmark for longitudinal difference reporting in which vision-language models must compare two temporally separated CT studies from the same patient and generate clinically meaningful change descriptions. Targets a gap where medical foundation models handle only single studies despite temporal comparison driving real clinical decisions. Provides a concrete evaluation target for temporal medical VLMs.

entry.title: MuseCritic: Learning Multi-Aspect Song Rewards through Natural-Language Aesthetic Critiques

author.name: Jiabao Zhuang, Changhao Jiang, Hanchen Wang, Jiahao Chen, Zhixiong Yang, Zhenghao Xiang, Yifei Cao, Jiajun Sun, Hui Li, Ming Zhang, Tao Ji, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: MuseCritic is a semi-scalar reward model for full-length songs that first generates a natural-language critique across five aesthetic dimensions and uses it as an intermediate representation to predict continuous reward scores, trained by distilling teacher critiques then refining. Adds interpretability to music reward modeling for aligning long-form song generators with human preference. Involves a large group including well-known NLP authors.

entry.title: Towards the Harness of Embodied Agents

author.name: Qi Wang, Tianyi Wang, Chengyang Li, Shikun Ban, Yurun Chen, Yizhong Ge, Jason Qin, Chengtai Li, Wentao Zhu

entry.summary: Thea extends the coding-agent harness paradigm to embodied robotics, wrapping robot capabilities as callable tools inside an agentic loop. It supplies the two things the physical world does not give for free with a persistent symbolic scene graph as context and evaluation results surfaced as exit codes.

entry.title: Harness-IF: Evaluating Instruction Following Across Instruction Surfaces in Coding Agents

author.name: Zining Huang, Haoran Que, Hong Zeng, Ge Zhang, Zuo Wang, Jin Chen, Haodong Wang, Zhongfei Hou, Changxin Pu, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang

entry.summary: Harness-IF evaluates whether coding agents genuinely follow operational rules by scoring individual rules from execution evidence across five configuration surfaces a deployed agent reads. Its key idea is Against-Prior Accuracy, which scores only rules that oppose what the agent would do unprompted, separating real compliance from coincidence.

entry.title: Advancing MLLM-based UAV Image Understanding and Reasoning: A Benchmark and a Training-Free Multi-Agent System

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Shuoxun Zhang, Peng Ye, Lin Zhang, Jiakang Yuan, Shenghong Yi, Yuening Wang, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Builds a unified benchmark of 1,500 human-annotated question-answer pairs drawn from 13 public UAV datasets covering six capability dimensions and 16 tasks, then evaluates a wide set of open and closed multimodal models on aerial understanding and grounding. It also proposes a training-free multi-agent system to handle extreme scale variation, arbitrary orientations, and dense objects.

entry.title: PAIR: Pairwise-Aware Inclusion Reweighting for Adaptive Rollout Allocation in RLVR

author.name: Pixel Nomand, Elena Voss, Marcus Hale, Sofia Reyes

entry.summary: Observes that the leave-one-out group-relative policy gradient used in RLVR is a pairwise U-statistic rather than a sum of independent per-rollout terms, so pointwise budget allocators are statistically mismatched. PAIR reweights rollout inclusion based on pair-level contributions to allocate compute more efficiently.

entry.title: FLARE++: Low-rank attention with dynamic attention routing

author.name: Vedant Puri, Yongjie Jessica Zhang, Levent Burak Kara

entry.summary: FLARE++ makes low-rank latent attention routing input-conditioned: instead of fixed learned latent queries, an extra encoder pass gathers tokens into query vectors that depend on the current input. The aim is near-full-attention quality for PDE surrogates on irregular meshes at linear cost.

entry.title: Kernel Methods for Learning Operators with Multiple Inputs and Outputs

author.name: Adrien Weihs, Chunyang Liao, Jingmin Sun, Hayden Schaeffer

entry.summary: A kernel-based encoder-decoder framework for operator learning between products of distinct function spaces, with approximation theory showing the convergence rate is set by the hardest constituent subproblem rather than the total dimension. Training and inference have closed forms.

entry.title: Task- and dataset-specific information in protein language models

author.name: Roman Joeres, Ilya Senatorov, Olga V. Kalinina

entry.summary: Systematically probes 13 protein language models across 15 downstream tasks and 11 datasets to test the default practice of using last-layer embeddings, finding that intermediate layers often carry more task-relevant information. The study also characterizes latent-space geometry per layer.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Generative Models for Extreme Events via CVaR-Penalized Wasserstein Gradient Flows

author.name: Thejani Gamage, Hyemin Gu, Zhizhen Zhang, Ziyu Chen, Markos Katsoulakis, Luc Rey-Bellet

entry.summary: CVaR-GPA fine-tunes generative models to capture heavy tails and extreme events by running a Wasserstein gradient flow on a Lipschitz-regularized KL divergence penalized with a conditional value-at-risk term. The CVaR penalty restores velocity that otherwise vanishes in undersampled tails, and no prior knowledge of tail behavior is required.

entry.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

author.name: Pan Wang, Yihao Hu, Hang Wang, Zirui Lv, Xin Zhang, Jianshe Li, Jiang-Ming Yang, Wei Wu, Yongqi Tong

entry.summary: DARC proposes diagnosing agent failure types on a development set to decide which recovery interventions are admissible before test-time self-correction, avoiding generic playbooks that flood context with incompatible repair signals for invalid actions, missing procedures, and format errors. Extends compiler-style typed feedback benefits from coding agents to general language-agent tasks. Practical agent reliability work.

entry.title: Total Recall at What Cost? Benchmarking the Serving Cost of Agentic Memory Systems

author.name: Natchanon Pollertlam, Witchayut Kornsuwannawit

entry.summary: Benchmarks the serving cost of three agentic memory systems against a rolling window and full-transcript resubmission across two backbones and conversations up to 400 turns, pairing every cost measurement with accuracy on 665 LoCoMo questions. Finds memory-system cost is not predictable from conversation length and message size, with regressions missing actual costs by 18 to 69 percent. Fills a gap in cost-aware evaluation of long-running agents.

entry.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning

author.name: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang, Bingnan Li, Shuqi Gu, Kan Ren, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Hua

entry.summary: AVA-Encoder learns agent-native video representations by encoding a video into a hierarchical knowledge graph with typed edges and a linked asset layer of generated images, audio, and video, then reconstructing the video from that graph. The goal is a structured representation faithful enough for creative agents to reason over and manipulate film content. Bridges video understanding and controllable generation for agentic workflows.

entry.title: Context Blindness in DPO: Mitigating Object Hallucination in MLLMs via Context-Calibrated Preference Optimization

author.name: Byungoh Ko, Jinyoung Park, Jongha Kim, Jeehye Na, Jaewon Cho, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Shows that standard DPO for reducing multimodal object hallucination is largely context-blind: the authors define a Contextual Preference Gain metric measuring how much preference strengthens when relevant context is supplied, find higher gain tracks lower hallucination, and propose context-calibrated preference optimization. Provides diagnostic evidence that context-enriched preference data is not actually exploited.

entry.title: One attention head carries knight forks in a chess transformer, and here's a new toolkit that found it.

author.name: dl27

entry.summary: A demo of a new chess-transformer interpretability toolkit that localizes knight-fork detection to a single attention head in Maia-3 using logit lens and per-head ablation, with a Colab notebook and an interactive app. The post previews a forthcoming paper reporting that across hundreds of mined fork positions ablating the identified head costs about 2.78 logits while every other head in the layer costs at most 0.14.

entry.title: Detecting a Route Flip Is Easier Than Knowing Whether to Fix It: Causal Route-Mediated Damage in Quantized Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Parvel Gu

entry.summary: Studies how simulated 4-bit KV-cache quantization perturbs top-k mixture-of-experts routing, flipping which experts fire, and builds a causal apparatus to price the routing-mediated fraction of the resulting quality damage. Finds roughly a third of the damage on a small MoE is routing-mediated and argues that detecting a route flip is far easier than knowing whether repairing it helps.

entry.title: Cutting AI Datacenter Energy with Reinforcement Learning: Measured Power Control of LLM Training from One GPU to the Fleet

author.name: Eliseo Curcio

entry.summary: Instruments GRPO reinforcement-learning post-training with high-frequency GPU power telemetry at 7B to 72B scales and trains a PPO meta-controller that adapts generation parameters in response to measured power. Reports large reductions in power-limit violations alongside increased token throughput and energy efficiency.

entry.title: VQ-bench: A Composable Vector Quantization Framework

author.name: Ashwin Padaki, Amir Ingber, Edo Liberty

entry.summary: VQ-bench decomposes vector quantization into seven composable primitives, re-expresses 25 published quantizers as pipelines over those primitives, and releases an open-source reproducible benchmarking harness. It targets the resurgence of quantization work driven by vector-database and embedding infrastructure.

entry.title: When Self-Consistency Backfires: Majority Vote Hurts the Majority of Hard Science Problems for Small LLMs

author.name: Utkarsh Bahuguna

entry.summary: Shows that self-consistency majority voting reduces per-problem accuracy on the majority of GPQA Diamond questions for two small instruction-tuned models, with the effect pre-registered on a confirmatory split after exploratory observation. An oracle that routes each problem to the best sample count reveals large headroom left on the table by fixed-N voting.

entry.title: Foresight Without Seeing: Latent Futures for World Action Models

author.name: Jiakai Huang, Zhongbo Wu, Zheng Zhang, Zihan Wang, Shan You, Tao Huang

entry.summary: ForeWAM is a world action model that conditions robot action generation on predicted future dynamics without decoding future video, avoiding the heavy iterative denoising cost of explicit-future approaches. It provides the action head with a latent predictive interface that direct-policy models normally lack.

entry.title: Making AI-Generated Feedback Matter: From Provision to Student Enactment

author.name: Omar Alsaiari, Nilufar Baghaei, Jason M. Lodge, Dragan Ga\v{s}evi'c, Naomi Winstone, Hassan Khosravi

entry.summary: A large quasi-experimental study across 13,037 students and over 51,000 authored resources compares three AI-mediated feedback workflows, from simply providing AI comments to structured support for interpreting and acting on them. Distinguishes the provision problem, which generative AI largely solves, from the enactment problem of getting students to actually use feedback.

entry.title: FrontierFinance: A Challenging Benchmark for Measuring Frontier Intelligence of Finance Agents

author.name: Yuhao Zhang, O. Ozan Koyluoglu, Thejas Venkatesh, Richard Diehl Martinez, Vishank Bhatia, Arash Alidoust, Ashwin Paranjape

entry.summary: FrontierFinance is an open benchmark of 220 expert-crafted investment-research queries with 11,543 source-attributed rubrics spanning six use cases across the full investor workflow. It argues existing finance benchmarks target saturated data extraction and that reference-based or generic judge scoring fails on long-form analyst answers.

entry.title: Making Your LLMs More Objective: Stabilizing LLM Safety Behavior Across Traits with Trait-Invariant Safety Tuning

author.name: Lang Cao

entry.summary: Documents trait-induced safety variation, where the same request receives different refusal decisions depending on the persona or trait assigned in the system prompt, and introduces deviation and flip-rate metrics to quantify it. Provides a representation-level account of the mechanism and proposes trait-invariant safety tuning to stabilize behavior.

entry.title: Policy-as-logic for robust reasoning over rules

author.name: Rahul Nair, Bastian Lipka, Elizabeth Daly

entry.summary: Separates policy compliance into LLM-based fact extraction to ground predicates and an answer-set solver for the actual reasoning, so responses over written rules are interpretable, auditable, and robust to input perturbations. Reports better accuracy than policy-as-prompt and policy-as-code baselines with roughly a tenfold reduction in token usage.

entry.title: SegPAR: Class-Centric Decision-Based Sparse Attack for Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Dongsu Song, DaeYun GO, Boseung Seo, Jay Hoon Jung

entry.summary: Establishes a benchmark for decision-based black-box sparse adversarial attacks on semantic segmentation by adapting classification-domain baselines, then proposes SegPAR, which switches from image-centric pixel accumulation to class-centric exploration to drastically cut query cost. It also addresses misleading feedback signals specific to dense prediction.

entry.title: From Synthesis to Removal: Physics-Grounded Reflection Simulation and Diffusion-Based Video Dereflection

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Jiagao Hu, Fuhao Li, Yuxuan Chen, Fei Wang, Daiguo Zhou

entry.summary: Builds a closed loop for video reflection removal: a physics-grounded simulator generates paired reflected and clean videos by augmenting in structure space and rendering with a trained video diffusion renderer, a diffusion model performs temporally coherent dereflection, and a dedicated benchmark evaluates results. It targets the missing paired data, temporal coherence, and evaluation gaps in this task.

entry.title: A 12-CNOT Double Qubit Excitation Gate

author.name: Irfansha Shaik

entry.summary: Reports a 12-CNOT decomposition of the double qubit excitation operator, improving on the previous best of 13 CNOTs while also achieving the lowest CNOT depth and total circuit depth among known constructions. Such gates are core primitives in variational quantum chemistry circuits.

entry.title: DexterSQL: Deep Schema Exploration and Rule-based Correction for Text-to-SQL Generation

author.name: Anik Pramanik, Murat Kantarcioglu, Vincent Oria, Shantanu Sharma

entry.summary: DexterSQL improves prompting-only text-to-SQL with a deep schema explorer that disambiguates similar columns, a memory of recurring generation failures, and rule-based correction of missing or misplaced conditions. Targets accuracy gains without fine-tuning the base model.

entry.title: Preference Tree Optimization: Enhancing Goal-Oriented Dialogue with Look-Ahead Simulations

author.name: Lior Baruch, Moshe Butman, Kfir Bar, Doron Friedman

entry.summary: Preference Tree Optimization builds preference data for multi-turn goal-oriented dialogue by expanding a tree of candidate replies and simulating look-ahead conversations with virtual patients and an oracle evaluator, then applies DPO. Demonstrated on motivational interviewing counseling dialogue.

entry.title: Faithful, Sufficient and Understandable: Rethinking Graph Counterfactual Explanations via Discrete Diffusion Inversion

author.name: David Bechtoldt, Sidney Bender

entry.summary: Generates counterfactual explanations for graph neural networks using discrete diffusion inversion, so that edits remain on the data manifold while respecting categorical node and edge types and domain rules such as chemical valency. Argues existing explainers sacrifice either validity or faithfulness.

entry.title: Structural Silence: When AI Infrastructure Fails Speakers of Underrepresented Languages

author.name: Avijit Roy, Proma Roy

entry.summary: Argues that AI education tools disadvantage speakers of underrepresented languages before any training occurs, through web presence gaps, tokenization inefficiency, benchmark absence, and deployment assumptions, using Bengali as the case study. Identifies four interlocking infrastructural failures despite Bengali being one of the most spoken languages globally.

entry.title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: Agentic Optimization for Image-to-Video Adherence

author.name: Aman Tyagi, Hemanth Boinpally, Jonathan Chen, Douglas Gebert, Steven Hickson

entry.summary: Frames image-to-video generation with black-box models as closed-loop optimization instead of manual trial and error, with an iterative prompt optimization stage followed by parameter search to improve adherence to intent. Targets the reliability problems that stochastic generation causes in professional creative workflows.

entry.title: Reoptimization Algorithms for Contextual Bandits with Knapsack Constraints

author.name: Zhen Xu

entry.summary: Studies contextual bandits with knapsack resource constraints where customers must be assigned products built from finite-capacity resources and rewards are unknown linear functions of features. Proposes a reoptimization-based extension with regret guarantees relative to an oracle policy.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Data-Driven Assortment Optimization

author.name: Junyi Liao, Xiaohui Jiang, Zhengwei Tong, Ethan X. Fang, Vahid Tarokh

entry.summary: Replaces parametric choice models in assortment optimization with a guided discrete diffusion search over binary assortment vectors, avoiding combinatorial enumeration and reducing sensitivity to model misspecification. A reward-guided mechanism biases transitions using estimates of expected revenue.

entry.title: AutoGrable: What Is a Good Graph for a Table?

author.name: Tamara Cucumides, Floris Geerts

entry.summary: AutoGrable proposes a training-free criterion for deciding how to convert tables or relational databases into graphs for GNN learning, based on whether the color-refinement partition induced by a candidate construction separates rows with different labels. It replaces expensive trial-and-error graph search with a 1-WL-grounded test.

entry.title: RelShap: Relationally Consistent Shapley Explanations

author.name: Seungeun Lee, Joao Fonseca, Julia Stoyanovich

entry.summary: RelShap adapts Shapley-value attribution to relational data by restricting coalitions and background samples to configurations that are actually realizable under schema constraints and provenance. It is estimator-agnostic and composes with Kernel SHAP and related samplers.

entry.title: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models

author.name: Myeong-Ju Cho, Hye-Bin Shin, Seo-Hyun Lee, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: BLPM is an EEG-language foundation model that performs continuous latent predictive pretraining instead of masked reconstruction or discrete autoregression, aligning neural representations with language semantics for LLM integration. It targets cross-subject and cross-dataset generalization in neural decoding.

entry.title: Clustered Randomized Smoothing for Stochastic Prediction Functions

author.name: Eduardo Figueiredo, Frederik Mathiesen, Julian Schumann, Jens Kober, Arkady Zgonnikov, Luca Laurenti

entry.summary: Clustered alpha-smoothing repairs randomized smoothing for stochastic multi-modal predictors by clustering noisy samples, smoothing within clusters, and recombining, avoiding the mode collapse that makes standard smoothing output meaningless averages. It targets certified robustness in safety-critical regression such as trajectory prediction.

entry.title: When the Knowledge Base Becomes the Gold Standard: Measuring Resource-Shared Evaluation Loops in Entity-Level Machine Translation

author.name: Jinhyung Bae, Dain Kil, Seongmin Oh, Seungmin Lee

entry.summary: Shows that using a knowledge base as the evaluation gold standard for entity-level machine translation creates a self-referential loop when the same KB is injected into the system, so scores measure instruction compliance rather than translation quality. Demonstrates this with expert person-name annotations for a Korean historical corpus held independent of the injection pipeline. A sharp methodological warning for entity-aware MT and RAG evaluation.

entry.title: Spark-to-Paper: End-to-End Research Paper Generation as a Composable Skill

author.name: Zhuoyang Qian, Biao Wu, Yiran Wang, Chris D Yan, Desan Dai, Liangwei Zheng, Jin Jiang, Junsheng Zhang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: Spark-to-Paper implements end-to-end research paper generation as thirteen composable skills inside an existing coding assistant, separating model judgment from deterministic checkable operations and separating experiment planning from reporting so required evidence is specified before results are seen. Covers literature retrieval, experiment execution, figure production, and long-document consistency. Notable for its preregistration-like discipline within an automated science agent.

entry.title: Asymptotic Risk Calibration for Selective Question Answering

author.name: Shufan Lin, Sijin Dong

entry.summary: A-CRC-QA is a post-hoc calibration framework for selective question answering that reformulates selection-conditioned error control as a linear expectation constraint and applies monotonized empirical risk calibration inspired by conformal risk control, giving statistical guarantees on the error rate among accepted answers. Replaces ad hoc uncertainty thresholds with distribution-free control. Relevant to reliable LLM deployment.

entry.title: Test-Time Hallucination Control in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mehran Tamjidi, Hamidreza Dastmalchi, Ali Cheraghian, Mohammadreza Alimoradijazi, Aijun An, Hossein Rahmani

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free test-time method to reduce object hallucination in large vision-language models that avoids both the cost of multiple decoding passes and model-specific internal-state edits that can damage pretrained knowledge. Aims at practical reliability for deployed LVLMs. Positioned against both training-based and existing training-free baselines.

entry.title: UniSwap: Streaming Audio-Visual Identity Swapping for Talking Videos

author.name: Yuxuan Zhang, Haozhong Xiong, Jiayi Song, Jinpeng Yu, Yang Shi, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Huang, Liwei Wang

entry.summary: UniSwap jointly swaps face appearance and vocal timbre in talking videos inside a single streaming audio-visual diffusion transformer, using a swap-and-reconstruct pipeline to overcome the lack of aligned cross-identity training pairs. It preserves source motion, content and audio-video timing while transferring identity in both modalities.

entry.title: XBridge: Entity-Grounded Latent Bridge for Heterogeneous LLM Communication

author.name: Wooseong Yang, Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Yu Wang, Philip S. Yu, Junhyun Lee

entry.summary: XBridge enables decode-free latent communication between LLMs from different families, identifying an entity grounding problem where cross-attention bridges lose rare-token entity identity in the continuous bottleneck. Proposes mechanisms to preserve entity identity while transferring internal representations across heterogeneous architectures.

entry.title: How to Spend Your Oracle Budget: Practical Guidance for Protein Structure Prediction Models

author.name: Aleksandra Kalisz, Jack Simons, Krisztina Sinkovics, Noam Ghenassia, Shikha Surana, Henry Moss, Paul Duckworth

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic comparison of how to spend a limited external oracle budget when guiding protein structure prediction models, benchmarking FK-steering, DPO, and best-of-N against an optimization-over-outputs approach applied in latent space. Aims to give practitioners concrete guidance when biological oracles are expensive.

entry.title: Co-constructing sociotechnical AI governance: participatory system mapping using algorithm registers

author.name: \'I\~nigo de Troya, Maurus Enbergs, Neelke Doorn, Roel Dobbe

entry.summary: Uses participatory system mapping with diverse stakeholders to examine what public-sector algorithm registers actually reveal and hide about the sociotechnical systems they document. Argues for a more pluralistic, system-theoretic approach to safety and accountability in algorithmic governance.

entry.title: DreamFly: Causal Memory and Receding-Horizon Diffusion Planning for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yan Deng, Fei Xu

entry.summary: DreamFly adapts a diffusion-based vision-language-action model to aerial navigation with a causally aligned memory that only uses observations preceding the current decision, receding-horizon diffusion planning for longer lookahead, and a more reliable goal-termination mechanism. Targets partial observability in drone vision-language navigation.

entry.title: Beyond Parameter Space: NTK-Guided Personalized Aggregation for Robust Federated Learning

author.name: Mirko Konstantin, Stefan Zachow, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Proposes federated aggregation weights derived from neural tangent kernel style functional similarity measured by local inference behavior, rather than from parameter or gradient distances that poorly reflect predictive behavior under non-IID data. The aim is robustness to heterogeneous or malfunctioning clients.

entry.title: What Iterated Self-Feeding Probes of Language Models Measure, and a test that separates the construction from the model

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: Asks what iterated self-feeding probes such as self-consistency, refinement loops, and agentic loops actually measure, using a ring of token cells resampled by the model's own windowed conditional as a controlled substrate. Coupling two nearly identical rings under common random numbers turns damage spreading into a measurable quantity and separates properties of the probe construction from properties of the model.

entry.title: Spectral graph clustering with inhomogeneous latent geometry

author.name: Konstantin Avrachenkov, Lucas S. Sibemberg, Alexander Van Werde

entry.summary: Shows that when a latent geometry confounds a network, community structure can still be recovered from eigenvectors deeper in the spectrum, and introduces DBSPEC, a density-based spectral clustering algorithm robust to poor eigenvalue separation. The analysis uses a limiting integral operator and handles general rather than homogeneous toroidal latent geometries.

entry.title: LODESTAR: Trustworthy Entropy Is Navigated, Not Merely Measured -- Reinforced Polarizer Keeps a Frozen LLM from Being Confidently Misled by the Wrong Evidence

author.name: Po-Jen Ko, Che-Cheng Wu, Hung-Chun Hsu, Li-Yang Chang, Chuan-Ju Wang

entry.summary: Shows that selecting retrieval-augmented answers by lowest answer-token entropy improves F1 over top-ranked passages but fails systematically when a misleading passage makes a frozen model confidently wrong. Introduces a reinforced polarizer that intervenes on the reading context so entropy becomes a trustworthy selection signal. Addresses a concrete calibration failure mode in RAG.

entry.title: RT-SEMamba: Real-Time Speech Enhancement Mamba via Progressive Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Rong Chao, Sung-Feng Huang, Moreno La Quatra, Sabato Marco Siniscalchi, Wen-Huang Cheng, Szu-Wei Fu, Yu Tsao

entry.summary: RT-SEMamba is a fully causal speech enhancement model built from causal time-frequency Mamba blocks whose fixed-size recurrent state avoids the growing KV cache of Transformers, plus a progressive knowledge distillation scheme compressing an 8-layer teacher into a 1-layer student. Reports 3.32 PESQ on Voicebank-DEMAND at 25 ms latency and improves the distilled single-layer student from 3.06 to 3.18 PESQ. Practical for real-time on-device enhancement.

entry.title: SCOPE-Router: Cost-Aware Open-Set VLM Routing for Execution-Oriented Tasks

author.name: Tao Yu, Yifei Qu, Zhiqing Cui, Pengfei Zhou, Zhongtian Luo, Yujia Yang, Shenghua Chai, Haopeng Jin, Zhenghao Zhang, Xinming Wang, Hongzhu Yi, Wangbo Zhao, Zhenglin Wan, Yan Huang, Yeshani, Jinwen Luo, Yang You

entry.summary: SCOPE-Router introduces the first execution-oriented VLM routing benchmark (code, agentic and search tasks across 11 models spanning two orders of magnitude in price) plus a dual-tower cost-aware router using hybrid calibration and multi-positive-preserving objectives. Targets the gap between VQA-style routing research and real deployment economics.

entry.title: XYZFlow:Scaling Multi dimensional Shortcut Flows for Efficient Generative Modeling

author.name: Jinxiu Liu, Xuanming Liu, Kangfu Mei, Yandong Wen, Weiyang Liu

entry.summary: XYZFlow proposes multidimensional scaling of flow matching, using structured multidimensional conditioning to make probability paths more identifiable and treating autoregressive context as implicit trajectory straightening, so few-step generation does not require distilling a teacher. Targets the speed-quality tradeoff in image generation from first principles.

entry.title: StateFlow: Building, Evolving, and Accessing 3D World States for Previsualization

author.name: Yuyang Yin, Zixiang Li, Longxuan Deng, Hongkai Li, Shifang Zhao, Junnan Liu, Weirong Huang, Mengyu Wang, Tianxiao Fu, Yikai Wang, Peng-Shuai Wang, Xiaojie Jin, Yao Zhao, Yunchao Wei

entry.summary: StateFlow argues that previsualization for film, games and design needs an explicit persistent 3D world state (geometry, appearance, attributes, cameras) that can be built, evolved and queried, instead of one-shot prompt-driven image or video synthesis. Frames frames as local modifications or recombinations of a shared reusable state to enable controllable iterative editing.

entry.title: HandEdit: A Unified Benchmark for Egocentric Human-to-Robot Dexterous Hand Image Editing

author.name: Zhenjie Yang, Xingyu Jiao, Guopeng Zhong, Shuzhe Yang, Shi Che, Chao Wu, Chenyu Jiang, Dongjie Zhang, Yideng Zhang, Zheng Zhang, Muyun Jiang, Haisheng Su, Shuang Jin, Donghang Zhang, Chao Yang, Li Chen, Hongyang Li, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Xiaosong Jia, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: HandEdit is a large-scale embodiment-aware image editing dataset and benchmark for converting egocentric human hand and arm imagery into various dexterous robot embodiments, so abundant human video can be co-trained with robot policies. Motivated by the appearance, articulation and viewpoint gaps that general editing models cannot bridge without embodiment priors.

entry.title: StellaVLA: In-Context Structured Demonstration for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Siyu Xu, Yunke Wang, Zijian Wang, Dihao Zhu, Chenghao Xia, Chengbin Du, Daochang Liu, Tao Huang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: StellaVLA adapts vision-language-action policies at test time by conditioning on a single retrieved structured demonstration containing a task plan, sub-goal descriptions and verbalized 3D motion, generated automatically without human annotation. Aims to convey intent rather than raw actions so policies survive out-of-distribution scenes, viewpoints and objects.

entry.title: World Tokens: Enhancing Embodied Policies with Training-Time World Modeling

author.name: Qu Tang, Benhui Zhuang, Bo Yuan, Xue Yu, Longteng Guo, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: World Tokens uses world modeling only at training time through a World Adapter that links visual-language understanding, scene dynamics prediction and action generation, so embodied policies gain predictive structure without paying video-model inference cost at deployment. Positions itself between VLAs and heavier world-action models.

entry.title: The Off-Support Barrier: Why Semantic Safety Constraints Are Not Learning-Problem Invariants, and What Follows for Prior Design, Containment, and Verification

author.name: Yoshinori Watanabe

entry.summary: Argues that semantic safety constraints such as not escaping a sandbox are off-support objects not measurable with respect to the model and data distribution, unlike quantities like the real log-canonical threshold from singular learning theory. Derives as corollaries why outcome-based optimization yields reward hacking and why encoding safety through priors or soft penalties has poor leverage.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation

author.name: Ziqiang Wan, Li Gu, Zhixiang Chi, Zhi Liu, Seyed Mehdi Ayyoubzadeh, Yuanhao Yu, Yang Wang

entry.summary: MobileJudgeBench provides 931 human-annotated mobile agent trajectories across six benchmarks, four agent models, and 68 apps to test how reliable LLM-as-judge evaluation actually is in this setting. A simple screenshot-sampling baseline judge matches or beats purpose-built judging methods.

entry.title: Retry, Switch, or Abstain? Learning Strategy-Aware Tool-Use Policies via Controlled Error Injection

author.name: Chaoran Chen, Vy Nguyen, Ziji Zhang, Abhinav Gullapalli, Ziyi Wang, Yuxuan Lu, Dakuo Wang, Jing Huang, Zhou Yu, Jin Lai

entry.summary: BENCH2ROBUST converts failure-free tool-use benchmarks into controlled stochastic environments with transient, persistent, and silent tool failures, where episodes explicitly require retrying, switching paths, or abstaining. Uses this to study Bayesian tool memory as runtime recovery context alongside training-based interventions.

entry.title: Who Thinks Best Depends on How Long You Let Them: Budget-Dependent Rankings in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Rodrigo Guedes de Souza, Alison R. Panisson

entry.summary: Varies the token generation budget across seven levels for four models on three reasoning benchmarks over 56,476 inferences and finds model rankings reverse depending on the budget. Also reports non-monotone items where more budget lowers accuracy even after controlling for truncation, and substantial complementarity between models at constrained budgets.

entry.title: VAKRA: Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Across APIs and Retrieval Under Tool-Use Policies

author.name: Ankita Rajaram Naik, Anupama Murthi, Benjamin Elder, Siyu Huo, Raavi Gupta, Abhinav Jain, Praveen Venkateswaran, Abdulhamid Adebayo, Danish Contractor

entry.summary: VAKRA is a benchmark of over 8,000 executable APIs across 62 domains that jointly tests API interaction, multi-hop reasoning over structured tools, and multi-source reasoning under natural-language tool-use policy constraints. Correctness is verified by re-executing predicted calls against live APIs, allowing multiple valid solution paths.

entry.title: Backtrader-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Algorithmic Trading with Self-Generated MCQs

author.name: Ruoxi Zhao, Maziar Raissi

entry.summary: Introduces a contamination-resistant benchmark for LLM coding agents in algorithmic trading, combining deterministically generated multiple-choice questions derived from backtest configurations with a generator-solver pipeline that keeps only questions unanswerable without executing code. The design targets the twin problems of data leakage and the need for execution-grounded ground truth.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representations for Improved Myocardial Perfusion MRI Quantification

author.name: Christos Tsepas, Chang Yan, Maximilian Fuetterer, Sebastian Kozerke, Cian M Scannell

entry.summary: Extends physics-informed neural networks with spatiotemporal implicit neural representations to fit tracer-kinetic models to dynamic contrast-enhanced cardiac MRI, improving robustness of myocardial perfusion parameter estimation. The approach targets a noisy, ill-posed inverse problem where conventional least-squares fitting is unstable.

entry.title: Consolidator: Learning Persistent Routed Memory Across Context Boundaries

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: Tests whether copying short-term memory into a slower long-term store is enough for state to persist across context boundaries, using a shared slot-local transformation operator in a phasor memory network with KV cache and short-term memory cleared after each consolidation. The retained long-term memory also conditions a hierarchical router, so it influences which slots later inputs access, evaluated on a two-segment modular mapping task.

entry.title: Look What the Probes Dragged In! Real-World Chest X-ray Shortcuts in MedCLIP

author.name: Nikolette Pedersen, Regitze Sydendal, Veronika Cheplygina, Th\'eo Sourget

entry.summary: Attaches 17 linear probes across intermediate layers of MedCLIP's frozen ResNet-50 vision encoder to trace where real-world chest X-ray shortcuts emerge, evaluated with subgroup calibration on NIH-CXR14 and PadChest. Shows how spurious cues propagate through a medical vision-language model rather than only affecting final predictions. Useful for medical AI auditing.

entry.title: Confucius4-TTS: Transcript-Free Cross-Lingual Zero-Shot TTS with a Learnable Speaker Encoder

author.name: Huaxuan Wang, Huimin Wang, Ruiyu Zhang, Yingjie Li, Yitao Duan

entry.summary: Confucius4-TTS is a multilingual zero-shot text-to-speech system covering 14 languages that performs intra-lingual and cross-lingual voice cloning without requiring transcripts of the reference audio, using a two-stage text-to-semantic and semantic-to-acoustic pipeline with a learnable speaker encoder. Removing the transcript dependency makes in-the-wild reference audio usable. Technical report on a deployable system.

entry.title: A Forced-Structure Reduction and Verifiable Bounds for Conway's 99-Graph

author.name: Aalok Thakkar

entry.summary: An autonomous AI research agent attacks the long-open Conway 99-graph problem, producing verifiable partial results: an exhaustive impossibility bound for circulant constructions on the order-99 abelian groups and a forced-structure reduction collapsing existence to a 12-regular graph on 84 vertices. The work is presented as a reproducible agentic mathematics case study scored under a partial-credit metric.

entry.title: Poor Man's Agentic Modeling: Simulating Large LLM-Agent Societies on a Laptop

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: Replaces each LLM agent in a large social simulation with a cheap low-parameter surrogate fitted from a few thousand queries, enabling societies of many agents to be simulated on commodity hardware. Introduces an interaction-order by memory taxonomy that predicts in advance whether surrogate modeling will faithfully reproduce macroscopic behavior.

entry.title: CORA-Diff: Confidence-Oriented Residual Acceptance for Efficient Diffusion Language Model Inference

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yufeng Zhang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: CORA-Diff accelerates diffusion language model decoding by applying confidence-and-persistence gating only to positions the native transfer rule leaves unresolved, keeping the original rule intact and requiring no training. It exploits trajectory signals already present in the denoising process rather than learned filters or cache hacks.

entry.title: A Modular Agentic Framework for Synthetically Constrained Multi-Objective Hit-to-Lead Optimization

author.name: Kelvin P. Idanwekhai, Enes Kelestemur, Benjamin Strickland, Matthew Hart, Steini Davidsson, Angelos Angelopoulos, Ron Alterovitz, Marcello DeLuca, Alexander Tropsha

entry.summary: SABLE is an open-source agentic framework where an LLM interprets medicinal-chemistry goals and routes tasks to specialized tools for reaction-templated analog enumeration, ADMET prediction, docking-based affinity scoring, and Bayesian optimization. It acts as a computational twin of the analyze-and-prioritize stages of the design-make-test-analyze cycle under synthetic-accessibility constraints.

entry.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Sen Xu, Wei Wang, Shixi Liu, Jixin Min, Yingwei Dai, Zhibin Yin, Yirong Chen, Junlin Zhang

entry.summary: CLR reallocates test-time compute from sampling more solutions to targeted verification, condensing each reasoning trace into a few decision-critical claims and attempting semantic falsification of those claims. It exploits the asymmetry that refuting a specific claim is easier than constructing a fully correct solution, and requires no training.

entry.title: TRACE Bench: Task-driven Roleplay Agentic Checklist Evaluation

author.name: Jiahui Zhang, Ziwei Zhang, Yipeng Wang, Yibo Liu, Haozhou Pang, Yikai Hu, Hongyan Ren, Lan Zhou, Qi Gan, Kai Sheng

entry.summary: Proposes a roleplay evaluation framework that decomposes each character profile into a fixed checklist, then uses a user agent to converse while privately tracking which checklist items are satisfied, so scores trace to specific dialogue evidence. It cross-validates coverage against released transcripts from an existing commercial roleplay benchmark.

entry.title: Learning from Multimodal Pseudo-Labels for Robust Open-Vocabulary Instance and Panoptic Segmentation

author.name: Duy Tran Thanh, Yeejin Lee, Byeongkeun Kang

entry.summary: Builds an open-vocabulary instance and panoptic segmentation pipeline that generates pseudo-masks, captions, and labels with pretrained vision-language models, filters synonyms with CLIP guidance, and reconstructs captions with a GPT model to handle out-of-vocabulary terms. The goal is recognizing unseen categories without exhaustive human annotation.

entry.title: Instruction Alignment for Binary Code Representation Learning

author.name: Huaijin Wang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using compiler debug information to supply instruction-level alignment supervision for binary code representation learning, going beyond coarse function-level embeddings. The claim is that finer-grained correspondences yield more accurate and interpretable embeddings for reverse engineering and security tasks.

entry.title: Causal inference for group-contaminated structured outcomes: observable quotients, lossless reduction and exact randomization inference

author.name: Usef Faghihi, Amir Saki

entry.summary: Develops causal inference theory for outcomes observed only after unknown unit-specific group transformations, such as microscopy images with variable acquisition geometry. Characterizes exactly which targets are recoverable, when quotient reduction loses no statistical information, and provides exact randomization inference.

entry.title: Confidence Calibration of Deep Learning Systems

author.name: Coby Penso

entry.summary: A thesis on confidence calibration when clean validation data is unavailable, covering calibration under label noise via an estimated noise model and calibration under distribution shift. Motivated by safe deployment where predicted probabilities must be trustworthy.

entry.title: Defending against Model Extraction for GNNs with Model Reprogramming

author.name: Yan Wen, Zhenyi Wang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: GraphRP is a proactive defense against model-extraction attacks on deployed GNN APIs, repurposing model reprogramming rather than transferring image-domain noise defenses that ignore graph topology. The stated goal is preventing theft in real time while limiting utility loss.

entry.title: RECAST: A Machine-Learning Framework for Correction and Super-Resolution of Coarse-Grid PDE Solvers

author.name: Maryam Reza, Farbod Faraji

entry.summary: RECAST learns in-the-loop corrections to coarse-grid PDE time stepping and simultaneously reconstructs the fine-grid state from corrected coarse history, tested across six 1D PDE families spanning transport, diffusion, dispersion, reaction, and waves. It targets the accuracy loss from aggressive grid coarsening.

entry.title: Learning with Bilevel-Minimax Optimization for Efficient and Reliable Transfer Attacks

author.name: Yaohua Liu, Yifan Guo, Jiaxin Gao

entry.summary: BMAT formulates transfer-based black-box adversarial attacks as a bilevel-minimax problem that jointly couples initialization, surrogate adaptation, and perturbation dynamics, solved with a soft weight modulator and implicit gradient approximator. The aim is more reliable cross-architecture transferability.

entry.title: A Factor Graph Approach to Scalable Multi-Output Gaussian Process Regression

author.name: Wouter W. L. Nuijten, Esther G. van Pelt, Albert Podusenko, \.Ismail \c{S}en\"oz, Wouter M. Kouw

entry.summary: Recasts multi-output Gaussian process regression as message passing on a Forney-style factor graph, ordering candidate inputs into a nearest-neighbor chain along which latent Matern processes evolve with linear-Gaussian transitions. This avoids cubic dense kernel computations and handles outputs observed at different inputs naturally.

entry.title: NAE: Normalizing AutoEncoder

author.name: Muhammad Abdur Rafae, Niels Landwehr

entry.summary: Proves that the loss used by existing flow autoencoders (normalizing flows with approximate inverses) is suboptimal, since encoder and decoder surrogates must be optimized in alignment with the reconstruction objective, and proposes a conditional loss that aligns the surrogate gradient accordingly. Experiments include molecule generation.

entry.title: CookVoice: Unified Framework for Style Controllable Multi-Modal Human Voice Generation

author.name: Haowei Lou, Hye-Young Paik, Dai Jia, Kai Li, Lina Yao

entry.summary: CookVoice is a unified non-autoregressive framework for speech and singing voice generation that factorizes voice into content, prosody, and style with a flexible alignment strategy for multimodal control. It aims to replace task-specific voice cloning and editing systems with one controllable model. Relevant to the trend toward unified generative audio backbones.

entry.title: AWARe: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting via Activation-Weighted Adaptive REtention

author.name: Juncheng Liao, Jinfan Lv, Guoming Wang, Jupeng Zheng, Ling Xiao, Siliang Tang

entry.summary: AWARe mitigates catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuning multimodal LLMs by scoring parameter importance from activation patterns and adaptively constraining updates to parameters critical for prior capabilities. Aims to preserve general multimodal ability while learning downstream tasks. A practical continual-learning regularizer.

entry.title: COGENT: Counterfactual Gaussian Explanations for Volumetric Medical Images

author.name: Dorian Rz\k{a}sa, Bartosz Zabdyr, Krzysztof Piekarz, Jakub Grzywaczewski, Bartlomiej Sobieski, Przemyslaw Biecek, \.Zaneta \'Swiderska-Chadaj, Olga \'Sliwicka, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Joanna \'Swiebocka-Wi\k{e}k

entry.summary: COGENT generates counterfactual explanations for volumetric medical images directly in the parameter space of Gaussian-based 3D representations, optimizing selected Gaussian primitives through differentiable rendering with gradients from a downstream lung cancer risk predictor. Moves medical explainability beyond voxel-space saliency into structured 3D scene representations. Built on MedGS and the Sybil risk model.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Target-Existence Verification and Learned Mask Geometry Refinement: Winning Report of the MeViS-Text Track at the 8th LSVOS Challenge 2026

author.name: Jungyoon Lee, Gyuil Lim, Doeon Kim, Seong-heum Kim

entry.summary: Winning report for the MeViS-Text track of the 2026 LSVOS challenge, using SAM 3.1 to generate full-video candidate masklets and three heterogeneous multimodal LLMs that independently execute each reasoning stage before a synthesis pass commits a schema-validated verdict, including rejecting deceptive no-target expressions. Competition system rather than new method. Documents current practice for referring video segmentation with foundation models.
