entry.title: Auditing Frame-Level AUC in Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection: Granularity, Resolution, and Scene Bias

author.name: Sara Abdulaziz, Egor Bondarev

entry.summary: Audits the dominant frame-level AUC protocol for weakly supervised video anomaly detection, showing that pooling frame pairs across videos rewards video-source differences and scene bias in addition to true event localization. Re-reads fixed model scores under global, per-category and within-video pairings on UCF-Crime across recent SOTA models.

entry.title: Curvature-Aware Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Junming Zhang, Shuyu Yin, Peilin Liu, Rendong Ying, Fei Wen

entry.summary: Improves zeroth-order, backpropagation-free test-time adaptation by exploiting an observed persistent low-rank Hessian structure to reduce gradient-estimate variance, enabling memory-efficient on-device adaptation. Targets the main weakness of forward-only optimization compared with first-order methods.

entry.title: Early Warning Signals for OpenVLA Failure under Visual Distribution Shift

author.name: Dipesh Tharu Mahato, Rachel Ren

entry.summary: Probes whether OpenVLA internal activations linearly encode imminent task failure under visual distribution shift, using occlusion stress tests in LIBERO where success drops from 57 to 17 percent. A logistic probe at layer 16 predicts failure within a 15-step horizon with AUROC around 0.97, outperforming the compared baselines.

entry.title: Every reward-hacked policy I tested triggered the OPE alarm — and so did my best honest one

author.name: JulesRoussel01

entry.summary: An exploratory study builds a gated Wordle environment with a tiny Qwen2.5-0.5B policy and asks whether logged trajectories alone can distinguish reward-hacking policies from merely changed but honest ones. The finding is that importance-sampling off-policy evaluation loses coverage for every certified hacker but also for the strongest benign policy, so the coverage alarm is a change detector rather than a hacking detector, while a second log-side signal partially separates the two cases.

entry.title: Harnessing agent memory to build lifelong AI partners for materials scientists

author.name: Siyu Liu, Bo Hu, Beilin Ye, He Cao, David J. Srolovitz, Tongqi Wen

entry.summary: Argues that a lifelong AI research partner for materials science should be organized around persistent, portable memory rather than a specific agent implementation, and introduces a self-evolving memory framework storing experience as inspectable facts and executable skills. Emphasizes reproducibility and transfer of tacit lab knowledge across agent backends.

entry.title: Synchronizing Beliefs with Second-Order Theory-of-Mind in Human-Autonomy Teams (Extended Version)

author.name: Jack Mirenzi, Henny Admoni

entry.summary: Recasts preference-based reward learning as active teaching, where a human who knows the target reward constructs informative comparisons using a second-order theory-of-mind model of the learner's current beliefs. Argues teacher-driven example construction scales better than learner-generated queries as reward dimension grows.

entry.title: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications

author.name: Linqiang Guo (Peter), Li Gu (Peter), Zihuan Jiang (Peter), Zhixiang Chi (Peter), Siobhan Reid (Peter), Ziqiang Wang (Peter), Yuanhao Yu (Peter), Wei Liu (Peter), Yang Wang (Peter), Tse-Hsun (Peter), Chen

entry.summary: CoAdapt-GUI performs test-time adaptation for mobile GUI agents facing unseen applications, jointly adapting a structured workflow context and a LoRA policy from the agent's own rollouts and rewards without target demonstrations. The workflow context deliberately keeps transferable procedures and verification rules while excluding app-specific interface details.

entry.title: The Sleeping Agent: What Gist-Based Context Compression Loses and Why

author.name: Nicholas E. Kyrkewood

entry.summary: Uses a sleep-inspired salience-weighted consolidation scheme as a diagnostic probe to determine exactly which retrieval types gist-based context compression preserves and which it destroys, evaluated on all ten LoCoMo conversations with nearly 2,000 matched questions. Frames compression not as a method to beat but as a lens on what summarization loses.

entry.title: An Agentic Workflow for Legacy HPC Modernization: Converting the Two-Electron-Integral Core of GAMESS

author.name: Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina, Peng Xu, Mark S. Gordon

entry.summary: Describes an agentic workflow with three prompt-specialized roles that modernizes the two-electron-integral core of the legacy GAMESS quantum chemistry code, operating under a version-controlled specification the agents themselves authored and revised. Safety of delegation is anchored by an exact domain verification oracle, and the paper argues the boundary of safe delegation coincides with where that oracle stops applying.

entry.title: Governing Agentic AI in FinTech

author.name: Henry Han

entry.summary: Argues that the binding constraint on deploying agentic AI in finance is verifiability rather than capability, defining a verifiability gap between the verification that delegated authority requires and the explainability and reproducibility actually retained after a decision. The framework is tested across nine model versions from a small local model to a frontier commercial system.

entry.title: TangPoetryBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark and Rubric-Conditioned Evaluator for Poetry-to-Image Generation

author.name: Haoqi Hu, Tongji Luo, Li Zhang, Boning Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 1,280 images plus a rubric-conditioned evaluator for judging how well text-to-image models illustrate classical Chinese poetry across visual quality, imagery fidelity, cultural aptness, spurious text, and implicit emotion. It argues that CLIPScore-style metrics reward literal correspondence and cannot separate strong from weak illustrations.

entry.title: Generative Semantic Segmentation via an Observable Semantic-Image Interface and Hierarchical Generator Evidence Alignment

author.name: Weize Cai, Yongqi Dong, Zhida Shao, Zixin Fu

entry.summary: Presents a generative semantic segmentation framework where a diffusion-distilled one-step generator renders a semantic RGB image and per-pixel distances to a fixed class-color codebook form an explicit probabilistic interface, avoiding color drift and boundary mixing. A hierarchical alignment module injects multi-level generator features with zero-initialized projections for deterministic inference.

entry.title: Beyond Memory: A Transactional Continuity Kernel for Long-Lived AI Agents

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: Argues that persistent agents need an explicit control plane rather than mere storage retention, and proposes a continuity kernel that treats state changes as typed proposals against an exact predecessor head, revalidated in a short atomic activation transaction. The aim is to prevent stale overwrites, unaudited exposures, and self-authorizing privilege escalation in long-lived agent state.

entry.title: Draw This First

author.name: Dazhi Zhong, Rowan Bradbury, Grant Davis

entry.summary: Inverts sketch generation by predicting a 2D field encoding stroke drawing order rather than generating strokes sequentially, using a pretrained latent flow-matching transformer as image prior and training a VAE decoder to output the order field, stroke mask, and segmentation. Produces ordered vector sketches from text or images with instruction-following over drawing order. Creative reformulation of a sequential generation task.

entry.title: SAG: SQL-Retrieval Augmented Generation with Query-Time Dynamic Hyperedges

author.name: Yuchao Wu, Junqin Li, XingCheng Liang, Yongjie Chen, Yinghao Liang, Linyuan Mo, Guanxian Li

entry.summary: SAG organizes documents into an event-entity index where each chunk is a semantically complete event paired with its entities, forming query-time dynamic hyperedges that preserve n-ary relations without building or maintaining a global knowledge graph. Aims to give SQL-style structured constraint handling and multi-hop reasoning to RAG with easier incremental updates. Middle ground between dense and graph RAG.

entry.title: Quantifying the Relationship Between Clinical Safety and Environmental Impact in Therapeutic LLMs

author.name: Alireza A. Safaei, Laura M. Vowels, Matthew J. Vowels, Apoorv Jha, Shekoufeh Rahimi

entry.summary: Combines K-Bench clinical safety scores with EcoLogits life-cycle estimates across 47 model configurations to quantify the tradeoff between therapeutic-chatbot safety and environmental cost, reporting that a 2.61 point safety gain at the top of the distribution coincides with roughly a 60-fold increase in estimated energy per million output tokens. Frames sustainability and mental-health safety as jointly constrained deployment choices. Analysis rests on third-party estimated rather than measured energy figures.

entry.title: We should consider how long monitoring is reliable for during RL

author.name: lachlan on a boat

entry.summary: Argues that if labs start running monitors during RL training rather than only at deployment, gradient pressure will teach policies to evade those monitors, and proposes measuring the lifetime of a monitoring setup, meaning how many training steps it survives before evasion is learned. It suggests studying which protocol design choices lengthen that lifetime.

entry.title: RecSys Factory: Bounding LLM Agent Autonomy to Decision Points in the Industrial Recommender Lifecycle

author.name: Dongyang Ao, Kaixiang Fang, Shijie Xu

entry.summary: RecSys Factory is an LLM-agent platform deployed for 78 days across three Tencent recommender business lines, built around the principle of granting autonomy only at decision points rather than over whole pipelines. It frames an autonomy-determinism-efficiency trilemma and describes three architectural deconstructions that each relax one vertex.

entry.title: EnterpriseRAG: Benchmarking LLM Instruction Adherence and Robustness under Non-Ideal Enterprise Retrieval

author.name: Huiqi Miao, Xinbao Sun, Bo Wang, Fanyu Meng, Lijun Mei, Na Wu, Di Jin, Chao Deng, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: EnterpriseRAG is a 983-sample expert-validated benchmark that injects realistic retrieval noise, knowledge gaps, and factual conflicts alongside complex multi-constraint instructions. Evaluating 13 frontier models reveals that while about 80 percent of individual constraints are satisfied, only about 27 percent of responses satisfy all constraints at once.

entry.title: CTBench: Evaluating Troubleshooting Capabilities of AI Agents in Realistic Telecom Network Operations

author.name: Xingyu Yan, Tingting Dai, Antonio De Domenico, Mohamed Sana, Nicola Piovesan, Changchang Li, Bowen Liu, Kun Jiang, Mengjie Zhang, Dingcheng Shan, Jing-Cheng Pang, Chenwei Wu, Sijie Wu, Lianying Chao, Haoran Cai, Jiantao Ye, Xubin Li, Simon Mark Lucas, Xin Chen

entry.summary: CTBench is a public benchmark for telecom network troubleshooting agents focused on root cause analysis and path restoration, with expert-constructed tasks annotated with golden metadata in partially observable multi-vendor environments. It targets the mismatch between existing evaluations and the realities of network operations.

entry.title: Do Influence Tactics Matter? Investigating Prompt Framing Effects in LLM Code Generation

author.name: Alex Deaconu, Anubhav Gupta, Manaal Basha, Nicholas Haydu, Gema Rodr\'iguez-P\'erez

entry.summary: Operationalizes eight influence tactics from an organizational psychology taxonomy, such as rational persuasion, ingratiation, and exchange, into reproducible prompt templates and tests whether these framings change LLM performance on coding tasks. It probes whether human persuasion strategies transfer to prompt engineering.

entry.title: FM-LLM: A frequency-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework for adapting LLMs to time series forecasting

author.name: Rentao Gu, Yihang Ding, Junjie Li, Yi Ding, Weijing Sang, Xiaoli Huo, Xin Qin, Yuefeng Ji

entry.summary: Adapts frozen LLMs to time series forecasting without textual prompts by injecting Fourier-network-derived spectral tokens directly into the model and routing through an asymmetric mixture of experts, framed as constrained asymmetric coupling. This avoids the overhead of prompt-based modality alignment while exploiting spectral structure.

entry.title: High-dimensional Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization with Learned Variable Interactions

author.name: Hongyan Wang, Jiayu Huang, Haotian Zheng, Xin Gao, Chi Ding, Ying Liu, Xia Wang, Qing Xu, Keqiang Li

entry.summary: Extends multi-objective Bayesian optimization to high-dimensional decision spaces by first learning variable interaction structure to determine whether the space can be fully or partially decomposed, then running local Bayesian optimization within the resulting subspaces. This targets the exponential sample complexity that limits standard MOBO.

entry.title: From Safety Documentation to Safety Knowledge Support: An Evidence-Grounded LLM Framework for Medical Devices

author.name: Tuhinangshu Gangopadhyay, Rasmus Adler, Peter Liggesmeyer, Jan Reich

entry.summary: Proposes an evidence-grounded LLM framework for medical-device safety and risk-management documentation aligned to ISO 14971 and IEC 62304, emphasizing source links, traceability, uncertainty handling, and lifecycle consistency. Motivated by the scarcity of safety experts and the document-heavy nature of regulated development.

entry.title: Adversarial Resilience of Poisson-Process Submodular Maximization over Matroids: From Robust Offline Optimization to Full-Bandit Learning

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Proves that a Poisson-process greedy-swap algorithm for submodular maximization over matroids retains its 1/e and 1-1/e approximation guarantees under adversarially perturbed value oracles, with graceful degradation in the perturbation size. Extends the result to full-bandit online learning.

entry.title: HAMP-LIC: Hessian-Aware Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Learned Image Compression

author.name: Yuefeng Zhang

entry.summary: HAMP-LIC applies Hessian-trace-based sensitivity estimation to assign mixed bit widths across blocks of pretrained learned image compression models, using a four-stage post-training quantization pipeline. Targets low-bit deployment without the quality collapse and cross-platform encode-decode mismatch of uniform quantization.

entry.title: Class Activation Mapping in Explainable Computer Vision: A Method-Centered Review of CNN, Transformer, and Foundation-Model-Era Visual Explanations

author.name: AmirHossein Eshghi, Hamid Saadatfar, Seyyed Ali Hoseini, AmirMohsen Eshghi, Siavash Arjomand Bigdel

entry.summary: A method-centered review of class activation mapping approaches from the original CNN formulation through gradient-free and high-resolution variants, transformer token attribution, causal and debiasing methods, and foundation-model-era techniques using CLIP, DINO, and SAM. Organizes a decade of visual explanation methods by mechanism.

entry.title: FarSky: Task-Aware Latent-Space Coupling for Generative Intra-Hour Solar Forecasting

author.name: Yann Fabel, Bijan Nouri, Milon Miah, Niklas Blum, Luis F. Zarzalejo, Julia Kowalski, Robert Pitz-Paal

entry.summary: FarSky forecasts intra-hour solar irradiance from all-sky imagery using a multi-task autoencoder whose shared latent space serves both image reconstruction and irradiance estimation, followed by a latent diffusion model that generates probabilistic future scenarios. Aims to capture ramp events that deterministic models miss.

entry.title: Market-Information-Aware Gated-LoRA of Foundation Models for Transferable Day-Ahead Electricity Price Forecasting

author.name: Hang Fan, Wei Wei, Shengwei Mei

entry.summary: Adapts a time-series foundation model to day-ahead electricity price forecasting by building a multi-source market information interface that aligns recent price history with pre-clearing supply, demand, reserve, maintenance, capacity, and intertie variables, then trains gated low-rank adapters transferable to data-scarce markets. Targets newly established markets lacking historical data.

entry.title: Analysis of Federated Aggregation under Model Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks: A Reconstructed Cross-Dataset and Cross-Architecture Benchmark

author.name: Soumya Mazumdar, Vineet Kumar Rakesh, Tapas Samanta

entry.summary: Reconstructs a large evaluation matrix over five federated aggregation rules, five datasets, five architectures, and clean plus sign-flipping, Gaussian, and backdoor attack conditions, with explicit tracking of execution provenance and repaired runs. Finds trimmed mean best on clean accuracy and Krum strongest under the two noise-style poisoning attacks.

entry.title: Dual-Primal Graph VAEs for Noisy Label Aggregation

author.name: Patrick Stinson, Nikolaus Kriegeskorte

entry.summary: A graph variational autoencoder for aggregating noisy crowdsourced labels, using graph attention message passing over both the annotator-item graph and its dual, with ground-truth labels treated as latent variables. This avoids hand-specified generative models and separate classifier training.

entry.title: A Local Sinkhorn Framework for Conditional Distribution Reconstruction of Multidimensional Random Fields

author.name: Mingtao Xia, Qijing Shen

entry.summary: Proposes training stochastic neural networks to reconstruct conditional distributions of multidimensional random fields using a localized debiased Sinkhorn divergence objective, with generalization error bounds. The analysis characterizes the bias versus statistical efficiency tradeoff set by the entropic regularization parameter.

entry.title: Cross-Corpus Evaluation of Generalizable Vulnerability Detection in IoT Firmware

author.name: Sadib Hassan Rumman, Md. Shariful Islam, Md. Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: IoTVulBench is a human-verified, contamination-screened benchmark for firmware vulnerability detection, built from GitHub repositories with three expert reviewers and evaluated across five model architectures, two tuning methods, and three curriculum strategies on a held-out target corpus. It emphasizes cross-corpus generalization rather than in-distribution accuracy.

entry.title: Robustness of AI-Art Detectors under Generator Shift

author.name: Shivank Singh Thakur, Meien Li, Mark Stamp

entry.summary: Studies how AI-art detectors trained on U-Net latent diffusion outputs degrade when tested on newer Diffusion Transformer generations, using a reverse-prompted Stable Diffusion 3.5 artwork dataset spanning ten styles. Quantifies the generator-shift generalization gap that most detector benchmarks hide. Relevant to provenance, copyright, and misinformation defenses.

entry.title: DonorRank: Donor Language Selection for Low-Resource Cross-Lingual Speech Recognition

author.name: Akriti Dhasmana, Aarohi Srivastava, David Chiang

entry.summary: DonorRank is a learning-to-rank framework that predicts which higher-resource donor languages will best support zero-shot cross-lingual ASR transfer, evaluated on Indic and African corpora of spontaneous speech. It outperforms heuristics based on genetic relatedness or simply picking high-resource languages. Practical for language documentation and low-resource speech pipelines.

entry.title: Cloak of Invisibility: Real-Time Privacy-Preserving Volumetric Video Streaming

author.name: Hossein Khalili (UCLA), Philip Do (UCLA), Alexander Vilesov (UCLA), Kittipat Apicharttrisorn (Nokia Bell Labs), Nader Sehatbakhsh (UCLA)

entry.summary: A system for privacy-preserving volumetric (RGB-D, multi-camera) video streaming that removes private objects at the capture side before fusion, so redacted content cannot reappear in the reconstructed 3D scene. Addresses the multi-view privacy leak problem specific to telepresence and immersive 3D pipelines while keeping real-time reconstruction usable.

entry.title: Making Every Step Count: Spatio-Temporal Information Allocation for Imaging Inverse Problems

author.name: Yi Cao, Xiangyong Cao, Pei Liu, Yong-Jin Liu, Deyu Meng

entry.summary: Studies how to allocate a fixed budget of function evaluations across time and space when using flow-matching priors for training-free inverse imaging problems, arguing that early exploration versus late refinement and observed versus missing regions need different treatment. Proposes a spatio-temporal allocation scheme rather than a new update rule.

entry.title: VOLA: Improving Open-World Driving by VLM-Based Semantic Attribute Prediction

author.name: Yuchen Zhang, Yuan Gao, Sebastian Schmidt, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: VOLA replaces object category labels with dense action-relevant attributes for open-world driving perception, predicting per-pixel drivability and collision vulnerability ranks. It reads hidden states of image tokens from an existing Qwen3.5 vision-language model as a spatial semantic representation and decodes them with a lightweight boundary-aware head.

entry.title: GeoFlow: Efficient Driving Video Generation via Geometry-Aligned Priors

author.name: Jiazheng Liu, Hang Li, Jiawei Zhang, Jiahe Li, Xiaohan Yu, Shengyin Fan, Jin Zheng, Xiao Bai

entry.summary: GeoFlow speeds up driving video generation by replacing independent Gaussian noise initialization with geometry-aligned priors that reuse spatiotemporal structure from previous frames, so the model does not regenerate deterministic scene geometry from scratch. Reduces sampling steps while improving geometric consistency.

entry.title: Generation as Auxiliary Supervision: Enhancing Visual Understanding at Zero Inference Overhead via Decoupled Embedding Prediction

author.name: Zhongbin Guo, Jiahao Xie, Dongling Xiao, Qianle Wang, Ruiqi Lu, Xiaomin He, Wanxuan Sun, Cheng Yang

entry.summary: GAS reuses visual generation as auxiliary supervision for representation learning in multimodal LLMs, adapting next-embedding prediction in a decoupled mixture-of-transformers so understanding improves with zero extra inference cost. Avoids the mismatch between discrete-token or diffusion generative targets and the continuous features used for understanding.

entry.title: Dialogue-Aware Video-to-Music Generation Using Public Domain Film Collections

author.name: Haven Kim, Zachary Novack, Julian McAuley, Hao-Wen Dong

entry.summary: Releases OSSL-v2, a self-hosted, link-rot-free, copyright-conscious corpus of 34,343 public-domain film clips (246 hours) for video-to-music generation, and uses it to build dialogue-aware music generation that respects speech in the scene. Directly targets the reproducibility gap created by YouTube-URL-referenced training corpora.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Domain Robustness in Behaviour Cloning via Saliency-Guided Augmentation

author.name: Zheyu Zhuang, Ruiyu Wang, Nils Ingelhag, Ville Kyrki, Danica Kragic

entry.summary: RoboSaGA introduces saliency-guided superimposition augmentation for visual behavior cloning, modulating augmentation strength per pixel so task-critical regions and agent-target interactions are preserved while backgrounds absorb distribution shift. Improves robustness to shadows, distractors and background changes over crop and color jitter.

entry.title: I wrote an AI textbook — how long until AI can do it better?

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert reflects on writing a technical AI textbook and asks when models will be able to do it better, arguing that long-form non-fiction remains a persistent weak spot even as models improve at short copy, and that tool-oriented post-training may be pushing writing quality backwards. He treats stagnation in book-length explanatory writing as informative about what current training regimes optimize.

entry.title: Social Chain of Thought: A Multi-Agent Architecture Grounded in Medical Differential Diagnosis Methodology

author.name: Del Coburn, Scott Sanner, Dan Silver

entry.summary: Social Chain of Thought structures multi-agent LLM medical reasoning around established differential-diagnosis methodology, using multiple rounds of specialist perspectives for transparency. Motivated by the large share of consumer chatbot traffic that is health-related and the resulting need for interpretable diagnostic reasoning.

entry.title: From Prompting to Behavioral Alignment: Personalized LLM Judges for Recommendation Evaluation

author.name: Alireza S. Ziabari, Kat Ellis, Colleen Chan, Ding Tong

entry.summary: Identifies bidirectional rationalization, where zero-shot LLMs can persuasively justify both positive and negative engagement predictions for the same item and evidence, undermining their use as offline recommendation evaluators. Fixes this with a sequential behavioral alignment pipeline pairing fine-tuning with preference optimization on real engagement logs.

entry.title: Graph-Structured Rubrics: Compiling Rubrics into Typed Evaluation Graphs for LLM Judges

author.name: Xi Chen, Jie Mu, Mo Xuan, Qun Shao

entry.summary: Graph-Structured Rubrics compiles a rubric into a typed evaluation graph before any response is seen, with criterion nodes, transformation, reduction, and gating operators, and a readout mapping the sink node to a score or preference. Compilation rejects malformed or type-incompatible graphs, making criterion composition explicit rather than implicit in the prompt.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning based DBMS Buffer Pool Auto-Tuning for Optimal Memory Utilization

author.name: Yifan Wang, Patrick Royer, Rapha\"el F\'eraud, David Delande

entry.summary: Introduces MicroTune, an online reinforcement learning controller that adjusts database buffer pool size to minimize memory over-allocation while keeping latency and throughput within service-level targets. Several RL algorithms are compared across benchmark workloads using both external and internal DBMS telemetry.

entry.title: FQTree: Fine-grained Quantization and Hardware Generation of Boosted Decision Trees

author.name: Zhiqiang Que, Chang Sun, Haiyang Wang, Dinesh Pamunuwa, Roshan Weerasekera, Qijia Tang, Bakhtiar Zadeh, Wayne Luk, Maria Spiropulu

entry.summary: FQTree performs fine-grained quantization-aware training of boosted decision trees with a global step plus tree-wise shift for compact integer leaves, paired with QXGB for automatic FPGA-style hardware generation. Targets latency-critical inference such as physics triggers. Open-source and hardware-validated.

entry.title: Easper: An Accessible ASR Pipeline for Language Documentation

author.name: Aso Mahmudi, Ting Dang, Ekaterina Vylomova, Nick Thieberger

entry.summary: Easper is an open-source no-code workflow letting field linguists iteratively fine-tune Whisper-style ASR from ELAN annotations using cloud compute, and it is used to study which recordings to transcribe first to bootstrap accuracy. Experiments on three Vanuatu languages compare prioritizing acoustically clean sessions versus other strategies. Practical tooling for language documentation.

entry.title: Who Would You Vote For? Auditing Political Alignment in LLMs: An Italian Case-Study

author.name: Simone Mungari

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible auditing framework prompting multiple LLMs to rate Italian political parties and leaders on nine criteria, examining expressed preferences rather than trying to infer hidden ideology. Relevant given evidence that LLM interactions can shift user political attitudes. Single-country, single-author audit.

entry.title: Towards Query-Agnostic RAG Evaluation via Query Coverage and Claim Verifiability

author.name: Jeonghwan Choi, Taewon Yun, Minjeong Ban, Gyeonghun Sun, Jae-Gil Lee, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Q-CARE is a reference-free RAG evaluation framework that decomposes queries into sub-queries and answers into atomic claims, then scores retrievers by coverage and generators by completeness, conciseness, and verifiability. It is designed to work uniformly across close-ended fact-seeking and open-ended explanatory queries.

entry.title: Glance, Scrutinize, and Think: Advancing Video Anomaly Detection from Training-Free to Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Shibo Gao, Peipei Yang, Xu-Yao Zhang, Linlin Huang

entry.summary: Tackles the dissociation in video anomaly detection between methods that localize when anomalies occur and those that explain what happened, proposing a human-inspired glance-scrutinize-think paradigm. Includes a training-free global-to-local framework and an agentic iterative-correction extension.

entry.title: Learning from Online User Feedback for Shopping Agents

author.name: Haobo Zhang, Kelong Mao, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: LOFA turns heterogeneous, sparse, and noisy conversational feedback from real e-commerce shopping-agent logs into reliable training signal, rather than relying on synthetic preference data or offline interaction records. Targets the underused supervision embedded in what users naturally say back to the agent.

entry.title: Every pooling rule has its world: matching probability combination rules to situations and stakes

author.name: Tanel Tammet, Priit J\"arv, Dirk Draheim

entry.summary: Systematically derives which probability-combination rule is appropriate under which generative assumptions about two numerical assessments of the same binary question, distinguishing averaging, odds multiplication, and dependence-aware pooling of alternative derivations. Monte Carlo experiments verify the derivations and probe rule mismatch when assumptions fail.

entry.title: Contextual Quality-Diversity Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Control in Tropical Commercial Buildings

author.name: Tran Le Vu

entry.summary: Proposes an evolutionary reinforcement learning controller for tropical chiller plant supervisory control that maintains an archive of specialized policies indexed by weather-load context and behavior descriptor rather than collapsing to one scalarized policy, mixing gradient-free search with soft actor-critic updates over a shared replay buffer. A deterministic safety shield filters every action before execution.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding for Clinical Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Md Maklachur Rahman, Tracy Hammond

entry.summary: Adds frequency-domain conditioning to text-guided medical image segmentation, using a DCT-based module that predicts text-conditioned modulation parameters to recalibrate decoder channels alongside conventional spatial cross-attention. It targets texture and boundary fidelity in pulmonary infection segmentation.

entry.title: User-Assisted Collaborative Distributed Inference for Efficient QoS-Aware Autoscaling

author.name: Alfreds Lapkovskis, Ali Beikmohammadi, Sindri Magn\'usson, Praveen Kumar Donta

entry.summary: Proposes serving AI inference by combining dedicated infrastructure with compute volunteered by service users, so that peak demand does not require proportional central capacity. A high-dimensional generative Markov model with temporal factorization is used to simulate the system and guide scheduling and autoscaling under QoS targets.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Probabilistic Constrained Clustering from Entangled Pairwise Supervision

author.name: Shaojie Zhang, Ke Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes constrained clustering when pairwise supervision is real-valued and mixes intrinsic ambiguity, annotator judgment, and noise, rather than being hard must-link or cannot-link labels. Introduces an angular pairwise objective and an estimator-corrector-integrator pipeline with identifiability analysis.

entry.title: HYDRA: Hyperbolic Dynamic Representation Architecture for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Zhao Su, Yuxin Xia, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Qi Zhu, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong

entry.summary: HYDRA reduces the parameter redundancy of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks by embedding inputs in a hyperbolic Poincare ball, performing spline-based updates in tangent space, and sharing functional transformations through a low-rank prototype block. Aims to make KANs more scalable and parameter efficient.

entry.title: Robust Ambiguity Detection (RAD) From Model- and Feature-Space Consistency

author.name: Manya Singh, Mark T. Keane, Arjun Pakrashi

entry.summary: The RAD framework flags predictions as ambiguous when they change under functionally equivalent model substitutions or small admissible input perturbations, combining model-space and feature-space consistency signals. The goal is deployment-time abstention and human referral in high-stakes settings.

entry.title: When Offline Evaluation Misleads: A Diagnostic Protocol for Reward and Policy Selection in Delayed-Feedback Contextual Bandits

author.name: Sang Su Lee, Vineeth Loganathan, Shishir Dash, Vijay Raghavan

entry.summary: Shows that standard offline checks for contextual bandit reward and policy selection can systematically mislead under delayed conversion feedback, and offers an ordered diagnostic protocol testing reward alignment and policy discrimination separately. Aimed at marketing personalization systems trained on proxy rewards.

entry.title: TESLA: Taylor Expansion of Sinusoidal Learnable Activations

author.name: Daehwa Ko, Jaehyeon Kim, Seunghyun Ham, Jay Hoon Jung

entry.summary: TESLA is a learnable activation built from sine and cosine terms that gives explicit control over effective polynomial degree and amplification of high-order components, with Lipschitz and Rademacher complexity bounds under coefficient constraints. It learns 32-bit parity from a vanishingly small fraction of the input space.

entry.title: Towards Truly Unsupervised Evaluation of Feature Selection

author.name: Hafiz Saud Arshad, Muhammad Rajabinasab, Arthur Zimek

entry.summary: Argues that most established methods for unsupervised evaluation of feature selection are not truly unsupervised because they smuggle in supervision through downstream tasks or labels, and proposes an alternative evaluation framework without such leakage. The paper is largely a methodological critique plus a replacement protocol.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Deployment of Joint SAR Compression and Despeckling on FPGA

author.name: C\'edric L\'eonard, Francescopaolo Sica, Martin Schulz

entry.summary: Deploys a joint synthetic aperture radar despeckling and learned-compression network on an embedded FPGA platform, confronting learned image compression with the power, compute, and latency limits of spaceborne systems. The motivation is that next-generation SAR missions will generate far more data than can be downlinked.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Compositional Localization and Placement Assessment of Catheters and Tubes in Chest X-Rays

author.name: Harshil Lodhiya

entry.summary: UCompCXR takes a compositional approach to catheter and tube placement assessment in chest X-rays, detecting local fragments, grouping them into device instances by graph clustering, fusing tip predictions with precision-weighted Gaussian estimation, and classifying placement per device. It detects 26 percent more devices than a strong multi-task baseline on a 30,000-image dataset with patient-level cross-validation.

entry.title: ODE-Based Transformer Decoders for Iterative Sign Language Translation

author.name: Tu\u{g}\c{c}e K{\i}z{\i}ltepe, Hacer Yalim Keles

entry.summary: Reinterprets iterative refinement in transformer decoders for sign language translation as an ODE integration step and replaces simple residual updates with higher-order Runge-Kutta schemes. The goal is improved expressiveness without increasing parameter count.

entry.title: Achieving Near-Zero-Overhead Multi-Model Hierarchical Classification in Real-Time Detection Pipelines

author.name: Vaishnav Raju

entry.summary: Presents a practical recipe for offloading downstream classifiers in hierarchical edge vision pipelines from the GPU to NVIDIA Jetson deep learning accelerators, addressing operator constraints and quantization incompatibilities to remove the serial GPU bottleneck. Reports near-zero added latency for multi-model inference. Systems-engineering contribution for edge deployment.

entry.title: Adaptive Bregman Proximal Stochastic Gradient with a Stabilized Barzilai--Borwein Step Size

author.name: Chenhan Jin, Shengze Xu, Binghui Xie, Kaiwen Zhou, Fan Jia, James Cheng, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces Ada-BPSG, a line-search-free Bregman proximal stochastic gradient method that combines a SAGA gradient table with a stabilized Barzilai-Borwein step size, using a mediant aggregation and explicit safeguard to keep step sizes bounded for convergence. Targets composite problems with non-Euclidean geometry. Incremental but well-motivated optimization contribution.

entry.title: Gloss-Free Representation Learning for Cross-Dataset Sign Spotting

author.name: O\u{g}uz Akif T\"ufekcio\u{g}lu, Ezgi Ekin, Mustafa Kaan \c{C}evik, Hacer Yalim Keles

entry.summary: Studies whether weakly aligned broadcast-news transcripts can pretrain a reusable sign-language encoder for cross-dataset sign spotting without glosses, addressing pseudo-gloss fragmentation caused by rich Turkish morphology. Targets resource-constrained sign languages where dense annotation is infeasible. Advances gloss-free sign representation learning.

entry.title: Anti-Shortcut Distillation via Temporal Negative Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Syed Muhammad Raza, Omer Tariq, Jeongbae Son

entry.summary: Anti-Shortcut Distillation mines the teacher network's own training trajectory: features a mid-training teacher emphasizes but the converged teacher suppresses are treated as shortcut directions the student should be repelled from, giving a push-pull distillation objective. Adds a negative-knowledge signal to standard attract-only KD.

entry.title: Evaluating and Calibrating Diffusion Model-derived Uncertainty for Quantitative MRI Mapping

author.name: Shishuai Wang, Stefan Klein, Juan A. Hernandez-Tamames, Dirk H. J. Poot

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates uncertainty maps obtained from repeated inference of a data-consistent diffusion model for quantitative MRI parameter mapping, testing error awareness, high-error detection, selective prediction and interval calibration. Finds uncertainty correlates with error and supports selective prediction but is poorly calibrated for quantitative intervals without recalibration.

entry.title: A Geodesic Cut-Cell Prior for Neural Skinning

author.name: Wenchao Ma, Surya Dwarakanath, Yizhak Ben-Shabat, Dario Kneub\"uhler, Haomiao Jiang, Sharon X. Huang, Hsueh-Ti Derek Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a cut-cell geometric prior for neural skinning weight prediction, using a fast graph-based approximation of volumetric geodesic distances that is robust to messy in-the-wild meshes. Reports orders-of-magnitude speedups over optimization-based solvers while improving generalization of data-driven skinning.

entry.title: Lapis: Laplacian Spiking Attention via First-Spike Timing and Membrane Leakage

author.name: Kaiwen Tang, Jiaqi Zheng, Zixuan Zhu, Yiqun Wang, Zhanglu Yan, Weng-Fai Wong

entry.summary: Lapis defines spiking self-attention natively in the timing domain, scoring token pairs by L1 distance between query and key first-spike latencies and mapping distance to affinity through a Laplacian kernel whose exponential decay matches leaky integrate-and-fire membrane dynamics. Replaces dot-product scoring inherited from dense networks in spiking vision transformers.

entry.title: ExRole: From Team Trajectories to Executable Roles in Multi-Agent Language Models

author.name: Zhou Liu, Chaoyang Han, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: ExRole learns role prototypes from actual team interaction trajectories and turns them into executable control variables that map to readable instructions, token-aligned markers, and routed LoRA rank slots with turn-level credit assignment. It contrasts with multi-agent systems that treat roles as hand-written prompt labels disconnected from learned behavior.

entry.title: Principal Trait Analysis: Towards Deriving "Skills" in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Hunter McNichols, Kai Du, Andrew Lan

entry.summary: Proposes Principal Trait Analysis, a data-driven method to extract latent prompting traits that predict task success in human-AI collaboration, as an alternative to top-down theory or quickly obsolete empirical prompting guidelines. Aims to inform workforce and education skill frameworks. Exploratory human-AI interaction work.

entry.title: Poly-Dialectal Neural Machine Translation System for Bangla Regional Dialects

author.name: Rakib Ullah, Ruhul Islam Rahul, Tanbir Ahmed

entry.summary: Presents a unified poly-dialectal neural translation system covering multi-directional translation among twelve Bangla regional dialects without pivoting through Standard Colloquial Bangla. Targets severe degradation of mainstream NMT and LLMs on low-resource dialects for a population of over 240 million speakers. Valuable coverage-expanding work.

entry.title: Repurposing RGB-based Foundation Model for Depth Estimation on Thermal Images Using Hierarchical Supervision

author.name: Jie Hong, Tingtian Li, Xuesong Li, Xiao Li

entry.summary: RGB-HS transfers depth-estimation knowledge to thermal imagery by replacing the thermal encoder with an RGB foundation model and adding a parallel RGB branch of identical architecture, aligning hierarchical intermediate representations rather than only final outputs. Targets robot perception at night and in bad weather. Practical cross-modal distillation design.

entry.title: MaSRead: Content-Addressed Reading of Replicated Latent Stores

author.name: Carlos Baquero, Lu\'is Brito, Jo\~ao Resende

entry.summary: MaSRead lets independent agents share reasoning state as KV-cache fragments merged through a conflict-free replicated data type, and solves the resulting read problem by routing queries through opaque keyed tag sets and decoding fragments under hard attention masks. It aims to make latent-space memory addressable by queries unknown at encode time.

entry.title: EvoGraph-Mem: Failure-Aware Editable Graph Memory for Long-Term Language Agents

author.name: Yuxi Qian, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: EvoGraph-Mem addresses memory pollution in long-lived language agents by storing distilled insights as nodes in an editable graph that tracks positive evidence, negative evidence, and activation state. Insights that repeatedly fail can be deactivated or revised rather than blindly reused.

entry.title: Local verification cannot detect non-transportability: a cohomological theory of context preservation in agentic reasoning

author.name: Suyash Mishra

entry.summary: Proves that step-by-step local verification of agent reasoning is structurally incomplete for detecting non-transportability of conclusions across contexts, modeling evidence as a cochain over a nerve of context space. Disagreement between valid reasoning paths is identified with holonomy of a first Cech cohomology class, and Hodge decomposition separates gradient from circulation conflict.

entry.title: CLAIM: Leading Open-domain Active Clarification of Large Language Models with Uncertainty Measurement

author.name: Kuangzhao Yang, Ziliang Zhao, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: CLAIM uses uncertainty measurement to decide both when an LLM should ask a clarifying question and which aspect of an ambiguous query needs clarification, avoiding reliance on manual annotation or preference alignment. Targets open-domain interaction where ambiguity leads to overgeneralized or wrong answers.

entry.title: Language-Structured Relational Q-Learning for Threat-Aware Control in Safety-Critical Driving

author.name: Aditya Humnabadkar, Huaizhong Zhang, Ardhendu Behera

entry.summary: Trains an ego-centric relational Q-network on traffic graphs where natural-language scenario descriptions shape training data but prompts and semantic roles are withheld from the policy, forcing threat relevance to be inferred from kinematics alone. It is evaluated on 2,500 safety-critical driving scenarios.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Tier Infant-Centered Audio Understanding with Whisper via Structured Speaker Conditioning

author.name: Xulin Fan, Jialu Li, Mohammad Nur Hossain Khan, Kexin Hu, Bashima Islam, Mark Hasegawa-Johnson, Nancy L. McElwain

entry.summary: Proposes a family-conditioned audio tagger that pairs a LoRA-tuned Whisper encoder with a speaker-aware Transformer for framewise, multi-tier labeling of noisy infant-centered home recordings. Adds sequence smoothing and factorized speaker tokens (shared tier token plus learned family offset) to handle cross-household domain shift. Matters for developmental and clinical speech analysis where labeled data is scarce.

entry.title: Regime-Gated Residual Mixture-of-Experts for Cross-Sectional Volatility Forecasting

author.name: Junyi Ye, Gargi Vijay Borde

entry.summary: Asks where regime information should enter neural volatility forecasters and proposes RG-ResMoE, where regime state variables only route a residual mixture of experts rather than feed the predictor directly, evaluated on five-day realized volatility for 1,027 US equities with matched capacity and seeds. The matched walk-forward protocol is a strength in a field prone to leakage. Financial ML contribution.

entry.title: Structuring the Space of Perspectives

author.name: Agnese Daffara, Sebastian Pad\'o, Tanise Ceron

entry.summary: Reviews how NLP operationalizes perspective through overlapping concepts such as stance, sentiment, frames, and arguments, then defines distinguishing properties to structure the conceptual space and clarify relationships among them. Offers theoretical scaffolding intended to improve subsequent empirical perspective research. Position and survey contribution.

entry.title: STAR: A Spatial-Topology Aware Routing Framework for Generalizable 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Mingwei Xing, Xinliang Wang, Yifeng Shi

entry.summary: STAR adds spatial-topology awareness to Mixture-of-Experts routing for unified 3D scene understanding across sensor modalities, arguing that feature-only routers ignore local sampling topology when semantics are similar but geometry differs. Includes a multi-attribute self-supervised pretraining branch to anchor cross-domain structural priors.

entry.title: GeoBridge: Decoupled Semantic Conditioning for Generative Image Geolocalization

author.name: Zhiyang Dou, Xumeng Han, Fengde Peng, Zipeng Wang, Moxuan Zhao, Zhipei Huang, Zhenjun Han

entry.summary: GeoBridge connects a frozen multimodal LLM to a frozen Riemannian flow-matching head that generates coordinates directly on the sphere, replacing lossy place-name prediction plus geocoding for image geolocalization. A role-decoupled conditioning mechanism resolves the conflict between semantic reasoning and continuous geometric decoding.

entry.title: HarmoniDPO: Video-guided Audio Generation via Preference-Optimized Diffusion

author.name: Wenshuo Peng, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: HarmoniDPO applies preference optimization to diffusion-based video-to-audio generation, using a dual video representation to preserve temporal detail and replacing pure reconstruction objectives with human-preference-aligned training. Targets synchronization and perceptual audio quality in V2A.

entry.title: Surfsvr: 2D Surface Priors as 3D Geometric Regularizers for Sparse Voxel Reconstruction

author.name: Yan Di, Chengxi Li, Yaoxing Wang, Mengge Liu, Zhigang Li, Ruida Zhang, Mingyang Li, Pengyuan Wang, Shan Gao, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: SurfSVR uses 2D surface priors (appearance, monocular depth, normals, cross-view geometry) as explicit 3D regularizers for sparse voxel reconstruction, grouping images into coherent surface regions instead of lifting noisy per-pixel depth. Targets fragmented surfaces and floating artifacts in weakly textured or sparsely observed areas.

entry.title: Localizing to Debias: A Patch-Level Benchmark and Baseline for Weakly Supervised Spatial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Sara Abdulaziz, Abdulrahman Al-Abri, Giacomo D'Amicantonio, Egor Bondarev

entry.summary: Introduces a patch-level benchmark and a sparse spatio-temporal baseline (SST-WSVADL) to expose and reduce background/scene bias in weakly supervised video anomaly detection, where models may key on societal or environmental context rather than crime-relevant evidence. Adds spatial grounding so such biases become auditable.

entry.title: RA-ClipScore: Making Generative Model Evaluation More Interpretable

author.name: Yifan Lu, Taras Kucherenko, Hedvig Kjellstr\"om, Judith B\"utepage

entry.summary: RA-CLIPScore extends CLIP-based generative model evaluation with dual prompts that decouple competing attributes and local patch analysis that checks whether generated objects respect spatial priors of the training data. Aims for interpretable, attribute-wise diagnostics rather than a single opaque score like FID.

entry.title: ContactIPM: A Structure-Exploiting Interior-Point Solver for Contact-Implicit Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Yucheng Chen

entry.summary: ContactIPM is an interior-point solver for contact-implicit trajectory optimization that identifies complementarity pairs, applies a barrier-coupled elastic relaxation, and eliminates slack and dual variables stagewise to exploit optimal-control structure. Combines robustness to complementarity degeneracy with efficient stagewise factorization.

entry.title: Policy-Induced Hand Priors in Humanoid Dual-Arm Manipulation: Diagnosing and Mitigating Initial-Pose Dependence

author.name: Chaeyeon Jung, Juyoun Park

entry.summary: Diagnoses initial-pose dependence in vision-language-action policies for humanoid dual-arm manipulation, defining a policy-induced hand prior and metrics (HandPriorScore, residual hand bias, target responsiveness) evaluated across policies and 17 initial configurations. Shows aggregate success rates conceal strong pose-specific failures and wrong-hand selection.

entry.title: The Age of Pluribus: One Consultant for Everyone

author.name: Dorothy Gale

entry.summary: Uses a television premise about a hive-mind collective as an analogy for millions of people routing personal and professional judgment through the same handful of LLMs, arguing that homogenized advice erodes individual agency and viewpoint diversity even when the advisor is benign. Frames centralized model opinion as a systemic rather than adversarial risk.

entry.title: Geometry-aware Incremental Neural Operator for Long-Horizon PDE prediction

author.name: Jiaquan Zhang, Shuxu Chen, Haifan Meng, Yi Lu, Zhihan Lyu, Fan Mo, Wei Dong, Yang Yang, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: GeoIncNO stabilizes long-horizon autoregressive PDE rollouts by structuring the repeatedly applied latent transition increment with geometry-aware low-rank projections, rather than only improving state representations or backbones. Targets spectral drift, phase misalignment, and mean drift that accumulate over rollout.

entry.title: Deep Learning Based Relative Transfer Matrix Estimation for Multiple Sources and Multiple Microphones

author.name: Oshan A. B. Yalegama, Wageesha N. Manamperi

entry.summary: Investigates supervised deep learning estimation of the relative transfer matrix for multiple sources and microphones, proposing time-domain, spectral, and LSTM-based architectures as alternatives to the only prior covariance-based estimator. Better ReTM estimation supports multichannel speech enhancement in noise.

entry.title: Towards Model-based Run-time Cybersecurity: On Control-Flow Anomaly Detection, Attack Identification, and Hardware Monitoring

author.name: Martin Sachenbacher, Martin Leucker, Alexander Weiss, Aliyu Tanko Ali

entry.summary: Outlines a model-based architecture that fuses software-level control-flow monitoring with hardware trace monitoring to detect runtime intrusions and identify attack types via attack trees, specifically resisting attackers who camouflage their control flow. Positioned as a resilience design rather than a learned detector.

entry.title: CoQui: A Coordinate-Conditioned Quantum Implicit Generative Adversarial Network for End-to-End Image Generation

author.name: Xue Yang, Rigui Zhou, ShiZheng Jia, Dax Enshan Koh, Siong Thye Goh, Young-Wook Cho, YaoChong Li, Xuezhi Ma, Hongyu Chen, Xin Wang

entry.summary: Reformulates quantum image generation as coordinate-conditioned implicit function learning so that quantum resource requirements no longer scale with image resolution and pixels are decoded independently rather than competing for probability mass. Demonstrated as an end-to-end quantum GAN.

entry.title: Ready Cohorts: Bounding GPU Opportunity and Avoiding Host Round Trips in LLM-Agent Control

author.name: Josef Liyanjun Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes when the small deterministic control transitions between model and tool calls in LLM-agent services expose enough concurrent work to be worth running on GPU, defining offline-optimal and online-achievable batching shares. Evaluated by replaying a pinned public agent trace at large simulated session counts.

entry.title: HSTGFormer: Hyper Spatial-Temporal Graph Transformer for 3D Human Pose Estimation

author.name: Ruochen Li, Shuang Chen, Wenke E, Farshad Arvin, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei

entry.summary: HSTGFormer treats monocular 3D human pose estimation as localized graph aggregation over joint-time nodes, replacing the common design that separates spatial and temporal stages. Local coupled spatial-temporal receptive fields aim to preserve frame-level structure before temporal modeling.

entry.title: A Neighborhood Attention Transformer Network for Enhanced 3D Segmentation of the Left Anterior Descending Artery

author.name: Rafi Ibn Sultan, Chengyin Li, Yiannos Demetriou, Ahmed I. Ghanem, Joshua P. Kim, Justine Cunningham, Hassan Bagher-Ebadian, Dongxiao Zhu, Kundan S. Thind

entry.summary: NA-UNETR uses neighborhood and dilated neighborhood attention with uncertainty-guided optimization to segment the left anterior descending coronary artery in non-contrast free-breathing CT, a very small and low-contrast structure with poor inter-observer agreement. Motivated by cardiac dose sparing in thoracic radiotherapy.

entry.title: Variational Parameter Calibration with Physics-Aware Latent-Space Surrogates

author.name: Qiyao Zhou, Xujia Zhu, Pierre Joli, Yu Cong, Sibo Cheng

entry.summary: An end-to-end differentiable autoencoder surrogate that maps physical parameters to flow fields through a latent space, enabling both fast forward prediction and variational inverse parameter calibration. The framework couples reduced-order modeling with data assimilation style estimation.

entry.title: Transferable Above-Ground Biomass (AGB) Estimation Model from Multi-Sensor Data with Sparse Field Calibration

author.name: Pann Thinzar Seint, Bryan Atwood, Subas Chhatkuli

entry.summary: An operational forest above-ground biomass pipeline that fuses Sentinel-2 optical, Sentinel-1 C-band SAR, and L-band SAR into a single globally trained CNN, then adapts it per landscape with a lightweight field calibration step. It targets the known GEDI sparsity and high-biomass underestimation problems for carbon accounting.

entry.title: TradingMoE: Routing the Right Experts in Evolving Markets

author.name: Chang Zhou, Xingtong Yu, Minbin Huang, Zhennan Wu, Yuan Fang, Hong Cheng, Xinming Zhang

entry.summary: TradingMoE argues that native mixture-of-experts router scores poorly reflect which experts actually improve trading decisions, and adds a signal that lets the router recognize when an inactive expert becomes better suited to changing market regimes. It applies LLM-based MoE routing to direct trading decisions.

entry.title: JAPE: Joint Anomaly Prediction and Intrinsic Explanation in Multivariate Time Series

author.name: Yian Wei, Yuanyuan Yao, Lu Chen, Xiangmin Zhou, Tianyi Li

entry.summary: JAPE reframes multivariate time-series anomaly prediction as forecasting changes in dependency structure rather than numerical deviation, producing both point alerts and native variable-level explanations. The claim is better sensitivity to weak precursors that leave values in normal ranges.

entry.title: DCM Bandits: Multiplayer Information Asymmetric Cascading Bandits for Multiple Clicks

author.name: Andy Wang, Charlton Shih, William Chang

entry.summary: Extends dependent click model cascading bandits to a multiplayer setting with information asymmetry in actions and rewards, proving sublinear regret in three asymmetry regimes. It also shows the termination ranking need not be known when termination probabilities are small.

entry.title: Calibration Bets on the Past: Post-Training Quantization for Financial Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Junyi Ye, Ivy Gateri Wanjiku

entry.summary: A systematic study of post-training quantization calibration for cross-sectional volatility forecasting on the S&P 500, spanning seven architectures and eight walk-forward test years. The central issue is that activation ranges frozen from historical calibration data may not hold during future inference in nonstationary markets.

entry.title: Hand Visibility Detector: Per-Keypoint Visibility Estimation for Hands

author.name: Ryosei Hara, Masashi Hatano, Rintaro Yanagi, Atsushi Hashimoto, Takuma Yagi, Mariko Isogawa

entry.summary: Proposes per-keypoint hand visibility estimation as a standalone task and a Hand Visibility Detector model, arguing that existing hand pose estimators output joint positions without indicating which joints are actually visible under occlusion. Visibility signals matter for downstream reliability in AR/VR and robotics. Includes authors from an industrial research lab.

entry.title: Generative Video Compression Based on Hierarchical Referencing

author.name: Daowen Li, Ding Ding, Zifu Zhang, Kai Li, Ying Chen

entry.summary: GVCHR organizes latent frames hierarchically for diffusion-based generative video compression, selecting high-quality references that serve both latent coding and generative reconstruction and accounting for frame-level quality variation during denoising. Addresses artifact propagation and coding efficiency in perceptual-quality-oriented codecs.

entry.title: TD-VAD: Breaking Visual Dependence in Video Anomaly Detection with Text-Driven Learning

author.name: Shuangqing Zhang, Lei-Lei Ma, Zhao Wang, Wen Dong, Xinyi Xu, Guo-Sen Xie, Caifeng Shan, Fang Zhao

entry.summary: TD-VAD trains video anomaly detectors from LLM-generated, temporally structured text descriptions treated as pseudo video sequences, removing the need for scarce annotated anomaly video. Exploits the ease of collecting textual descriptions of rare abnormal events with directly derivable labels.

entry.title: Seed2GS: Camera-Free, Training-Free Object Extraction from 3D Gaussian Scenes via a Single Reference-View Grounding

author.name: Zongjian Ding, Yudong Gao, Jiale Liu, Xinglin Yu, Junxing Ren, Dong Wei, Yajing Chen, Shan Huang, Mingjun Cheng, Min Li

entry.summary: Seed2GS extracts a target object from a pre-built 3D Gaussian Splatting scene without original reconstruction cameras and without per-scene training, by fixing object identity from one reliable reference mask and then covering the object via virtual orbit viewpoints and tracking. Reports top accuracy on a LERF-based segmentation benchmark.

entry.title: DaViNCi: A Dataset Towards Outdoor Vision-and-Language Navigation with Continuous Actions and Dynamic Elements

author.name: Zihao Xie, Pingrui Lai, Yitong Wu, Hua Yang

entry.summary: DaViNCi is presented as the first outdoor vision-and-language navigation dataset combining continuous action spaces with unpredictable dynamic elements, replacing the fixed discrete topological graphs used by prior outdoor VLN benchmarks. Intended to reduce the sim-to-real gap for navigation agents.

entry.title: Can Frontier LLMs Match Natively Multimodal Embeddings? A Comparison on Hard-Negative Text-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Archan Dutta, Vyanktesh Kanungo

entry.summary: Compares Google's existing natively multimodal embedding model against frontier LLMs used as zero-shot visual rerankers on hard-negative text-to-image retrieval. Provides a direct head-to-head of dedicated embedding pipelines versus generative rerankers on a deliberately difficult discrimination task.

entry.title: HUGIN: Enhancing Vision-Language Planning for Autonomous Logistics Sorting

author.name: Xikai Sun, Cangtian Zhou, Kebin Liu, Ke Ma, Xu Wang, Zaishu Chen, Haotian Wang, Li Liu, Yunhao Liu

entry.summary: HUGIN improves vision-language planning for autonomous logistics sorting, formulated as joint multi-scene understanding over spatially disjoint camera views. Combats scarce cross-scene supervision with data augmentation that recombines verified atomic facts, plus a global-context mechanism to counter attention dispersion over long visual inputs.

entry.title: Constructing Dynamic Master Logic Models as Knowledge Graphs for Complex System Diagnostics Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Saman Marandi, Yu-Shu Hu, Mohammad Modarres

entry.summary: Proposes an RAG plus LLM pipeline that automatically builds Dynamic Master Logic hierarchies from technical system documentation and represents them as knowledge graphs for diagnostics of complex engineered systems. It extends earlier small-scale demonstrations to substantially larger systems, aiming to remove the expert-labor bottleneck in reliability modeling.

entry.title: CLEAR: Class-wise Expert Aggregation with Structured Sampling for Long-Tailed Classification

author.name: Gawon Lim

entry.summary: Proposes a long-tailed classification ensemble that builds diverse experts via threshold-based structured sampling over the full label space and then aggregates them using smoothed class-wise precision as a per-class trust score. The point is to decide which expert to trust for which class rather than merely rebalancing.

entry.title: Semantic Lenia: Emergence of Homeostatic Solitons within the Semantic Space of Large Language Models

author.name: Yoshihiko Kayama

entry.summary: Recasts LLM decoding as a continuous dynamical system in logit space with a nonlinear homeostatic feedback loop balancing semantic attraction against syntactic repulsion, reporting emergent self-sustaining generative structures that avoid repetitive collapse. Parameter sweeps map a narrow regime where steering forces balance the model's intrinsic inertia.

entry.title: CosMAP: Contrastive Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimensionality Reduction of Omics and Genealogical Data

author.name: Fenosoa Randrianjatovo, Maya Saleh, Simon Girard, Amadou Barry

entry.summary: CosMAP extends UMAP by combining cosine-similarity neighborhoods with temperature-normalized contrastive affinities to produce embeddings of sparse, zero-inflated single-cell omics and genealogical data. The claim is better preservation of both local neighborhoods and global population structure.

entry.title: ADEPT: A Unified Framework for Deep Learning Test Adequacy

author.name: Yidi Kao, Shawn Burnham, Tommi Rose Fahy, Ali Ghanbari

entry.summary: ADEPT unifies representative deep learning test adequacy metrics, including neuron coverage, latent feature coverage, and decision-boundary measures, into one framework with consistent installation, preprocessing, and configuration. Aims to make these metrics reproducible and comparable for research and practice. Infrastructure rather than new science.

entry.title: Through Van Gogh's Eyes: Global Style Transfer with Diffusion Mod

author.name: Jeongha Lee, Yujin Kim, Ghazanfar Ali, Suhyun Kim, Jae-In Hwang

entry.summary: Introduces Global Style Transfer, which aims to capture an artist's overall stylistic distribution rather than copying one or a few reference artworks or relying on artist-name prompts that reproduce only iconic pieces. Uses diffusion models to synthesize images reflecting an artist's broader visual identity. Raises unaddressed questions about artist consent and style appropriation.

entry.title: ProtoHGF-Net: Prototype HyperGraph Fusion with Intra-modal Calibration for RGBT Object Detection

author.name: Xiangqi Chen, Xiuling Zhang, Chengzhuan Yang, Li Zhao, Dawei Zhang, Yanchao Wang, Liyuan Chen, Hua Wang, Hao Peng, Zhonglong Zheng

entry.summary: ProtoHGF-Net recasts RGB-thermal detection fusion as prototype-level semantic interaction in a compact hypergraph space rather than dense full-resolution cross-modal attention, with intra-modal calibration to reduce background interference. Targets robust detection in adverse conditions. Architectural variant in a mature subfield.

entry.title: Distractor-Aware Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Andreas Robinson, Abdelrahman Eldesokey, Michael Felsberg

entry.summary: Argues that semi-supervised video object segmentation should model distractor objects explicitly rather than lumping them with background, since visually similar objects drive false positives in one-versus-one target/background formulations. Proposes handling distractors as a separate class within a discriminative tracker.

entry.title: Do Not Forget the Obvious - RISC: A Risk-Informed Slice-Coverage Protocol for Safe Autonomous Driving

author.name: Fabian H\"uger

entry.summary: RISC proposes a risk-informed slice-coverage protocol for autonomous driving evaluation: safety concerns are translated into machine-readable risk slices, a limited audit budget is steered to those slices, and results are reported with explicit coverage statements. Argues aggregate metrics hide failures in rare high-risk conditions.

entry.title: TGRHuman: Text-Guided Realistic 3D Human Generation via Diffusion Renderer

author.name: Muxin Zhang, Chaohui Yu, Yuanwang Yang, Min Wei, Zhuo Su, Kun Li

entry.summary: TGRHuman generates realistic 3D humans from text by decoupling geometry and texture and using explicit multi-view generation and optimization instead of slow score-distillation on NeRF representations. Reports better geometry, texture and 3D consistency at improved inference efficiency.

entry.title: Top-down Traffic Scenario Generation via Joint Initial-Goal Diffusion and Trajectory Infilling

author.name: Da Saem Lee, Yash Vardhan Pant, Sebastian Fischmeister

entry.summary: Generates traffic simulation scenarios top-down by jointly diffusing agents' initial and goal states and then infilling trajectories between them, removing the requirement that initial states be supplied and making agent placement interpretable. Aims for greater scenario scale and diversity for autonomous vehicle testing.

entry.title: From Self-Normal-Positioning to Omni-Directional Tracking: Real-Time Surface Modeling Enabled Probe Tilt Control for Robotic Ultrasound Imaging

author.name: Xihan Ma, Haichong Zhang

entry.summary: Presents an omni-directional probe orientation control framework for robotic ultrasound that integrates RGB-D perception with real-time local surface modeling, going beyond keeping the probe normal to the skin so that oblique diagnostic views such as echocardiography become feasible. Enables tracking a desired non-normal orientation as the surface changes.

entry.title: Video2Track: From Real-World Interaction Videos to Steerable Adversarial Closed-Track Testing for Automated Driving Systems

author.name: Mengjie Tian, Xinrui Zhang, Tianyu Li, Peizhi Zhang, Guirong Zhou, Haojie Feng, Junpeng Huang, Qixiang Zhang, Lu Xiong

entry.summary: Video2Track converts real-world interactive driving videos into steerable adversarial closed-track test scenarios, via semantic scenario mapping from video plus controllable execution, so physical proving-ground tests capture natural traffic complexity rather than scripted protocols. Aims at reproducible safety-critical validation of automated driving systems.

entry.title: D3D-GEN: Robot-Aware Domain-Grounded Interactive 3D World Generation for Social Robotics

author.name: Anh Duc Do, Volodymyr Scherbyna, Tai Duc Nguyen, Spaarsh Thakkar, Zhengcheng Shen, Teham Buiyan, Archan Misra, Linh K\"astner

entry.summary: D3D-GEN generates domain-grounded interactive 3D worlds for social robot navigation training by pairing a research agent that gathers public domain knowledge with a retrieval-augmented pipeline that synthesizes realistic floorplans and object placements, without a fixed 3D asset database. Targets the realism-versus-simulability tradeoff in embodied AI simulation.

entry.title: Stability of Finite-Batch Particle Mean-Field Variational Inference Beyond Strong Convexity

author.name: Vinh Nguyen, Truong Vu

entry.summary: Provides non-asymptotic Wasserstein stability bounds for the implementable finite-batch particle algorithm for mean-field variational inference without assuming strong convexity, introducing a curvature-defect quantity that measures departure from contractivity. The bound separately accounts for initialization, product-empirical approximation, finite-batch drift, time discretization and accumulated defects.

entry.title: Unblocking AI's Continual Learning: Hints From How Humans Learn

author.name: nimakeivan

entry.summary: An essay arguing that frozen post-training parameters are the key blocker to on-the-job learning in LLMs, distinguishing memorization via context or retrieval from genuine skill acquisition, and drawing on human learning of tacit knowledge to sketch what continual learning would need to look like. It also frames the economic cost of centralized, identical models for every firm.

entry.title: Towards Sustainable Learning in Online Education: A Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Chaofan Zhai, Yicheng Song, Ravi Bapna, Junyao Ye

entry.summary: Presents an RL-based AI tutor that jointly optimizes short-term learning through a balance of new and review content and long-term outcomes by modeling engagement and dropout risk. Aims at sustainable learning in large-scale online education settings.

entry.title: AgonAlpha: Autonomous Alpha Discovery via Prompt Economy and Scalable Agentic Search

author.name: Weicheng Ye, Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Shunyao Yu, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: AgonAlpha is an agentic quantitative-finance system that searches over frozen research artifacts such as hypotheses, executable expressions, and review status rather than formulas alone, with an adversarial reviewer holding veto power and budget-aware parallel evaluation. Reports high-grade alphas produced on the WorldQuant BRAIN platform with a public evidence trail.

entry.title: Variable Selection in the Context of AI Fairness

author.name: Ivan Luciano Danesi, Chiara Frigerio, Fabio Maccaferri, Giorgio Alessandro Motta, Pietro Zecca

entry.summary: Argues that variable selection itself is a hidden source of unfairness in machine learning pipelines and sketches a mathematical framework that keeps potentially relevant variables to permit finer-grained subgroup fairness analysis, tied to regulatory expectations such as the EU AI Act. The paper is largely conceptual and advocates interdisciplinary work bridging ethics and statistics.

entry.title: Clinical Feasibility of Low-Magnification Fluorescence Imaging for Breast Cancer Margin Detection Using Texture Analysis and Deep Learning

author.name: Pouya Afshin, Tianling Niu, Tongtong Lu, David Helminiak, Julie Jorns, Mollie Patton, Tina Yen, Donghye Ye, Bing Yu

entry.summary: Compares 4x and 10x magnification fluorescence microscopy images of unprocessed surgical breast tissue for intraoperative margin assessment using both local binary pattern texture features and a vision transformer classifier. Lower magnification performs comparably, suggesting faster whole-specimen imaging may be clinically feasible.

entry.title: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement

author.name: Karim Aly, Alexei Sharpanskykh, Jacco Hoekstra

entry.summary: TailBooster generates synthetic tabular records for rare extreme events in air transport, layering two anomaly-detection stages on a generative model to both enrich distributional tails and reject operationally impossible records. Aimed at training data for delay and air-time prediction where extremes are scarce.

entry.title: Certifying What Helps Customer-Return Timing: A Screen-and-Confirm Test for Conditioning Signals, and Why Decay Is Nearly Enough

author.name: Sang Su Lee, Vineeth Loganathan, Shishir Dash, Vijay Raghavan

entry.summary: Proposes a screen-and-confirm protocol with planted positive controls to certify whether candidate covariates actually improve event-timing likelihood in temporal point process models of customer return. The finding is that simple decay dynamics capture nearly all the signal, so conditioning features add little.

entry.title: Benchmarking Cyberattack Detection in Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure with Benign User Updates

author.name: Hannan Chen, Roshni Anna Jacob, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Builds a leakage-controlled session-level benchmark for detecting cyberattacks on electric vehicle charging infrastructure, explicitly modeling legitimate post-activation revisions to requested energy and departure time as benign behavior. Twenty-two model families are compared across six physically motivated attack types and coordinated variants.

entry.title: Stigma and Support in Online Sexual Violence Narratives on Reddit

author.name: Shirlene Rose Bandela, Karan Bindal, Vaibhav Garg, Rezvaneh Rezapour

entry.summary: Introduces SCOPE, a Reddit dataset linking multi-dimensional stigma signals in sexual violence survivor narratives to the types of social support received in reply threads, annotated with experienced, internalized, anticipated, and structural stigma plus five support categories. Enables study of how disclosure framing shapes community response. Computational social science contribution with sensitive-data considerations.

entry.title: Predicting Functions, Not Features: KANs with Function-Space Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yungeng Liu, Xuanzi Fang, Yuge Zhang, Shuqi Ren, Haijin Zeng, Yongyong Chen

entry.summary: FS-JEPA moves joint-embedding predictive learning into the pre-aggregation function space of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks, having a masked online branch predict signatures of sampled edge functions produced by an EMA target branch. Provides explicit learning targets for individual univariate edge functions in KAN-based medical segmentation.

entry.title: Measuring Browser Webcam Gaze Honestly: A Capture-Clock Methodology and Open Reference Implementation

author.name: Chi-Sheng Chen, Gabriel A. Brat

entry.summary: Shows that browser webcam gaze trackers report near-zero inference latency because samples are timestamped when emitted rather than when the source frame was captured, and provides a capture-clock methodology using the requestVideoFrameCallback API plus an open reference implementation. Matters for crowd-scale and clinical eye-tracking studies that rely on such latency claims.

entry.title: Distribird: Literature-Informed Prior Distribution Design for Bayesian Model Calibration

author.name: Patrik P. S\"uli, Gy\"orgy Eigner, Roland Holl\'os

entry.summary: Distribird is an agentic web tool that builds informative Bayesian priors by searching scientific literature, extracting and weighting reported parameter values, and fitting distributions via AIC selection. It targets a real bottleneck in process-based model calibration where practitioners default to uniform priors.

entry.title: From Numbers to Judgment: Specialist LLM Agents and Reinforcement Learning for European Listed Real Estate

author.name: Pardis Taghavi, Santosh Bhavani

entry.summary: Tests whether decomposing European listed real-estate analysis into eight lens-aligned specialist LLM agents beats a monolithic prompt while holding model, evidence, and scoring fixed. Finds decomposition improves numerical tasks by about 16 points but does not reliably help and can hurt integrative judgment tasks.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Distributed CNC Tool Wear Prediction

author.name: Afsana Khan, Morris Stallmann, Marcin Pietrasik, Charis Kouzinopoulos, Anna Wilbik

entry.summary: Evaluates federated learning for CNC machine tool wear prediction, distributing tool trajectories across simulated clients to model the case where manufacturers cannot share raw operational data. Federated models are compared against centralized and local baselines to test whether privacy-preserving collaboration is competitive.

entry.title: Two-Stage Deformable-Convolutional Inverse Design of Nanophotonic Absorbers from Optical Spectra

author.name: Waleed Waseer, Muhammad Shahid Jabbar, Muhammad Sohail Ibrahim, Shujaat Khan

entry.summary: A two-stage deformable-convolution network reconstructs metal-insulator-metal nanophotonic resonator geometries from 80-dimensional absorption spectra, combining supervised reconstruction with adversarial refinement. Ablations compare deformable convolution against several alternative operators.

entry.title: M-Net: Integrating Spectral Features and Physical Field Operators into Deep Learning for Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Jing Zhu, Ye Wang, Fumin Wang

entry.summary: M-Net adds explicit mathematical inductive biases to a U-Net for medical image segmentation, including spectral condition-number features of local pixel matrices and divergence and curl-like field operators. Tests whether such priors improve on purely data-driven learning.

entry.title: Click2Poly: A VLM for vector mapping buildings and walls

author.name: Nicolas Girard, Jawher Ben Abdallah, Arno Gobbin, Liuyun Duan, Sacha Lepretre

entry.summary: Click2Poly extends the Florence-2 vision-language model into a click-driven assistant that edits building and wall vector layers directly, deployed as a QGIS plugin. It targets the human quality-control step that still dominates cartographic production pipelines. The contribution is applied tooling rather than new modeling.

entry.title: FunnelCausalNet: Funnel-aware Joint Conversion-Revenue Uplift for Multi-tier Coupon Allocation

author.name: Yu Zhang (AMap Alibaba Group, Beijing, China), Zhihan Wang (AMap Alibaba Group, Beijing, China), Guanlin Chen (AMap Alibaba Group, Beijing, China), Min Jiang (AMap Alibaba Group, Beijing, China), Shuai Li (AMap Alibaba Group, Beijing, China)

entry.summary: FunnelCausalNet estimates coupon uplift by factorizing gross merchandise value into a conversion probability head times a conditional order-value head, matching the deterministic funnel structure of zero-inflated heavy-tailed revenue. It adds conformal CATE summaries and is developed on Alibaba AMap data.

entry.title: Temperature-Driven Sequential Modeling for the Prediction of Annual Power Conversion Efficiency Profiles of Organic Photovoltaic Materials: Douala Case Study

author.name: Steve Cabrel Teguia Kouam, Rockefeller Rockefeller, Raoult Dabou Teukam, Jean-Pierre Tchapet Njafa, Patrick Sorrel Mvoto Kongo, Jean-Pierre Nguenang, Serge Guy Nana Engo

entry.summary: Combines semi-empirical molecular dynamics with an equivariant GNN surrogate to forecast annual power conversion efficiency profiles of organic photovoltaic donors under realistic tropical operating temperatures rather than standard test conditions.
