author.name: Ghanshyam Verma, Simanta Sarkar, Devishree Pillai, Hotaka Shiokawa, Yourong Xu, Fiona Veazey, Peter Hubbert, Hui Su, Paul Buitelaar

entry.summary: KGCaRe answers complex conditional questions by building a knowledge graph from documents with a multi-prompt extraction strategy, storing it in a graph database, and combining symbolic graph reasoning with vector retrieval. The claim is that hybrid structured plus unstructured evidence improves accuracy and explainability over plain retrieval-augmented generation.

entry.title: Instability of LLM Pre-Pretraining: It Doesn't Always Help. An Investigation on Multiple Languages

author.name: Sofiia Riazhskykh, Nam Luu, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar

entry.summary: Attempts to replicate the claim that pretraining on artificial languages before real data improves token efficiency, extending the test to multiple natural languages across four language families, two tokenizers, and several model sizes. Finds the reported gains are highly setup-dependent and relates outcomes to quantified linguistic properties such as morphological richness and dependency tree features.

entry.title: EmoS: A Theory-Grounded Framework for Evaluating and Aligning Emotional Intelligence in Spoken Language Models

author.name: Junyu Wang, Siyuan Zhang, Peiyuan Jiang, Jian Zong, Jingyu Zhang, Tianrui Wang, Yuqin Lin, Zhenghui Chen, Shuqing Xie, Ziyang Ma, Meng Ge, Xiaobao Wang, Longbiao Wang, Jianwu Dang

entry.summary: Introduces an emotional intelligence benchmark for spoken language models organized around a four-branch psychological theory covering perceiving, understanding, using, and managing emotion across ten sub-tasks, plus a specialized evaluator model. Reports that a leading proprietary audio model reaches only about half the score, far below human baselines.

entry.title: Is the ACL Responsible NLP Checklist a Box-Ticking Exercise? A Large-Scale Analysis of EMNLP 2025

author.name: Nusrath Jinnath, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: Curates and releases the full set of responsible research checklist responses and justifications from a major NLP conference plus links from checklist items to paper sections, then analyzes nearly 74,000 responses. Finds that authors tend to isolate ethics answers from the substance of their papers, suggesting compliance-oriented rather than integrated responsible practice.

entry.title: NewtonGS: Physics-Structured Object-Level Neural Newtonian Dynamics for Gaussian Scene Animation

author.name: Lianlei Shan, Feiyang Ye, Yan Chen, Yong Wu

entry.summary: NewtonGS gives each object in a Gaussian splatting scene a compact 22-dimensional physical state covering pose, velocities, scale dynamics, mass, and contact properties, then rolls it forward with a learned Newtonian dynamics model. This enables controllable object-level animation rather than only reconstructing time-varying scenes.

entry.title: BRUCE: Benchmarking Robustness Under Corruption Escalation for Scientific Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: BRUCE stress-tests scientific vision-language reasoning under escalating image corruptions such as blur and low contrast, introducing metrics that quantify how reasoning stability degrades rather than only clean accuracy. It aims to expose fragility that standard benchmarks hide.

entry.title: DINO-3DRA: Leveraging 2D Foundation Model Semantics for 3D Cerebral Aneurysm Segmentation

author.name: Jiayang Lu, Fengming Lin, Alejandro F. Frangi, Ali Sarrami-Foroushani

entry.summary: DINO-3DRA injects frozen 2D DINOv3 features into a 3D U-Net for cerebral aneurysm segmentation in rotational angiography, using spatial mixing and calibrated residual fusion to avoid the discontinuities of naive slice-wise transfer. It reports a substantial Dice improvement over nnU-Net with under six million trainable parameters.

entry.title: SeqLoc: Beyond the Single Frame for Cross-View Geo-Localization in Feature-Sparse Scenes

author.name: Junwei Zheng, Yun Huang, Ruize Dai, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Kunyu Peng, Kailun Yang, Jiaming Zhang, Guangming Wang, Olaf Wysocki, Rainer Stiefelhagen

entry.summary: SeqLoc addresses cross-view geo-localization failure in feature-sparse rural scenes by aggregating a sequence of panoramas into a recursively updated log-belief volume, with entropy-based tempering and a map-guided recovery mechanism. It also releases CV-FSS, a benchmark of sequential rural panoramas aligned to OpenStreetMap.

entry.title: How Much Does It Cost to Answer My Question? Benchmarking Cloud VLM-based VQA Systems

author.name: Henri Vanhuynegem, Weitao Xu, Yiran Shen, Guohao Lan

entry.summary: This benchmark quantifies how client-side image preprocessing choices affect answer quality, payload size, token cost, and latency when mobile visual question answering offloads to cloud vision-language APIs. It treats preprocessing as the main tunable variable given opaque proprietary serving stacks.

entry.title: SynVAR: Synergizing Spatial and Semantic Alignment in Visual Autoregressive Model

author.name: Zhennan Chen, Tianxing Shi, Pengcheng Xu, Kepan Nan, Qian Wang, Zili Yi, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: SynVAR is a training-free enhancement framework for visual autoregressive generation that targets cross-scale error propagation in the next-scale prediction paradigm. It combines early global guidance for spatial structure with receptive-field and semantic alignment controls to suppress accumulated errors in complex multi-object scenes.

entry.title: LIBAD: A Multimodal Anomaly Detection Benchmark for Li-Ion Battery Electrode Manufacturing

author.name: Wenbo Sui, Daniel Lichau, Harold Phelippeau, Zhao Liu

entry.summary: LIBAD is a multimodal anomaly detection benchmark for lithium-ion battery electrode manufacturing collected from real roll-to-roll production, pairing double-sided visible imaging with high- and low-resolution X-ray radiography. It targets continuous-process manufacturing and weakly correlated modalities where defect evidence may appear in only one channel.

entry.title: ZOMP: Zeroth-Order Multi-Modal Prompt Tuning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sajjad Ghiasvand, Yifan Yang, Mahnoosh Alizadeh, Ramtin Pedarsani

entry.summary: ZOMP tunes deep prompts in both the vision and text branches of a frozen CLIP model using simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation, requiring only forward passes. This targets settings such as memory-limited edge devices and closed proprietary APIs where backpropagation is unavailable.

entry.title: Robotic Fabric Alignment System for Sewing Using Global Local Weighted ICP

author.name: Wenbo Dong, Dipankar Bhattacharya Member, Kai Tang, Akinari Kobayashi, Fuyuki Tokuda, Akira Seino, Norman C. Tien, Kazuhiro Kosuge

entry.summary: HarnessWAM wraps world action models in an agentic scaffold where a vision-language-model task manager maintains an evidence-grounded scene belief and a structured task graph, and a capability-conditioned projection constrains open-ended semantic plans to sequences the underlying policy can actually execute. It targets what the authors call the prediction-deliberation gap, where finite-horizon prediction cannot support global planning, verification, and failure recovery.

entry.title: Emotion in an active inference model of human driving

author.name: Julian F. Schumann, Johan Engstr\"om, Ran Wei, Jens Kober, Martijn Wisse, Arkady Zgonnikov

entry.summary: Extends active inference models of human driving to include affective state, representing emotion along valence and arousal axes in continuous rather than discrete state spaces. The goal is a principled cognitive model that captures how emotion shapes traffic decision-making.

entry.title: Towards Researcher Agents for Knowledge-Graph Question Answering

author.name: Tommaso Soru, Abdulsobur Oyewale

entry.summary: Builds a text-to-SPARQL agent that, after each validation round, proposes and tests modifications to its own prompts, rules, and tool-orchestration code. Nine successive self-evolved versions were produced on DBpedia using a cheap reasoning model, with the best configuration then deployed on stronger backbones.

entry.title: Directed Neuro-Symbolic Stochastic Execution for Verification of Distributed Parallel AI Programs

author.name: Gautham Koorma, Vikas Sharma, George Edwards, Mahdi Eslamimehr

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid testing framework for distributed parallel AI programs that couples LLM-guided prediction of concurrency schedules with symbolic constraint solving and coverage-guided stochastic mutation. Correctness is specified in linear temporal logic with proofs of soundness, bounded completeness, and probabilistic completeness.

entry.title: PATH: Next-Interval Prediction via Autoregressive Tree Hierarchy on Tabular Data

author.name: Pengxiang Cai, Wanchen Lian, Chenyang Liu, Xiaohan Li, Qingyuan Zeng, Jinhong Wang, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: Reframes conformal interval prediction as an autoregressive next-interval task, exploiting the observation that prediction intervals have a nested hierarchical geometry naturally represented by binary trees. The method learns how probability mass flows through the tree rather than relying on post-hoc calibration rules applied to an uncertainty surrogate.

entry.title: Metanormative Theory for RL-Based Moral Agents

author.name: Aleks Knoks, Marija Slavkovik

entry.summary: A philosophy-informed analysis arguing that recent reinforcement learning approaches to machine ethics ignore metanormative theory, which handles uncertainty about which moral theory is correct. The authors translate those ideas into criteria for when an RL agent can be called moral and where standard RL architectures fall short. It is conceptual bridge-building between value alignment engineering and normative ethics.

entry.title: Hierarchical Self-Improvement: A Framework for Task-Specific Evolvable Agent Harnesses

author.name: Tailin Zhou

entry.summary: This framework makes the executable scaffold around a frozen model, the harness, into a continuously evolving artifact specialized per task family, rewritten from environment feedback by an evolver that is itself rewritten by a meta-evolver. All three levels share one frozen model, so improvement comes from code and workflow evolution rather than weight updates. It probes how far self-improvement can go without training.

entry.title: MedCalc-R1: Knowledge-Guided Reward Framework for Medical Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haotian Wang, Lian Yan, Xingzhi Yao, Fanshu Meng, Ye He, Jingchi Jiang, Yi Guan

entry.summary: MedCalc-R1 replaces brittle tolerance-based numeric rewards in medical calculation tasks with a knowledge-guided hybrid reward that forces explicit generation of the computational formula, verified externally, combined with soft and hard scoring components. This stabilizes reinforcement learning and improves interpretability for clinical arithmetic. Addresses a real reward-design pain point in verifiable-reward training.

entry.title: UniMoMo: Expert Merging-Based MoE Acceleration for Large Recommendation Models

author.name: Lei Xin, Bin Gu, Peize Li, Zitong Wang, Jianbo Zhao, Changjiang Jiang, Yanyue Xie, Chao Huang, Xuyang Zhao, Zunhai Su, Fanhu Zeng, Zhenglun Kong

entry.summary: UniMoMo compresses a trained sparse mixture-of-experts recommendation model into a smaller standard MoE under an explicit expert budget, formulated as constrained graph coarsening that groups experts by functional similarity measured on unlabeled calibration data rather than parameter distance. A layer-adaptive scheme prevents degradation. It targets deployment cost for large industrial recommenders without extra online modules.

entry.title: SkillReason: Reasoning-Enhanced Agent Skill Retrieval for Implicit User Requests

author.name: Donghong Jiang, Endian Lin, Luoping Cui, Hanqing Liu, Mingjie Liu, Fan Yang, Hong Wang, Zhao Yang, Chuang Zhu

entry.summary: SkillReason tackles retrieval of the right agent skill when user requests are short and leave required capabilities implicit, releasing a benchmark of 3,729 queries against a corpus of over 61,000 skills across nine domains. Its two-stage method uses chain-of-thought reasoning as training-time supervision to bridge terse goals to capability descriptions. Skill retrieval is becoming a bottleneck as skill libraries grow large.

entry.title: AI Evaluation Should Measure Verification Cost, Not Correctness Alone

author.name: Viviana Crescitelli, Generoso Immediato, Fabio Persia, Stefania Costantini

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that AI evaluation should measure the cost of verifying outputs, not just correctness, introducing verification-cost errors defined as wrong outputs that a stated fraction of verifiers fail to catch within a realistic budget. The definition is operational and deployment-relative rather than a property of the text itself. It reframes hallucination measurement around human oversight economics.

entry.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

author.name: Juncheng Dong, Ding Tong, Ishan Gupta, Yuyan Wang

entry.summary: The first edition of a shared challenge benchmarking whether AI systems can adapt an instructional video to a specified learner persona, an ability education research calls pedagogical content knowledge. Submissions are screened by an LLM judge, ranked by crowd pairwise voting and finalized by an expert panel. Results indicate systems handle subject content well but adapt presentation to the learner poorly.

entry.title: CRUISE: Vision-Language Model-Guided Uncertainty-Aware Cross-Modal Sensor Fusion for Robust Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junyao Wang, Yulin Xu, Yu Li, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: CRUISE uses a vision-language model to guide uncertainty-aware fusion of camera, LiDAR, and radar features for autonomous driving, aiming to weight sensors sensibly under adverse weather and out-of-distribution conditions where naive feature-level uncertainty estimates fail. Reports improved robustness in degraded-perception scenarios.

entry.title: OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks

author.name: Siqi Wang, Xinlin Li, Zhenglin Li, Li Li

entry.summary: OpenLoopEvolve represents an agent's observation, planning, memory, verification, recovery, stopping, and budget behaviors as versioned portable policy assets that can be evolved online during a run or offline across traces. Aims to make long-horizon control experience accumulable rather than trapped in a single context.

entry.title: Adaptive Semantic Capacity Allocation for Parallel Generative Recommendation

author.name: Chenxi Li, Yuchen Lu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: Shows that uniformly expanding semantic identifier slots in parallel generative recommenders yields limited gains, indicating redundant capacity, and proposes adaptive allocation of the number of slots and per-slot codebook size according to the heterogeneous demands of different semantic subspaces. Enables longer identifiers without expensive beam-search decoding.

entry.title: WuYuEval: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Large Language Models in Solid Waste Management

author.name: Yi Zhang, Hongyang Wang, Zheng Hao Leong, Zihao Wu, Kaijun Lin, Zhixing Pan, Qixun Huangfu, Wei Ren, Wenyan Wu, Fangyun Wang, Wenting Yu, Hengyu Lin, Muling Yang, Zongguo Wen

entry.summary: WuYuEval is a multi-level benchmark for solid waste management expertise, with roughly 4,590 multiple-choice foundation items and 247 expert scenario questions involving multi-objective optimization and constraint tradeoffs. Targets professional engineering and policy decision competence rather than general knowledge.

entry.title: Coarse-to-Fine Registration of Jawbone CT and Intraoral Scan Data Using GeDi and ICP with Pseudo-IOS Ground Truth

author.name: Sho Mitarai, Hikaru Kayo, Hisashi Ozaki, Yuichiro Imai, Megumi Nakao

entry.summary: Proposes a pseudo intraoral scan evaluation framework where a surface point cloud is synthesized from CT in the same coordinate frame so the true registration transform is known, enabling rigorous accuracy measurement. Uses a coarse-to-fine pipeline combining learned GeDi descriptors with ICP refinement.

entry.title: Defending Retrieval-Augmented Intrusion Detection Against Knowledge Poisoning and Prompt Injection

author.name: Kaysarul Anas Apurba, Md. Hasibul Hasan, Mahedee Zaman Moon, Sk. Md. Mizanur Rahman, Atsuo Inomata

entry.summary: Presents a multi-agent retrieval-augmented intrusion detection system hardened against knowledge poisoning and prompt injection in its vector store, using trust scoring, label-embedding consistency checks and prompt sanitization. Reports partial recovery of clean performance up to thirty percent poisoning rates on a standard network intrusion dataset.

entry.title: Can We Optimize the Performance-Carbon Emission Break-Even Point?: The Quest for Greener LLMs

author.name: Sourav Das, Tanmay Joshi, Kripabandhu Ghosh

entry.summary: Folds a calibrated differentiable energy surrogate, fit from on-hardware profiling, into the fine-tuning loss to search for configurations where task accuracy improves at near-zero additional carbon cost during inference. Tests three architecturally distinct small model families.

entry.title: Fourier Self-Supervision for Fine-Grained Generalized Category Discovery

author.name: Sarah Rastegar, Mina Ghadimi Atigh, Pascal Mettes, Yuki M. Asano, Cees G. M. Snoek

entry.summary: Adds Fourier-domain self-supervision to generalized category discovery, using low-pass filtering to capture coarse category structure and high-pass filtering to sharpen fine-grained distinctions. Aims to stop contrastive discovery methods from latching onto superficial visual cues.

entry.title: Tabular Numeric Stretch Transformation

author.name: Zihao Ye, Juyong Kim, Johnna Sundberg, Burak Varici, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: Formulates numeric feature preprocessing for tabular deep learning as an optimization that stretches feature distributions to make the target function smoother and easier to learn, with unsupervised minimax and supervised target-aware variants. Positions preprocessing rather than architecture as the underexplored lever.

entry.title: SiriusDeliver: Automating Data Warehouse Delivery at Tencent

author.name: Haining Xie, Xiaokai Zhou, Jiaming Yang, Siqi Shen, Ziwei Wang, Yifeng Zheng, Tengyue Xu, Yipeng Shi, Zefang Zong, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang, Debiao He, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: SiriusDeliver is a production agent deployed at Tencent that automates enterprise data-warehouse task delivery, covering context retrieval, workflow configuration, code generation, submission, and failure diagnosis. It adds dependency-aware orchestration and lifecycle-aware artifact control that generic coding agents lack.

entry.title: RecoverFly: A Failure-Aware Reinforcement Learning Post-Training Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Boxiong Wang, Hui Kang, Geng Sun, Jiahui Li, Chao Yu, Daxin Tian

entry.summary: RecoverFly post-trains UAV vision-language navigation policies with failure-aware reinforcement learning to add the corrective supervision that behavior cloning cannot provide for closed-loop flight. Targets sample inefficiency, long-tailed scene distributions, and distribution shift during optimization.

entry.title: From Semantic Grounding to Decision Optimization: A Unified Framework for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Zeyuan Ma, Jiaxin Chen, Di Huang

entry.summary: A framework for drone vision-language navigation that adds object-level semantic grounding to observations, aggregates long-horizon history with a relevance-weighted temporal module, and stabilizes action choice to escape local traps and repeated exploration. It targets three coupled failure modes in aerial instruction following.

entry.title: LEED: Local Embedding Evolution Distance for over-smoothing estimation and virtual node selection in GNN

author.name: Killian Cressant, Pedro B. Velloso

entry.summary: LEED is a per-node metric that tracks how individual graph node embeddings change layer by layer, giving finer resolution on over-smoothing than global measures such as Dirichlet energy. The metric is then used to pick where to insert virtual nodes to relieve over-squashing.

entry.title: PhysAttNet: Enhancing Predictive Performance in Industrial and Astrophysical Time Series via Physics-Informed Attention

author.name: Amal Saadallah, Julia Tjus, Petra Wiederkeher, Wolfgang Rhode

entry.summary: PhysAttNet adds physics-informed attention to convolutional time-series forecasters so that learned temporal attention aligns with physically meaningful events rather than drifting into unstable patterns. It targets industrial monitoring and astrophysical event detection under noise and measurement uncertainty.

entry.title: CONFER: Conflict-Aware Evidence Negotiation for Regime-Calibrated Weak Supervision in Multimodal Emotion Recognition

author.name: Bojing Hou, Ruohao Li, Yitong Zhu, Luwen Yu, Yuyang Wang

entry.summary: CONFER treats multimodal emotion recognition as negotiation among modality experts represented as graph nodes carrying beliefs, uncertainty, and runtime reliability, instead of trusting self-reported labels as ground truth. Message passing weighted by compatibility and reliability resolves cross-modal conflict before a peer-supported prediction readout.

entry.title: From Uncertainty to Failure Attribution: Self-Diagnosing Models for Failure Attribution under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yiyao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces the task of failure attribution under distribution shift, going beyond detecting out-of-distribution inputs to explaining why a prediction is unreliable. The proposed self-diagnosing model jointly outputs a prediction, an uncertainty estimate, and a structured failure-attribution vector distinguishing several unreliability types.

entry.title: Predicting blood clot growth from sparse post-onset measurements with latent neural differential equations

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman, Ying Qian, He Li

entry.summary: Uses latent neural differential equations to infer unmeasurable parameters of a multiphysics blood-clotting model from a few biochemical inputs plus sparse early clot-size measurements, then forecasts thrombus progression. The framework is demonstrated on simulated data from a coagulation-and-diffusion model.

entry.title: Constrained Learning with Universally Learnable Concept Classes

author.name: Herlock SeyedAbolfazl Rahimi, Spyridon Pougkakiotis, Dionysis Kalogerias

entry.summary: Establishes universal PACC learnability, meaning probably approximately correct guarantees on both objective optimality and constraint satisfaction, for dual algorithms over infinite-dimensional nonconvex hypothesis classes. The authors reconcile generalization requirements with strong Lagrangian duality by posing the population problem over a universal reproducing-kernel Hilbert space.

entry.title: No Unique Minimizer, No Problem: On the Consistency of Robust Neural Classifiers

author.name: Subhabrata Majumdar, Anand Deo, Partha Pratim Saha, Abhik Ghosh

entry.summary: Develops a consistency theory for robust neural classifiers trained with S-divergence losses that does not assume parameter identifiability, treating the population minimizer as an equivalence class. Proves empirical minimizers converge to the population solution set under stochastic optimization over non-identifiable parameter spaces.

entry.title: Task-to-Model Optimization for Enterprise LLM Coding Assistants: A Data-Driven Framework for Cost-Optimal Routing

author.name: Srinivasan Manoharan, Junhua Zhao, Fangbo Tu, Haifeng Wu, Jian Wan, Maliah Rajan M, Ashwin Hegde, Mithun Sasidharan, Kalyan Chakravarthi Podamekala

entry.summary: Presents a nine-stage enterprise methodology for routing coding-assistant requests to the cheapest model that meets quality and latency constraints, covering telemetry, task taxonomy discovery, difficulty grading and production-like benchmarking. Argues that naive token-price minimization backfires once retries, escalations and developer waiting time are counted.

entry.title: Memory-Efficient Activation Checkpointing with Sliding Window and Hirschberg's Algorithm for 0/1 Knapsack Solving in PyTorch

author.name: J\k{e}drzej Maczan

entry.summary: Replaces PyTorch's full dynamic programming table for activation checkpointing selection with a sliding-window plus Hirschberg divide-and-conquer solver for the underlying 0/1 knapsack problem. This removes the memory blowup that crashes the default solver at around one hundred items on a 64 GB machine.

entry.title: Math-Vision Diagrams: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Mathematical Diagram Generation Capabilities

author.name: Harish Kashyap, Kiran Byadarhaly, Sriram Chakaravarthy, Sanyukta Tuti, Aryan Mistry

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of paired prompts and reference images specifically for evaluating whether language models can generate mathematically precise diagrams, a capability that requires joint spatial reasoning, mathematical reasoning and rendering. Argues existing math and diagram benchmarks do not cover this intersection.

entry.title: From Approachability Residuals to Anytime-Valid Evidence: The Online Convex Geometry of Testing by Betting

author.name: Jinze Zhao

entry.summary: Establishes an exact pathwise identity linking Blackwell approachability distance to the average of support-function residuals plus online-learning regret, then composes it with betting-based sequential testing. The result is a finite-time transfer where an explicit target gap forces rejection by a given time and non-rejection certifies convergence.

entry.title: ReliableNet: A Chance-Constrained Approach to Trustworthy Classification in Deep Learning

author.name: Ange-Cl\'ement Akazan, Ineza Remy Mugenga, Abebe Geletu, Jean Medard Ngnotchouye, Issa Karambal

entry.summary: ReliableNet reformulates training to directly bound the probability that a model is simultaneously confident and wrong, treating this joint event as the reliability failure that defeats abstention and human review. The authors cast it as chance-constrained empirical risk minimization with a smooth conservative surrogate.

entry.title: RouteGuard: Certifying Routing Gain in LLM Multi-Agent Systems When Complementarity Is Not Enough

author.name: Anchen Sun, Kaiqi Yang

entry.summary: RouteGuard argues that neither gate AUC nor advisor complementarity determines whether routing among LLM advisors actually helps in deployment, decomposing routing gain and governing it by a conditional-regret functional. It supplies a finite-sample certification bracket with a matching lower bound and reports guardrail verdicts on router benchmarks.

entry.title: A Distribution Mapping Approach to Counterfactually Fair Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianhan Zhang, Jitao Wang, John D. Piette, Donglin Zeng, Chengchun Shi, Zhenke Wu

entry.summary: Develops a data preprocessing algorithm that enables counterfactually fair reinforcement learning by mapping counterfactual states and rewards through quantile distribution matching before policy learning. The motivation is high-stakes sequential decisions in healthcare that could systematically restrict some subpopulations' access to services.

entry.title: Multitask Scanning Probe Microscopy

author.name: Aditya Raghavan, Yu Liu, Ian Mercer, JP Maria, Sergei Kalinin

entry.summary: Demonstrates a closed-loop autonomous microscopy workflow where a multitask Gaussian process learns spatial and cross-modal correlations and chooses both the next location and the next measurement modality. This addresses the practical problem that different probe modalities have very different acquisition costs and damage risks, making exhaustive multimodal mapping infeasible.

entry.title: Did the Grid Erase the Event? EndoClock for Auditing Medical World-Model Pipelines

author.name: Yarin Udi, Tom Sharon-Shahak, Roee Masad, Dan Pri-Tal

entry.summary: Argues that resampling multimodal medical recordings onto a fixed-rate grid can destroy the evidence needed to detect a clinical event when the observation clock itself depends on latent or acquisition state. Contributes a four-regime taxonomy of where the diagnostic witness survives and an auditing tool for medical world-model preprocessing pipelines.

entry.title: Position Bias in Ordinal Classification: A Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Yu Wang, Jeffrey Zhou, Menglin Liu, Ge Shi

entry.summary: Systematically characterizes how label order, demonstration order, and demonstration placement shift LLM predictions on ordinal classification, testing ten frontier models plus eight prompt, task, and model factors across five datasets. Finds all models sensitive to all three positional sources, accuracy and stability frequently misaligned, and only lower rating-scale cardinality reliably improving both.

entry.title: PhysX-CoT: Structured Physical Reasoning from a Single Image to Simulation-Ready 3D Assets

author.name: Jie Huang, Xiaohe Li, Jiahao Li, Fangli Mou, Chen Qian, Yuqiang Fang, Junhao Fan, Kaixin Zhang, Zide Fan

entry.summary: PhysX-CoT turns single-image generation of simulation-ready 3D assets into an explicit, machine-parseable chain of physical reasoning steps covering part decomposition, 2D and 3D grounding, relations and physical properties. Exposing intermediate states allows supervision, conditioning and verification instead of emitting one opaque serialized asset.

entry.title: Stochastic Physics-Informed Neural Networks on Lie Groups for Learning Underwater Vehicle Dynamics

author.name: Evan F. Palmer, Ross L. Hatton, Geoffrey A. Hollinger

entry.summary: Learns stochastic underwater vehicle dynamics with a physics-informed neural network built on Euler-Poincare mechanics and Lie group geometry, using structure-preserving stochastic integration plus moment and finite-dimensional matching for geometrically consistent training. The approach targets marine autonomy tasks where analytic hydrodynamic models are unreliable.

entry.title: Rethink Before You Execute: Adaptive Execution for World Action Models

author.name: Feng Ye, Yiming Zhao, Yong Yu, Hongxu Zhou, Yong Pan, Yuan Xue, Peng Jia, Chuanmin Jia

entry.summary: TempoWAM replaces the fixed action-chunk execution prefix of world action models with an adaptive scheme: a recurrent progress monitor estimates task progress from observations, instruction, remaining actions, and execution history, and an adaptive protocol decides when to re-plan. The premise is that chunk reliability varies by task stage, so replanning should depend on accumulated execution outcomes rather than step counts.

entry.title: The Agentic Clusterfuck

author.name: Chapin Lenthall-Cleary

entry.summary: A forecasting piece arguing that once an open-weight agent can reliably cover its own inference costs while pursuing profit, economic incentives will drive mass proliferation, flooding the internet with automated schemes, scams, and cheap deniable capability for malicious actors. The author assigns roughly a third probability to something like this within a few years.

entry.title: The Field Knows: Cross-Dimensional Geometry from Navigation to Black Holes

author.name: Chenghao Xu

entry.summary: Learns a continuous metric field via a causal contrastive loss that maps scenes into Lie algebra coefficients exponentiated into Riemannian or Lorentzian metrics. The same framework reportedly recovers obstacle-avoiding geodesics in robot navigation and event horizons in black hole spacetimes with zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: QuantumMind: Constraint-Grounded Agentic Reasoning for Speedup Analysis in Quantum Computing

author.name: Yijing Zuo, Zhe Fu, Zihan Nie, Zhihui Zhu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Presents an auditable agentic workflow that generates and conservatively screens claims of quantum speedup, formalizing the task, checking access and output models, matching against a registry of quantum primitives and known barriers, and applying a deterministic ten-check validator. The output is a scoped, source-linked acceleration claim record.

entry.title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs

author.name: Nuthakki Siva Gopala Krishna, Kanishka Jain

entry.summary: Argues that knowledge distillation transfers not only capability but also behavioral traits such as how a model describes its own identity, and proposes an adversarial multi-agent framework to probe self-identity consistency in students versus teachers. Raises concerns about output homogeneity and accountability across distilled model families.

entry.title: Biologically Informed Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Center Generalization of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Alejandro L. Garc\'ia-Navarro, Carlos Sevilla-Salcedo, Bel\'en Rodr\'iguez-S\'anchez, Vanessa G\'omez-Verdejo

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic representation learning framework for MALDI-TOF mass spectra that jointly models acquisition-specific variability and biological supervision so models transfer across hospitals. Targets microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction under domain shift.

entry.title: TomaMMU: A Comprehensive Multimodal Understanding Benchmark for Tomato Leaf Diseases

author.name: Gia-Han Truong, Khang Nguyen Quoc, Luyl-Da Quach

entry.summary: Releases a large multimodal dataset of nearly twenty-nine thousand tomato leaf disease images with over two hundred thousand human-annotated question-answer pairs, plus a benchmark organizing seven agricultural tasks into perception, pathology understanding and expert diagnosis tiers. Enables systematic evaluation of vision-language models on agricultural diagnosis.

entry.title: SAFE-CHEM: Uncertainty-Aware Policy Switching for Robust Robotic Chemistry

author.name: Laura Jones, Shazil Shahzad, Ayesha Sana, Gabriella Pizzuto

entry.summary: Introduces an uncertainty-aware framework for learning-based robotic chemistry that uses an ensemble to detect when a learned manipulation policy is extrapolating and switches to a safer fallback policy. Targets the deployment barrier that overconfident policies can cause catastrophic failures in early-stage materials chemistry experiments.

entry.title: Listwise Cross-Encoder Fine-Tuning vs. Agentic Instruction Tuning for LLM Rerankers: A Systematic Study in Medical Procedure Reranking

author.name: Matan Fainzilber, Shlomit Plavner

entry.summary: A systematic comparison in medical procedure reranking finds that a 109M-parameter cross-encoder fine-tuned with a listwise objective outperforms a 4B instruction reranker whose prompts were optimized by an agentic loop. The setting is health insurance retrieval with a large lexical gap between patient and clinical language.

entry.title: LHSDet: High-Resolution AI-Generated Image Detection via Visual Question Answering

author.name: Qian Yao, Jun-Jie Huang, Yongjun Wang, Luming Yang

entry.summary: LHSDet detects AI-generated images at native high resolution by casting the task as visual question answering with a fine-tuned vision-language model, avoiding the downsampling that destroys low-level texture evidence. It aims to generalize to unseen generators without huge pretraining corpora.

entry.title: MRBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Human Motion-Text Retrieval

author.name: Fulong Liu, Liang Xu, Chengqun Yang, Yuhao Zhang, Yichao Yan, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: MRBench is a human motion-to-text retrieval benchmark built through a multi-stage curation pipeline that balances motion categories, verifies unambiguous alignment, and generates descriptions at several levels of granularity. It responds to prior benchmarks dominated by indoor motions and repetitive template-like captions.

entry.title: EvBS: Event-guided Blur Synthesis for Domain-adaptive Motion Deblurring

author.name: Junsik Jung, Seokryun Choi, Yoonki Cho, Woo Jae Kim, Andrew Jeong, Sung-Eui Yoon

entry.summary: EvBS synthesizes realistic blurred and sharp training pairs for the target domain by using event camera streams to separate motion from visual content. This lets the method transfer extrinsic motion from other sequences onto given content, generating more diverse calibration data for pretrained deblurring models.

entry.title: Test-Time Prototype Adaptation for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Haozhe Wang, Jintao Cheng, Weibin Li, Xiaoyu Tang

entry.summary: TPA is a training-free plug-in for open-vocabulary segmentation that adapts only at the output level, identifying confident anchor patches from a host CLIP model's own predictions on unlabeled data and refining prototypes transductively. It requires no changes to the host model's weights or forward pass.

entry.title: Tropical Cyclone Forecasting via Latent Rectified Flow using Satellite Imagery and Atmospheric Fields

author.name: Meheru Zannat, Sk. Md. Masudul Ahsan

entry.summary: A latent rectified flow model jointly forecasts infrared satellite imagery and four reanalysis atmospheric fields for tropical cyclones out to nine hours in a single pass, using a five-channel variational autoencoder. It contrasts with prior generative forecasters that produce either imagery or fields, require many sampling steps, and derive tracks from physically disconnected regression heads.

entry.title: Graph-Guided Safe Diffuser: Topological Graph Guidance for Safe Diffusion Planning

author.name: Nakgyu Yang, KwangBin Lee, SooJean Han

entry.summary: G2SD argues that inference-time safety guidance deforms diffusion-planner trajectories off the learned data manifold, and instead abstracts that manifold into a learned latent graph on which a high-level topological planner selects nodes that condition the diffusion model. Theory characterizes when manifold rupture occurs, with the hierarchy enforcing safety structurally.

entry.title: TRACE-Memory: Public-Conditioned Retrieval and Utility-Aware Evidence Admission for Personalized Generation

author.name: Jing Wang, Zhu Wang, Yifan Guo, Yulong Yang, Yunji Liang

entry.summary: TRACE-Memory argues that personal memory should be injected only when it adds value beyond what a public, non-personalized answer already provides. Its two stages first query for genuinely missing user-specific information and then admit a compact, traceable evidence subset, possibly the empty set, based on incremental response utility. This targets both over-personalization and unnecessary privacy exposure.

entry.title: MathShikkha: A Controlled Study of Answer-Only and Chain-of-Thought Supervision for Bangla Mathematical Reasoning in Small Language Models

author.name: Rahma Simin Ali, Jawad Hossain

entry.summary: A controlled study of Bangla mathematical reasoning finds that chain-of-thought supervision distilled from a strong teacher gives no significant in-domain gain over answer-only fine-tuning for three of four small student models, despite far longer outputs. The matched protocol holds data, loss masking, decoding and scoring fixed so only the training target varies. A useful negative result for low-resource reasoning distillation.

entry.title: EnergyBridge: Benchmarking Household Energy Management, User Participation, and Grid Flexibility

author.name: Xudong Wu, Zeqing Wu, Jiarui Zhang, Xuhao Fan, Ziang Ding, Yuming Zhuang, Mingqi Yuan, Yilun Du, Hongjie Jia, Yunfei Mu, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: EnergyBridge benchmarks household demand flexibility end to end by connecting capacity reporting, resident authorization of a specific event, and physical execution in building simulation environments for two cities, with an LLM-based simulator of user participation. Against hundreds of persona-matched human role-play judgments the simulator preserves method rankings with about a five point acceptance error. It highlights that physical flexibility only counts once humans consent.

entry.title: Context Is Not Authority: Structured Runtime Governance for Financial Market Agents

author.name: Rui Tang, Qiangqiang Liu, Yichi Zhang, Youwei Wang, Xi Chen, Chen Dong

entry.summary: Introduces SAGE-Fin, a runtime authority-handoff contract for financial agents that gates the actual effect of an action (a trade, a customer commitment, a deployed policy) rather than the text proposing it, tracking missing institutional obligations as coverage debt and requiring typed receipts matched to the consuming adapter. Prior authorizations are rechecked after state changes.

entry.title: PolicyKG: An Agentic LLM Pipeline for Translating Institutional Policies into SHACL Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Ponkrit Kaewsawee, Chaklam Silpasuwanchai, Chutiporn Anutariya

entry.summary: PolicyKG is an LLM pipeline that reads policy PDFs, labels sentences as obligation, permission, or prohibition, maps them to deontic logic, and emits machine-checkable SHACL constraints, coordinated by a LangGraph state machine with per-stage validators. A YAML vocabulary registry grounds predicates in a target ontology so retargeting needs no retraining.

entry.title: ChronoState: Hidden Elapsed-Time Conditioning for Temporal-State Action Selection in Frozen-Backbone Language Models

author.name: Sam Siavoshian, Omar Ramadan, Amir K. Saeed, Benjamin A. Johnson, Amin Mohamed El-Amin Diab, Benjamin M. Rodriguez

entry.summary: ChronoState tests whether elapsed wall-clock time can be injected into a frozen language model as a system-side scalar rather than as tokens, and composed with symbolic prompt state to pick correct time-dependent actions such as cache expiry or deadline handling. Introduces a small benchmark and evaluates with a frozen 3B backbone.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Uncertainty Propagation in First-Order Proof Search

author.name: Tanel Tammet

entry.summary: Extends the GK first-order theorem prover, which supports positive and negative claims, numeric confidences, and prioritized defaults with exceptions, by adding structure-preserving quantitative reporting derived from retained proof histories. Avoids requiring finite global grounding and flags incomplete searches as such.

entry.title: ASPaeroFlow: Decomposition Heuristics for Joint Air Traffic Flow & Capacity Management

author.name: Alexander Beiser, Markus Hecher, Nysret Musliu, Georg Trausmuth, Stefan Woltran

entry.summary: ASPaeroFlow jointly optimizes air traffic flow management and dynamic airspace configuration, which are usually treated separately with circular fixed-demand and fixed-capacity assumptions, by combining instance-space decomposition heuristics with local exact answer set programming. Benchmarked up to industry-scale instances.

entry.title: GeoPhysAdapter: Scale-Matched Geophysical Adaptation for Cross-Domain Landslide Mapping with Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Zhihang Liu, Mei-Po Kwan, Jinlin Wu, Hao Li

entry.summary: GeoPhysAdapter adapts a frozen vision foundation model for cross-region landslide mapping by injecting terrain, material, and rainfall-trigger information at their native spatial scales instead of resampling everything to a common grid, addressing scale mismatch that causes confident false alarms. Aimed at rapid post-event mapping without local labels.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Heuristic Design from Simulation Traces: A Case Study in Dynamic Production and AGV Scheduling

author.name: Jinbo Li, Chuanhao Li

entry.summary: Uses an LLM manager agent to read event-level simulation traces from the worst replication of a candidate scheduling heuristic, form bottleneck hypotheses, and dispatch editing agents that revise policy code in parallel, keeping only verified improvements. Applied to dynamic production and automated guided vehicle scheduling.

entry.title: ICM Out! Better Tournament Strategy from Computed Continuations, vs. Solvers and LLMs

author.name: Boning Li, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Replaces the Independent Chip Model for poker tournament strategy with Strategic-Continuation Optimization, which enumerates current-hand outcomes, maps them to successor tournament states, and prices those states with continuation values from the finite tournament model, capturing blind schedule, position, and elimination pressure that ICM ignores. Compared against solvers and LLMs.

entry.title: Adaptive Sequential Test Planning for Multi-Mechanism Reliability Qualification via Bayesian Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Youssef A. Elhagrasy, Ian Hill, Andr\'e Ivanov

entry.summary: Formulates semiconductor reliability qualification as a partially observable sequential decision problem and solves it with Monte Carlo tree search over a seed-action simulator coupled to extended Kalman filter belief estimation, adapting stress decisions to per-device degradation instead of using static population-level plans. Models competing failure mechanisms such as bias temperature instability.

entry.title: Coordinated incentives in AI-generated misinformation governance

author.name: Qin Li, Gui Zhang, Minyu Feng, Matjaz Perc, Attila Szolnoki

entry.summary: Models AI-generated misinformation governance as a three-party evolutionary game among a regulator, an AI enterprise, and users with heterogeneous rewards and punishments, deriving replicator equations and stability conditions for competing governance and content-production strategies. Concludes that neither regulation nor market incentives alone suffices and that coordinated incentive alignment is required for a stable truthful-content regime.

entry.title: Innovating with Generative AI: A Human Bottleneck Framework

author.name: Julian De Freitas, Ayelet Israeli, Gideon Nave, Artem Timoshenko, Olivier Toubia

entry.summary: Proposes a human bottleneck framework for how generative AI reshapes innovation, arguing that cognitive and social constraints across ideation, screening, preference measurement, and diffusion are unevenly relieved or worsened by AI. Authors are prominent marketing and business researchers.

entry.title: EMMR: Emotion-Mediated Multimodal Reasoning for Personality Assessment in Asynchronous Video Interviews

author.name: Dongsheng Hu, Tianyi Zhang, Chuang Liu, Yuan Zong Yong Li, Wenming Zheng, Xiu-xiu Zhan

entry.summary: EMMR is a two-stage multimodal framework that extracts emotion cues from video, audio, and text and uses them as mediating evidence for personality assessment in asynchronous video interviews. Argues text-only LLM approaches miss nonverbal signals relevant to traits.

entry.title: Tools to Explain Neural Networks for Power System Dynamics

author.name: Petros Ellinas, Johanna Vorwerk, Spyros Chatzivasileiadis

entry.summary: Applies Neural Tangent Kernel analysis to explain why machine-learning surrogates for power system dynamics train well or poorly, connecting learning behaviour to the modal and eigenvalue structure familiar from small-signal stability analysis. Aims to make surrogate models trustworthy enough for grid operators to adopt.

entry.title: SignLlama: Enhancing Gloss-free Sign Language Translation by Prioritizing Visual Features for LLMs

author.name: Shiwei Gan, Xiao Liu, Yafeng Yin, Zhiwei Jiang, Bowen Guo, Lie Xie, Sanglu Lu, Hongkai Wen

entry.summary: Analyzes why LLMs fine-tuned for gloss-free sign language translation underuse visual input, attributing it to a visual-text distribution gap and to autoregressive concatenation that biases models toward text tokens. SignLlama restructures the adaptation to prioritize visual features.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Semantics and Reconstruction:Unifying Sign Language Translation and Production

author.name: Xiao Liu, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Jiaxin Yin, Bowen Guo, Yaqi Sun, Zhiwei Jiang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Asks whether sign language understanding and production can be unified in one model, which is harder than unifying understanding subtasks because production inverts the mapping direction from text to sign. Proposes a framework bridging semantic recognition and motion reconstruction objectives.

entry.title: Visual Distortion Detection in UGC Images Using Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Ziheng Jia, Yingji Liang, Jiaying Qian, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: Proposes VIGIL, which uses a large multimodal model to localize and describe specific visual distortions in user-generated images instead of predicting a single quality score. Focuses on the synthetic-to-authentic generalization gap that hurts models trained on artificially degraded data.

entry.title: Multimodal Federated Learning under Dual-Axis Modality Missingness

author.name: Adiba Orzikulova, Jaehyun Kwak, Jaemin Shin, Yunqi Guo, Xiaomin Ouyang, Guoliang Xing, Steven Euijong Whang, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: Addresses multimodal federated learning where clients hold different modality sets and individual samples are also missing modalities, a dual-axis missingness setting prior work treats separately. Flux learns per-sample per-modality confidence and fuses it into an adaptive temperature that adjusts prediction sharpness.

entry.title: SafeQL: Search-based Refinement for Safe and Efficient LLM-based Text-to-SQL

author.name: Geonho Lee, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: SafeQL turns the database engine from a passive error reporter into an active guide for text-to-SQL refinement, performing search-based repair over schema-valid components instead of regenerating whole queries after failures. Targets invalid references to nonexistent tables, columns, functions, and values.

entry.title: UniDFKD: A Unified Semantic Prior Framework for Architecture-Agnostic Data-Free Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Xuewan He, Tong Chu, Zihan Cheng, Yuchen Su, Qianxin Xia, Guoming Lu, Jielei Wang, Wen Li

entry.summary: UniDFKD makes data-free knowledge distillation architecture-agnostic by replacing batch-normalization statistical priors, which modern vision transformers lack, with a unified semantic prior for synthesizing training data. Aims to prevent the catastrophic degradation seen when distilling ViT teachers without data.

entry.title: ZetaGPT: A Reference Implementation of Positional--Encoding--Free State--Space--Attention Language Models

author.name: R\'ois\'in Luo

entry.summary: ZetaGPT is a reference implementation of a language model that removes explicit positional embeddings or rotary encodings by inserting causal state-space equations before attention so order information is implicit. Frames positional information as an inherent property of the computation rather than an added component.

entry.title: Learning Preference Adaptation for Large Language Model Personalization via Verbal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuting Liu, Wei Wu, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo

entry.summary: Studies task-specific preference adaptation, deriving from a universal natural-language user preference summary a task-conditioned view that keeps decision-relevant evidence and drops distracting context. AlignXada is a training-free meta-learning framework that performs this adaptation via verbal reinforcement.

entry.title: STAIR: Effective Incident Response Using an End-to-End Agentic Planning Framework

author.name: Hanlin Jiang, Jionghao Huang, Shaofei Li, Bojia Yu, Peng Jiang, Yuxin Ren, Ning Jia, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: STAIR is an agentic planning framework for cyber incident response that represents the live incident as a graph state, aligns actions to the current recovery stage, and reuses historical experience to stay stable over long horizons. Contrasts with static expert playbooks and unstructured LLM tool-use planners.

entry.title: Distributed Optimization with Streaming Data: A Temporal Weighting Perspective

author.name: Muhammad Faraz Ul Abrar, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Erik G. Larsson

entry.summary: Theoretical study of decentralized optimization when data arrives as a stream and the objective is a time-weighted average of losses across a network. The paper analyzes multi-iteration decentralized gradient methods and derives guarantees for strongly convex smooth losses.

entry.title: TSPORec: Token Selection via Preference Optimization for LLM-Based Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Wenqiao Zhu, Chao Xu, Haipang Wu, Ji Liu

entry.summary: TSPORec uses preference optimization to choose which tokens of item descriptions a language-model recommender should keep, instead of naively truncating to the first few tokens for cost reasons. The goal is to cut inference cost in sequential recommendation without discarding informative text.

entry.title: Predictive safety filter enhanced curriculum learning control for efficient vehicle dynamics controller

author.name: Baocong Zhang, Siliang Lu, Chenyang Li

entry.summary: Combines curriculum reinforcement learning for vehicle motion and dynamics control with a physics-based predictive safety filter that screens actions before execution. The aim is to reduce hand calibration effort of classical controllers while retaining stability guarantees learning alone cannot provide.

entry.title: TSDS-Toolbox: A Toolbox for Measuring Time-Series Dataset Similarity

author.name: Yen-Ku Liu, Hongjie Chen, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt

entry.summary: Provides a unified toolbox for benchmarking methods that measure similarity between time-series datasets, motivated by the role such similarity plays in selecting source data for fine-tuning time-series foundation models. It emphasizes reproducible comparison and easy extension with custom measures.

entry.title: Measuring and Reducing WebGPU Dispatch Overhead for LLM Inference

author.name: J\k{e}drzej Maczan

entry.summary: Measures WebGPU per-operation dispatch overhead for browser-based LLM inference using a sequential-dispatch protocol that separates dispatch cost from synchronization, showing naive single-op timing overestimates cost. Concludes that at batch size one the bottleneck is dispatch count rather than kernel quality, motivating operator fusion.

entry.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for Robust Traffic Sign Perception in Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Pedram MohajerAnsari, Amir Salarpour, Mert D. Pes\'e

entry.summary: LAMDA improves traffic sign recognition robustness to physically realizable attacks such as shadows, glare and printed patches by aligning features to fixed text prototype banks generated from vision-language descriptions with a frozen CLIP text encoder. It needs no adversarial examples during training and adds no inference cost.

entry.title: Label-Free Parkinson's Disease Screening from Face and Voice through Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Jiaheng Su, Yu Sun

entry.summary: Screens for Parkinson's disease from face and voice using only frozen pretrained encoders and healthy control data, with no disease labels touching any fitting step. Voice scoring uses a contrastive activation addition direction built from synthetic dysarthria degradations while faces use nearest-neighbor anomaly distance to the control cluster.

entry.title: Dynamic Distribution-Aware Uncertainty Tracking in Vision-Language Representation Learning

author.name: Ao Zhou, Zhiwei Jiang, Zifeng Cheng, Cong Wang, Shufan Yang, Haoru Chen, Qing Gu

entry.summary: DDA-UQ argues that post-hoc uncertainty estimators for vision-language models overfit failure patterns of the source domain and cannot handle shifting test distributions. It replaces static output-to-uncertainty mapping with a dynamic distribution-aware process that tracks test-time distribution changes.

entry.title: HOPPER: Learnable Hop Extraction for Linearized Graph Sequence Models

author.name: Isuru Herath, Arin Gopakumar, Sharan Sahu

entry.summary: HOPPER makes linearized graph sequence models learn how to construct their propagation sequences instead of relying on fixed graph operators, adapting hop extraction to the graph, features and task. The aim is to keep information depth decoupled from processing depth while avoiding over-smoothing and over-squashing.

entry.title: A Probabilistic Circuit-Induced Pseudo-Metric for Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Bhumika K, Vidhya S, Narayanan C Krishnan

entry.summary: Instead of reducing a probabilistic circuit to its root likelihood for out-of-distribution detection, this work forms a hierarchical likelihood vector from selected internal nodes and defines a pseudo-metric comparing distributions through expectations of these vectors. The metric is shown to be an integral probability metric over a function class induced by the circuit.

entry.title: CoCoNav: Conformal Control for Safe Robot Navigation in Crowds

author.name: Cheng Guo, Mingzhe Ni, Zheng Liang, Yihu Ling, Yuan Hu, Michele Caprio, Daniele Pucci, Wei Pan

entry.summary: CoCoNav combines online conformal calibration of pedestrian trajectory prediction errors with runtime-certified model predictive control for crowd navigation. A horizon-specific conformal proportional-integral controller adapts error bounds to maintain long-run coverage while avoiding the infeasibility caused by overly conservative hard constraints.

entry.title: EFFEKT: Efficient Federated Knowledge Transfer to Foundation Models

author.name: Matteo Caligiuri, Francesco Barbato, Pietro Zanuttigh, Francesco Restuccia

entry.summary: EFFEKT lets resource-limited federated clients train lightweight proxy models that collaborate with a server-side foundation model, which learns domain-specific LoRA adapters without seeing private data. Bi-directional cross-distillation keeps the proxy and foundation feature spaces aligned across multiple domains.

entry.title: Transfer Learning-Enabled Distortion Compensation for Amplitude-Phase-Time Block Modulation-Based Nonlinear Single-Carrier Wireless Communications

author.name: Guoxing Duan, Min Fan, Cheng Yi, Bensheng Yang, Wei Xu, Haiming Wang, Xiaohu You

entry.summary: Analyzes decentralized learning in nonzero-sum linear-quadratic stochastic games where players do not even know opponents exist, observing only a shared state and their own actions. The authors prove that independent epsilon-greedy iterated least-squares dynamics still converge in a meaningful sense despite unidentifiable system parameters.

entry.title: ADEx-FNO: A Unified Ambient-Domain Framework for Fourier Neural Operators on Varying Geometries

author.name: Roberto Nuca, Giovanni Testa, Luca Galimberti, Matteo Parsani

entry.summary: ADEx-FNO handles varying geometries for Fourier neural operators by embedding each physical domain in a fixed ambient hypercube described by a signed distance function, without altering the Fourier layers. Fields are deterministically extended, mapped to a shared latent grid, processed, then interpolated back to arbitrary target discretizations.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Robust Acoustic Localization with Calibrated Uncertainty

author.name: Jennifer N. Kampe, Changwoo J. Lee, Xin Shen, Ari Lehti\"o, Sandro von Brandenburg, Ossi Nokelainen, David B. Dunson, Otso Ovaskainen

entry.summary: Refines rather than replaces the physics of acoustic source localization for passive acoustic monitoring, where multipath, near-field effects, and complex propagation break classical hyperbolic and score-based methods. The method delivers robust localization with calibrated uncertainty for ecological point-process data at scale.

entry.title: Mind the Hook: Source-Level Auditing of Privacy Defenses in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: Audits privacy defenses in retrieval-augmented generation at the source level, inventorying which pipeline hook each defense actually modifies and matching metrics to the leakage channel they observe. The audit finds that some differential-privacy-style benchmark reimplementations only alter retrieval scores while their generation hooks are unimplemented stubs, explaining why they shift membership-inference numbers but leave generated-text entity leakage unchanged.

entry.title: Verifiably grounded machine interpretation of lunar geology

author.name: Tom Sander, Kay Wohlfarth, Christian W\"ohler

entry.summary: Trains a multimodal vision-language model to produce verifiably grounded stratigraphic interpretations of lunar mare basalt volcanism from co-registered topographic, spectral, and geologic maps. Reports that the system balances geologic priors with local visual evidence for descriptive tasks but defaults to priors rather than vision for numeric age dating.

entry.title: VADER: Adaptive Debiasing for Hallucination Mitigation in Video Large Language Models

author.name: Dong Xing, Jiaxin Chen, Hang Yang, Peixun Liu, Qiushi Yang, Yuqing Wang

entry.summary: A training-free method to reduce hallucination in video large language models by diagnosing layer-wise visual-to-text evidence flow per input and instantiating an adaptive intervention, rather than applying a fixed global visual bias correction. It also reweights evidence to counter cross-frame redundancy that defeats contrastive decoding.

entry.title: VANE: Reliable Test-Time Training for Vision-Language-Action Models via Future Visual Representation Prediction

author.name: Hongjin Ji, Guoyang Xia, Luoyang Sun, Fangxiang Feng, Lei Ren

entry.summary: VANE makes test-time training safe for vision-language-action policies by isolating candidate updates from the live policy, evaluating them against the future visual consequences of executed actions, and committing only updates supported by that evidence. It targets the risk that online adaptation changes downstream behavior before its effects are known.

entry.title: Phase State Space Models: Parallel, Surrogate-Free Training of Spiking Networks

author.name: Wilkie Olin-Ammentorp

entry.summary: This paper reinterprets resonate-and-fire spiking neurons as phase state space models, enabling parallel rather than sequential training without surrogate gradients and connecting the formulation to hyperdimensional computing. A demonstration integrates short-time Fourier analysis, recurrent memory and attention-like features in one spike-compatible network.

entry.title: You Don't Need To Stay in The Loop: An Agentic Robotics Loop for Robot-Policy Improvement

author.name: Hang Yu

entry.summary: AgenticRobotics ports the coding-agent pattern to robot policy improvement: an LLM controller drives disposable workers through durable train-evaluate-improve transactions with controller-owned measurement, crash recovery, an evidence-graded skill library and expiring tool registry. The design assumption is that robotic tools such as trained policies and data collection routinely fail, so tool quality must be measured and invalidated continuously.

entry.title: SurgWMBench: A Vision-Based Benchmark for World-Modeling Surgical Instrument Motion Planning

author.name: Huanrong Liu, Weiliang Huang, Bob Zhang, Weichao Cai, Chunlin Tian, Qingbiao Li

entry.summary: SurgWMBench is a vision-based benchmark for world models that must jointly predict surgical instrument motion and the resulting evolution of the operative visual state, rather than only classifying phases or forecasting trajectories. It provides standardized evaluation for surgical world modeling, an area with fragmented protocols.

entry.title: SHRIMP: Iterative Refinement of Robot Task Plans

author.name: Mya Schroder, Yuna Hwang, Callie Y. Kim, Leqian Cheng, Jeffrey Li-cheng Liu, Chenchen Zheng, Xinning He, Bilge Mutlu

entry.summary: SHRIMP lets non-expert users generate hierarchical robot primitive plans from natural language and then iteratively inspect and refine them before execution, addressing semantic ambiguity and the opacity of language-to-action translation. The system emphasizes user validation of plans rather than blind execution of generated code.

entry.title: Latent World Models with Monotone Planning Costs for Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Amirhosein Chahe, Siwei Cai, Lifeng Zhou

entry.summary: Builds an image-goal navigation latent world model on a frozen DINO-family encoder and trains it with an autoregressive rollout loss plus a monotone cost ranking loss that forces increasingly perturbed action sequences to receive higher planning costs. The insight is that accurate prediction is insufficient if the planning cost ranks candidate action sequences incorrectly for CEM-style planners.

entry.title: Conditional Distribution Estimation for Functional Responses with Random Forests

author.name: Poorbita Kundu, Antonio R. Linero

entry.summary: Introduces functional distributional random forests that estimate the entire conditional law of a functional response as a covariate-dependent distribution over sampled functions, trained by minimizing kernel maximum mean discrepancy within leaf nodes. This goes beyond conditional mean curves to capture how covariates shape variability, timing, and shape.

entry.title: Long SKILL Compliance as Logical Reasoning: Closure-Grounded Detection with Scaling-Guided On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Shuaitao Zhao, Feng Ni, Lichao Ma, Jiaye Lin, Fei Han, Yang Wei, Lu Pan

entry.summary: Represents long enterprise policy documents as a two-layer constraint dependency graph, with an upper layer routing scenarios and a lower layer capturing dependencies among atomic constraints, then uses two-level retrieval plus dependency closure for compliance judgment. On-policy distillation transfers this capability to smaller models to cut inference cost.

entry.title: Open-World Semantic Segmentation with Sensitivity Modeling

author.name: Anastasios Romanos Varvarigos, Nikos Giakoumoglou, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Extends a dual-decoder open-world segmentation model with a third decoder so the system can segment known classes with Gaussian prototypes, isolate unknown content via contrastive learning, and group anomalies without extra supervision. Targets overconfident misclassification on novel content in deployed vision systems.

entry.title: PRISM: A Predictive Protocol for Permutation Optimization via Landscape Diagnostics

author.name: Blessings Mambwe

entry.summary: Proposes measuring cheap fitness-landscape diagnostics such as move autocorrelation and fitness-distance correlation before choosing a search operator for permutation optimization, and shows the protocol makes testable predictions across synthetic landscapes, neural architecture search, scientific pipelines and LLM instruction ordering. Also identifies regimes where search barely beats random sampling.

entry.title: A New Approach to Characterising Optimisation Problems Using Programmatic Representation and Complexity Measures

author.name: Marcus Gallagher, Katherine M. Malan

entry.summary: Characterizes optimization problem instances by the complexity of the code implementing their objective function, using Halstead volume as a cheap proxy for the entropy of the program and relating it to search landscape difficulty. Intended to support algorithm selection and configuration.

entry.title: Input convex neural networks as surrogates in mathematical optimisation

author.name: Yu Liu, Jan Kronqvist, Fabricio Oliveira

entry.summary: Advocates input convex neural networks instead of standard ReLU feedforward networks as surrogate models embedded inside mathematical optimization problems when the underlying response is approximately convex. Shows the convex structure yields tighter linear relaxations and cheaper mixed-integer formulations, sometimes with no integrality gap.

entry.title: VectraYX-Vision-1B: A Sub-2B Spanish/LATAM Cybersecurity Vision-Language Model with Structured Visual Reasoning and Native Tool Use

author.name: Juan S. Santillana

entry.summary: Pretrains the first dedicated bidirectional selective state-space encoder for Arabic masked language modeling as a linear-time alternative to quadratic self-attention in Arabic BERT variants, trained on modest consumer GPUs. Evaluates against established Arabic transformer encoders on understanding tasks.

entry.title: Same Question, Different Answer? Measuring and Mitigating Prompt Privilege for Equitable AI Access

author.name: Lier Jin, Lan Hu, Binqi Shen, Hanyu Cai, Yuting Xin

entry.summary: Defines prompt privilege, the phenomenon where semantically equivalent requests get systematically better answers when phrased by users with prompt-engineering expertise, and proposes measurement plus mitigation. Frames this as an equity of access problem distinct from the adversarial robustness and prompt optimization literatures.

entry.title: LexKairos: Benchmarking Legal Temporal Capabilities in LLMs

author.name: Chenyang Li, Zejia Feng, Yuqin Huang, Yuxiao Ye, Huiyuan Xie

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark for legal temporal reasoning in Chinese law spanning statutory temporal knowledge, case timeline modeling, and combined statute-case temporal inference across nine sub-tasks drawn from real judicial materials. Evaluates several LLMs on a dimension existing legal AI benchmarks largely omit.

entry.title: Intent Speaks Louder: Controllable User Simulation Beyond Response Imitation

author.name: Bo Wang, Ruixing Zhang, Yunqi Liu, Yang Zhang, Liangzhe Han, Tongyu Zhu, Leilei Sun

entry.summary: Argues that controllable user simulation should separate which local interaction intent the next user turn realizes from how that intent is verbalized, and introduces a method that exposes intent as an explicit per-turn directive over a six-way intent taxonomy. Aims to prevent fluent but pragmatically wrong simulated turns, such as accepting when the user should be repairing.

entry.title: UniScale: Arbitrary-Scale Industrial Anomaly Generation

author.name: Shilei Zeng, Linxin Guan, Xurui Li, Yaohan Tang, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: UniScale generates synthetic industrial defects at arbitrary scales, addressing the loss of small-anomaly information caused by aggressive latent downsampling in diffusion models. It uses error-suppressed multi-scale training to learn location-aware defect textures while limiting upsampling interpolation artifacts.

entry.title: DeCo: Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Generation through Decoupling and Recoupling

author.name: Shilei Zeng, Xurui Li, Yaohan Tang, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: DeCo generates industrial anomalies on a target product without any real defective images of that product by decoupling defect structure from its source product and recoupling it with target textures. It uses a dual-routing flow to bind texture-invariant anomaly structure to a dedicated token under a product-consistency constraint.

entry.title: SegDem: Segmentation helps Demosaicing

author.name: Ping Chen, Xiangming Wang, Yongyong Chen, Jiezhang Cao, Kai Zhang, Jingyong Su, Jie Liu, Haijin Zeng

entry.summary: SegDem argues that reconstruction and scene understanding are complementary views of shared structure and transfers instance-segmentation decoder representations into an image demosaicing network. This gives the low-level reconstruction task access to semantic and structural priors beyond local texture statistics.

entry.title: SCoPE: Training-Free Audio-Visual Event Perception via Sparse Cross-Modal Prior Exchange

author.name: Jaemo Jeong, Junho Yoon, Hyunju Kim, Dongman Lee

entry.summary: SCoPE is a training-free audio-visual event perception method that makes all queried labels compete for shared evidence, addressing false co-activations where a wrong related label scores as high as the correct one. It exchanges sparse cross-modal priors so that thresholding is not the only defense against confusable labels.

entry.title: SportsGrounder: Proposal-Aided Interleaved Grounding for Dense Sports Video Reasoning

author.name: Yizhi Li, Jiawei Jiang, Guanhong Wang, Yingcai Wu, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: SportsGrounder pairs a large multimodal model with an open-vocabulary visual expert to produce interleaved grounding for dense sports video, where many small, visually identical players and a ball must be tracked over long contexts. The design counters the tendency of current models to fall back on textual priors when fine visual detail is missing.

entry.title: AdaDINO: Pair-Aware In-Backbone Adaptation of Frozen DINO for Efficient Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Xu Zhang, Xinqing Li, Jianpeng Xie, Zeshuai Zhu, Xin He, Yun Liu

entry.summary: AdaDINO adapts a frozen DINO backbone for bi-temporal remote sensing change detection by inserting gated local adaptation modules that exchange information between the two image streams inside the encoder. Shared temporal residuals with opposite signs sharpen genuine change responses rather than comparing independently encoded features after the fact.

entry.title: AgriField-40K: Adapting Vision Models to Agriculture With Efficient Continual Pretraining

author.name: Vasileios Tzouras, Paraskevas Pegios, Lazaros Nalpantidis

entry.summary: AgriField-40K aggregates 17 public sources into a field-centric agricultural vision dataset, and AgriMAE continually pretrains a natural-image masked autoencoder using only lightweight adapters. The adapter-based adaptation reportedly matches or beats full fine-tuning on downstream agricultural tasks.

entry.title: SCTD 3.0: Sonar Common Target Detection in the Wild - A Large-Scale, Multi-Scene Dataset from Real Marine Surveys

author.name: Peng Zhang

entry.summary: SCTD 3.0 releases over 10,000 real synthetic aperture sonar image snippets covering ten target categories across varied seabeds, frequencies, viewing angles, and ranges. It aims to replace small single-scenario sonar benchmarks that fail to capture real acoustic scattering conditions.

entry.title: Staying True to the Origin: Continuous Image Stylization with Smooth Transitions

author.name: Rui Xu, Hanmo Zhang, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: This work treats image stylization as a continuous control problem for diffusion transformer editing models, using a two-stage training strategy and a style-strength spline so users can smoothly trade content fidelity against style intensity. The goal is preserving semantic structure while allowing strong stylization on demand.

entry.title: Hierarchical Fast--Slow ReAct Agent for Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Zhaochen Lan, Zhi Yang, Yuxiang Fu, Mengxiang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical fast-slow agent for zero-shot object-goal navigation that keeps a value-map controller for reactive frontier selection while a slower deliberative loop reconsiders previously observed evidence rather than discarding it after each argmax decision. It also defines fallbacks when a vision-language model query fails, which fixed-schedule VLM-in-the-loop systems lack.

entry.title: Agent-MD: Selective LLM Intervention with Event-Driven Escalation for Stateful GCMC--MD Campaigns

author.name: Yijie Wang, Zhen-Yu Yin, Zhenheng Tang, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: Presents a framework that inserts LLM reasoning only at campaign setup and event-triggered review points while a deterministic rule-based agent handles routine molecular simulation continuation, analysis, and archiving. It is demonstrated on a grand canonical Monte Carlo plus molecular dynamics desorption campaign over several clay systems.

entry.title: CyberAGENTS: Structured Autonomy for Agentic Gamified Learning in Cybersecurity

author.name: Ivan Hornung, Deepthi Marasinghe Arachchige, Tharindu Kumarage, Garima Agrawal, Yuli Deng, Ying-Chih Chen, Huan Liu

entry.summary: Presents an agentic framework for gamified cybersecurity education that enforces structured autonomy through ontology-guided validation, schema-governed behavioral control, and competency-based progression. The design is grounded in learning science to counter inconsistent behavior and hallucinated reasoning from generative tutors.

entry.title: FemWear: A Specialized Wearable Foundation Model for Women's Health

author.name: Yifan Wang, Chenzhong Li

entry.summary: FemWear adapts a pretrained multimodal wearable sensor backbone to women's health tasks using low-rank adapters that train about one percent of encoder parameters, learning one shared longitudinal representation across menstrual, sleep, autonomic and pregnancy-related outcomes. Evaluation spans six cohorts and dozens of primary metrics. It illustrates parameter-efficient specialization of sensor foundation models for an underserved health domain.

entry.title: Discovering Diverse Planning Policies for Multimodal Embodied Agents with Quality-Diversity Optimization

author.name: Pengfei Xu, Yong Liu, Xiaoya Nan, Qiang Yang, Peilan Xu

entry.summary: This work applies quality-diversity evolutionary search to multimodal embodied planning, treating planning-policy templates as evolvable individuals stored in a behavior-indexed archive so an agent can switch styles when its dominant mode stalls. The motivation is that single-style large-model planners get stuck repeating ineffective interactions. It brings an established optimization paradigm to LLM-based embodied agents.

entry.title: Theory-Guided Deception Detection: A RAG-Based Artificial Intelligence Exploration

author.name: David M. Markowitz, Timothy R. Levine

entry.summary: Seven retrieval-augmented pipelines grounded in different deception-detection theories were compared against baselines across 700 statements, four models and nearly 40,000 judgments. Accuracy stayed near typical human levels around 55 percent regardless of theoretical grounding, with only a small reduction in truth bias. A well-powered null result cautioning against claims that theory-grounded retrieval unlocks lie detection.

entry.title: From Manuals to Maintenance: Fine-Tuning MedGemma for Multi-Modal Imaging System Support in Low-Resource Settings

author.name: Bernes Lorier Atabonfack, Zion Kongbi Nfo, Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Tolulope Olusuyi, Clemence Ingabire, Mohammed Hardi Abdul Baaki, Mawuli Deku, Abdulrazaq Zubair, Alyasaa Anas, Raymond Confidence, Maruf Adewole, Udunna C. Anazodo

entry.summary: A question-answering system for maintaining medical imaging equipment in low- and middle-income countries, built from a nine-country needs survey and technical manuals into a curated set of over 10,000 filtered pairs, then used to fine-tune a medical foundation model with quantized low-rank adaptation. The model interprets error logs and produces step-by-step troubleshooting guidance. Addresses device downtime as a concrete healthcare access bottleneck.

entry.title: An Explainable GNN Framework for Component-Level Anomaly Diagnosis

author.name: Sena Ozgunay (IMT, ANITI, LAAS-DISCO, LAAS, Comue de Toulouse), Louise Trav\'e-Massuy\`es (LAAS-DISCO, Comue de Toulouse, ANITI), Jean-Michel Loubes (IMT, REGALIA), Raul Sena Ferreira (LAAS)

entry.summary: Proposes an explainable graph neural network framework for industrial multivariate time series that attributes anomalies to disrupted inter-sensor influences rather than simply blaming the most deviant sensor, enabling component-level fault diagnosis. Targets root-cause identification in complex process systems.

entry.title: CARD: Controlled Agentic Reddit Discussions for Credit Card Simulation

author.name: Yaoning Yu, Kai-Min Chang, Ye Yu, Yi-Chia Wang, Haojing Luo, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: CARD generates synthetic credit card discussion threads matched to real Reddit threads using non-verbatim guidance over reply structure, comment function, stance, tone, and variation, with a planner, a writer, and a calibration loop that adjusts comment populations to close distributional gaps with real threads.
