Targets realistic simulation of consumer financial conversation.

entry.title: HugSelect: An Explainable Multi-Criteria Decision-Support Framework for foundation-model selection

author.name: Alireza Joonbakhsh (Shiraz University), Arda Canser Adal{\i} (Utrecht University), Slinger Jansen (Utrecht University), Farshad Khunjush (Shiraz University), Siamak Farshidi (Wageningen University, Research)

entry.summary: Frames foundation-model selection as an auditable software component decision and builds a knowledge base of over seventy thousand hub models combining metadata, extracted capabilities and community-perceived quality, then offers explainable multi-criteria ranking. Argues popularity-based discovery is inadequate for engineering use.

entry.title: A Grounded and Decomposed Framework for Relation-Level Hallucination Evaluation in Abstractive Summarization

author.name: Praveen Kumar Katwe, Rakesh Chandra Balabantaray, Kali Prasad Vittala, Naman Kabadi

entry.summary: Builds a dependency-parsing pipeline with negation handling, passive-agent recovery and entity grounding to extract relations from source documents and summaries, then scores relation-level hallucination with an index. Targets fabricated or distorted entity relationships in abstractive summarization.

entry.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in English to Romanian Machine Translation

author.name: Ioana Grigore, Sergiu Nisioi

entry.summary: Combines a fine-tuned LLM gender classifier that inserts inline gender hint tags with a Transformer translation model trained to honour those tags, reducing default-masculine and stereotyped outputs when translating English into Romanian. Includes a purpose-built dataset for the language pair.

entry.title: Hybrid Neural-Classical Correction for Frozen Time Series Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Ablation Study on High-Frequency Stock Prediction

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Suranadi De Silva, Shankhadeep Mondal

entry.summary: Studies hybrid correction of a frozen time series foundation model for high-frequency stock return prediction, comparing a small attention corrector and an even smaller gated low-rank corrector, each combined with random forest residual learning, across ten large-cap technology stocks. Provides a systematic ablation of adapting general forecasters to a hard specialised domain.

entry.title: GALA: Graph-Augmented LLM Agents for Root Cause Analysis and Incident Response in Microservices

author.name: Yifang Tian, Yaming Liu, Zichun Chong, Zihang Huang, Yiran Li, Hans-Arno Jacobsen

entry.summary: Presents GALA+, a graph-augmented LLM agent for microservice root cause analysis that uses service dependency graphs to bound exploration and fuses multi-modal telemetry with a trace- and graph-aware scoring module. Unlike prior systems it goes beyond fault ranking to produce actionable incident response steps.

entry.title: How People Evaluate AI-, Expert-, and Peer-Style Financial Advice

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A preregistered vignette experiment with 285 participants holds financial advice content constant while varying communication style across AI assistant, certified planner, and community forum framings, and independently manipulates source labels including mislabeling. Separates the effect of who people think is speaking from the effect of stylistic cues.

entry.title: Triple Expert Learning from Noisy Labels for Semi-Supervised Vision Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Xuanyu Liu, Zheng Fang, Hongyang He, Yundi Hong, Daizong Liu

entry.summary: TriNoL adapts vision foundation models semi-supervised by routing unlabeled samples into three confidence bands and assigning each to a dedicated LoRA expert for high-confidence, ambiguous, and noisy pseudo-labels. This prevents one low-rank adapter from absorbing conflicting gradients.

entry.title: GLocFM: A Geometry-Aware Foundation Model for 3D Indoor Wireless Localization

author.name: Chenghong Bian, Chaozheng Wen, Hongze Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: GLocFM is a geometry-aware foundation model for indoor wireless localization that jointly consumes WiFi channel measurements and 3D point-cloud scene geometry, formulating position estimation as maximum-likelihood scoring over candidate transmitter locations. The geometry conditioning is intended to exploit non-line-of-sight paths and generalize to unseen scenes.

entry.title: DAVE: A Decoupled Audio-Visual Enhancement Framework for Real-World Speech Separation

author.name: Wei Zhou, Wanyi Ning, Yinshang Guo, Qianxiao Fang, Haitao Qian, Yingpeng Li

entry.summary: DAVE decouples visual conditioning from the separation network for real-world audio-visual speech enhancement so that degraded or unreliable video does not corrupt separation, and releases a 219,411-mixture corpus built by combinatorial acoustic augmentation of public meeting recordings. Uses progressive multi-objective optimization to balance separation and enhancement goals.

entry.title: FeedbackTrack: Visual-Cortex-Inspired Cross-Frame Feedback for Transformer Tracking

author.name: Yueyang Cang, Xiaoteng Zhang, Zhiyuan Ning, Yuchen He, Li Shi

entry.summary: FeedbackTrack adds sparse, layer-aligned cross-frame feedback to pretrained transformer trackers, caching previous-frame intermediate states and reinjecting them into matching layer groups through query modulation and gating pathways. Motivated by recurrent feedback connections in visual cortex.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Restoration: Empowering All-in-One Restoration with Pixel-Level Multimodal Guidance

author.name: Chunxiao Liu, Wei Liu, Anbin Xiong, Erli Meng

entry.summary: MGN-AIR performs all-in-one image restoration at pixel granularity with multimodal guidance, rather than applying one uniform strategy to a whole image whose regions may suffer different degradation types and severities. Enables finer-grained control over the restoration process.

entry.title: Defining Decentralization: An Ontological Perspective

author.name: Jakub Kacper Szel\k{a}g, Aydin Abadi, Mohammad Naseri

entry.summary: Argues that decentralization has no agreed definition across computer science and proposes an ontological account distinguishing it from related notions it is often conflated with. The motivation is the rise of decentralized AI paradigms such as collaborative training, distributed inference, and agentic systems where decentralization is treated as a design goal.

entry.title: Exact Rank and Convex Calibration Dimension Lower Bounds for the Multi-Label F1 Loss

author.name: Mingyuan Zhang

entry.summary: Determines the exact rank of the instance-wise multi-label F1 loss matrix, showing it equals s squared minus s plus two for s labels, and derives lower bounds on the convex calibration dimension of surrogate losses. The proof routes the score matrix through subset-incidence matrices and a positive-definite Cauchy matrix.

entry.title: Domain-Aware Pruning: Sparsity and Domain Generalization via Regularized Probabilistic Masking

author.name: Parham Sazdar, Mostafa Tavassolipour, Reshad Hosseini

entry.summary: Domain-Aware Pruning learns continuous per-parameter retention probabilities with a regularizer that penalizes keeping domain-sensitive weights, so sparsification also selects a domain-invariant subnetwork. It treats compression and out-of-distribution generalization as a single objective rather than separate goals.

entry.title: The Cost of Adaptivity: Matching Lower Bounds Across Learning Problems

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Adria Binte Habib

entry.summary: Formalizes the price an algorithm pays for not knowing nuisance quantities such as gradient scale or smoothness, using a slice-normalized minimax ratio, and separately quantifies the cost of allowing post-hoc rather than preannounced queries. Provides a finite-horizon composition law for Gaussian certification across many coordinates.

entry.title: Gradient Under Microscope: Benchmarking Resource Utilization of Memory-Efficient Gradient Computation Methods

author.name: Sarthak Mahapatra, Zihan Zhou, Khatoon Khedri, Mehdi Hosseinzadeh, Reza Rawassizadeh

entry.summary: Benchmarks five optimizers against three memory-saving strategies, namely standard training, gradient checkpointing and gradient accumulation, across four transformer models including a 1B-parameter Llama variant and a small vision-language model. Gradient accumulation emerges as the most reliable strategy, cutting loss substantially without extra GPU memory.

entry.title: FEAST: Federated Shared-Space Training for Resource-Heterogeneous Clients

author.name: Bostan Khan, Masoud Daneshtalab

entry.summary: FEAST trains a federated supernet so that parameters exclusive to large subnetworks are not starved when most clients can only afford small ones, by training multiple subnetworks within each client's compute budget. Budget-tailored routing sends only relevant supernet slices and sparse aggregation merges returned parameter subsets.

entry.title: Hallucinations and Constraints : Regulating surgical workflow recognition beyond accuracy

author.name: John S. H. Baxter, Pierre Jannin

entry.summary: Proposes that in medical image and signal analysis, topological errors are a measurable analogue of hallucination, since they can be expressed as linear temporal logic predicates. Some such constraints can be explicitly enforced through probabilistic graphical models, offering a route to regulate surgical workflow recognition beyond raw accuracy.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability-Guided Selective Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models for Centimeter-Level Flood Depth Estimation

author.name: Nafis Fuad, Xiaodong Qian, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: Fine-tunes vision-language models to estimate street-level flood depth at centimeter resolution from imagery, training on a large synthetic corpus rendered in a game engine. Notably, mechanistic interpretability analysis identifies the few causally relevant cross-attention layers, and sparse fine-tuning of just those layers is compared against full QLoRA tuning.

entry.title: Real-time physics inversion for retrieval of sub-pixel wildfire temperatures from VSWIR imaging spectroscopy

author.name: William R. Keely, Philip G. Brodrick, Katherine Mistick, Adam Chlus, Robert O. Green, Philip E. Dennison

entry.summary: A full-physics retrieval framework estimates sub-pixel wildfire temperatures from airborne imaging spectrometer data, using GPU-accelerated nonlinear least squares to converge within flight cadence. Forward-model assumptions are validated on simulated spectra with injected thermal signatures.

entry.title: The Spectral Neuron

author.name: Alex Shtoff

entry.summary: Introduces the spectral neuron, a scalar model that returns a chosen eigenvalue of an affine matrix function of the inputs, with learned symmetric matrices. The aim is a unit that is more expressive than a linear model while retaining shape control and interpretability.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion for Nonparametric Instrumental Variable Quantile Regression

author.name: Xingdong Feng, Xinhong Jiang, Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Junwei Liu

entry.summary: A two-stage estimator for nonparametric instrumental variable quantile regression that first learns the joint conditional distribution with a conditional diffusion model, then estimates the structural quantile function via kernel-smoothed conditional moments. Excess-risk and end-to-end error bounds are provided.

entry.title: Kernel Methods for Refined Prophet Inequalities

author.name: Patrick Loiseau, Mathieu Molina, Vianney Perchet, Sebastian Perez-Salazar, Victor Verdugo

entry.summary: Refines classical prophet inequality guarantees by bounding the relative variance of the maximum, since the worst-case-tight hard instances rely on rare enormous realizations. This yields a nonparametric complexity measure interpolating between deterministic instances and the fully unconstrained worst case, analyzed with kernel methods.

entry.title: Tied Trit-Planes: Constraining PTQTP to a Uniform Nine-Level Quantizer, with a Persistent Folded Format for Disk-Streamed Mixture-of-Experts Serving

author.name: Matteo Grella

entry.summary: Constrains a two-plane ternary post-training quantization scheme so that tying its scales at a fixed ratio collapses it into a uniform nine-level quantizer, which folds losslessly into a single 4-bit code plane. That folded format becomes the persistent serving representation for disk-streamed mixture-of-experts inference, with the same bytes on disk, in expert cache, and in the integer kernel.

entry.title: Diagnosing as Cardiologists Do: ECG Agents with Doctor-Grounded Priors for Clinical Reasoning Across Diseases and Populations

author.name: Hongxiang Gao, He-yang Xu, Yuwen Li, Minghui Zhao, Zhipeng Cai, Xingyao Wang, Chenxi Yang, Jianqing Li, Chengyu Liu

entry.summary: LuminaECG structures ECG interpretation the way cardiologists work, rendering signals on standard grid paper and explicitly delineating P-wave, QRS, and T-wave boundaries with color-coded segmentation so an agent reasons over measurement-grounded visual evidence. The framework is evaluated for reasoning across diseases and populations.

entry.title: Personalized Federated Learning via Variance-Aware Nonparametric Empirical Bayes

author.name: Jae Ho Chang, Arnab Auddy, Subhadeep Paul

entry.summary: Proposes a personalized federated learning method that treats each client's local risk-minimization estimate as a noisy observation and fits a shared prior by nonparametric maximum likelihood. The key extension, called variance-aware NPEB, handles the realistic case where the asymptotic variance of local estimators is unknown and parameter-dependent. Matters as a statistically principled alternative to heuristic personalization objectives.

entry.title: Rethinking Attention Locality in Spiking Transformers

author.name: Zeqi Zheng, Zizheng Zhu, Yuping Yan, Wenxuan Pan, Zhaofei Yu, Yaochu Jin

entry.summary: Analyzes whether existing locality-enhancement tricks in spiking transformers actually produce spatial locality, using mean attention distance diagnostics, and finds computational locality does not imply spatial locality and that uniform enhancement ignores architecture-specific needs. The authors propose a spatially contiguous attention design informed by that analysis.

entry.title: OccAnyScene: Towards Unified Indoor-Outdoor 3D Occupancy Predictio

author.name: Junjie Liu, Wanshui Gan, Zitong Dai, Guiping Cao, Yan Li, Ke Chen, Dongmei Jiang, Xiangyuan Lan, Jianguo Zhang

entry.summary: Defines a cross-scene 3D semantic occupancy task requiring one model to serve indoor and outdoor scenes with different cameras, voxel resolutions, ranges, and label sets, and proposes a Gaussian frustum framework built on a pretrained depth foundation model. It targets metric-consistent yet scene-adaptive image-to-3D lifting.

entry.title: Learning human joint torques from pixels

author.name: Chen Chen, Rui Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset and benchmark of over sixty thousand synchronized real-image frames with kinematics, anthropometrics, and biomechanically derived joint torque labels, enabling direct prediction of human joint torques from ordinary monocular images. This removes the need for electromyography, markers, force plates, or simulation.

entry.title: CodecArena: Codec Quality Assessment via Visual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiaye Fu, Weiqi Li, Qiankun Gao, Yanchen Zhao, Xiandong Meng, Jian Zhang, Siwei Ma, Jiaqi Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that dominant perceptual metrics reward texture plausibility over content fidelity, so generative codecs can hallucinate wrong faces or fake text and still score well. The proposed framework casts codec evaluation as source-conditioned comparative reasoning by a vision-language model optimized with reinforcement learning.

entry.title: BAG: Budget-Aware Gating for Diffusion Caching

author.name: Tong Zhao, Mingkun Lei, Yucheng Han, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a learned gating policy for caching intermediate features in diffusion transformers that jointly conditions on the remaining compute budget and the specific instance, unifying global pacing with adaptive reuse. This addresses the gap between budget-blind online heuristics and inflexible static reuse schedules.

entry.title: MemeMind: Reference-Guided Trace Construction for Offline Context Optimization

author.name: Run Yang, Weihang Wang, Boheng Sheng, Yuchen He, Jielei Zhang, Pengyu Chen, Zhiyu Wu, Qiang Sun, Huyang Sun, Longwen Gao

entry.summary: Improves offline context optimization for tool-using multimodal agents by recovering learning signal from queries where all rollouts fail: a reference answer is used to reconstruct and verify a successful tool trace, which is then added to the adaptation buffer and distilled into shared guidance and per-tool instructions. The underlying model stays frozen.

entry.title: MeanSR: Restoration Trajectory Learning for One-Step Perceptual Super-Resolution

author.name: Axi Niu, Jiawei Kou, Kang Zhang, Qingsen Yan, Jinqiu Sun, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: MeanSR learns a low-resolution-conditioned average velocity field so a single network step can map degraded inputs directly to plausible high-resolution outputs, avoiding both iterative denoising and distillation from an expensive teacher. It adds a stage-aware temporal sampling scheme and reformulates distribution trajectory matching for average-velocity generation.

entry.title: Marrying Optimal Transport and ODEs for Unified Continuous-Time 4D Reconstruction and Tracking

author.name: Liying Yang, Hao Mo, Jialun Liu, Chen Liu, Xinxing Yu, Chenhao Guan, Hui Ma, Xiao Cao, Ajian Liu, Yanyan Liang

entry.summary: Uni4R unifies dynamic 4D reconstruction and point tracking by learning a continuous velocity field through optimal transport combined with ODE integration, enabling predictions at arbitrary continuous timestamps rather than integer frames. The velocity field acts as a shared kinematic prior for both tasks.

entry.title: CIFA: Contextual-Intersectional Fairness Auditing for Hidden Subgroup Discovery in Face Analysis

author.name: Nazia Aslam, Khalid Adnan Alsayed, Thomas B. Moeslund, Kamal Nasrollahi

entry.summary: CIFA is a fairness auditing framework for face analysis that searches for hidden subgroups defined by interactions between demographic attributes and contextual factors such as blur, illumination, accessories or image quality. It shows models can look demographically fair in aggregate while failing badly on specific intersectional contexts.

entry.title: ADOPD: Reference-Privileged On-Policy Distillation for MLLM-Based Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jingtai He, Shiyuan Meng, Wenchao Meng, Qinmin Yang

entry.summary: ADOPD distills the benefits of reference-image comparison for industrial anomaly detection into a query-only multimodal LLM student, using a reference-privileged teacher and on-policy training. It explicitly guards against the teacher rewarding language-prior guesses that are not grounded in visual evidence.

entry.title: DistMoE: Private-data Rehearsal-free Routing in Mixture-of-Experts for Distributed Instruction Tuning

author.name: Mainak Singha, Niccol\`o Biondi, Elisa Ricci, Subhankar Roy

entry.summary: DistMoE performs distributed visual instruction tuning of multimodal LLMs by adding a private per-client feedforward expert alongside the shared public FFN in each decoder layer, with routing that works without rehearsal data. It addresses adaptation when data is siloed across private, domain-specific clients.

entry.title: LIRA: Local Cross-Layer Information Routing for Vision-Language-Action Decoding

author.name: Zhewei Zhang, Puyue Wang, Guanren Qiao, Yijie Weng, Jiawei Hu, Guo Li, Lujia Wang, Junyan Wang, Tao Gu, Hongliang Lu, Guiliang Liu, Hong Jia, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: LIRA reframes how vision-language features feed robot action decoders as depth-aware information routing, giving each fusion block a local window of VLM layers instead of a single fixed layer or only final-layer features. The interface between perception backbone and action head is the specific target.

entry.title: EsaacSim: A Multimodal Event Camera Add-on for NVIDIA Isaac Sim

author.name: Ignacio Bugueno-Cordova, Malte Kuhlmann, Nicol\'as Navarro-Guerrero, Miguel Campusano, Rodrigo Verschae

entry.summary: EsaacSim adds configurable event-camera simulation to NVIDIA Isaac Sim, generating grayscale and Bayer RGGB events synchronized with RGB, APS, depth, and IMU streams over native ROS2 interfaces. A motion-guided frame-gap synthesis strategy raises effective temporal resolution within the existing renderer.

entry.title: Personalized Lower-limb Exoskeleton Assistance via Preference-based Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Xiao-Yin Liu, Guotao Li, Weiqun Wang, Zeng-Guang Hou

entry.summary: Proposes a preference-based Bayesian optimization framework for tuning lower-limb exoskeleton assistance profiles to individual users while reducing the number of tiring online human-robot comparisons required. The goal is faster convergence to comfortable, effective assistance without inducing user fatigue.

entry.title: ROEVO: Robust Organized Edge Feature-based Visual Odometry Using RGB-D Cameras

author.name: Mingrui Liu, Xingxing Zuo, Renlang Huang, Minglei Zhao, Jiming Chen, Liang Li

entry.summary: ROEVO introduces organized edges, a representation that groups scattered edge pixels into sequential clusters so RGB-D visual odometry can preserve structural and textural information and perform edge-level association across frames. This enables a co-visibility graph and more robust tracking than prior edge-based odometry.

entry.title: Trajectory Divergence Horizon Decision for Reliable Dual-Arm Surgical Subtask Manipulation

author.name: Mingwu Su, Guankun Wang, Jinsong Lin, Rulin Zhou, Ziyi Hao, Zhiwei Fang, Huxin Gao, Jiewen Lai, Jiazheng Wang, Fan Zhang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Addresses the risk of fixed-length open-loop action chunks in surgical vision-language-action policies by deciding when to re-plan based on how quickly predicted trajectories diverge, applied to dual-arm surgical subtasks. It aims to limit accumulated error as the scene changes during delicate manipulation.

entry.title: SAIN: Structure-Aware Interactive Navigation with Active Dialogue Grounding for Mobile Robot

author.name: Yuhao Cao, Xiao Liu, Yang Xie, Lu Liu, Haoyao Chen

entry.summary: SAIN is a zero-shot framework for interactive instance-goal navigation that converts answers obtained through active questioning into persistent, structured spatial and object-centric state instead of consuming them as one-shot textual context. This lets a robot resolve ambiguous category-level instructions over the course of an episode.

entry.title: RoboSeg: Online Part-Level Semantic Reconstruction for Robotic Manipulation via a Single Eye-in-Hand Camera

author.name: Zhaochen Lan, Mengxiang Lin

entry.summary: RoboSeg performs online part-level semantic reconstruction from a single eye-in-hand RGB-D camera by prompting a vision-language model for functional part names, then running parallel geometry and segmentation threads to fuse part masks into a TSDF for task-oriented grasp generation. It requires no CAD models or pre-scanned meshes.

entry.title: WRAP: Wasserstein-Robust Adaptive Plug-in for Robot Localization

author.name: Minhyuk Jang, Astghik Hakobyan, Jungjin Lee, Naira Hovakimyan, Insoon Yang

entry.summary: WRAP is a filter-agnostic plug-in that supplies time-varying effective process and measurement statistics and then applies a mean-preserving Wasserstein-robust update to compute least-favorable covariances and a robust gain, without changing the propagation model or residual. On held-out UWB-IMU sequences it cut mean 3D position error substantially relative to baselines.

entry.title: Preview-Based Relative-Motion Control of an Insertion Tool for Neural-Thread Placement in Pulsating Tissue

author.name: Yongyan Cao

entry.summary: Designs a preview-based relative-motion controller for inserting neural threads into tissue that pulsates with heartbeat and breathing, estimating latency-delayed periodic surface motion, predicting it over a short horizon, and applying offset-free MPC. In simulation it reduces contact-phase placement error by roughly two orders of magnitude versus a lab-frame PD baseline, at the cost of higher peak contact force.

entry.title: Lasso Universality Under Linearly Dependent Covariates in the Sparse Regime

author.name: Soroush Mesforush, Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: Proves a Gaussian universality theorem for the lasso in the sparse regime when non-Gaussian covariates exhibit simultaneous row and column dependence, a broader dependence structure than most prior universality results allow. Numerical experiments support the theory.

entry.title: Provable Parameter-Free Fixed-Point Algorithms with Linear Convergence Rates

author.name: Quoc Tran-Dinh, Pham Ngoc Anh, Ha Manh Tien

entry.summary: Develops parameter-free and adaptive variants of the Halpern fixed-point iteration for contractive maps that need no line search, bisection, or prior knowledge of the contraction factor, with proven linear convergence for both the residual and distance to the unique fixed point. Per-iteration cost stays comparable to classical schemes.

entry.title: Does post-training quantization change welfare-relevant indicators in open-weight language models?

author.name: ashesfall

entry.summary: A pre-registration for hackathon-scale experiments testing whether post-training quantization of open-weight models changes indicators that some researchers treat as welfare-relevant, such as self-reports and behavioral consistency. The author commits publicly to the design and analysis plan before running anything, and promises to release code and data.

entry.title: FSTC-Encoder: Feature--Spatial--Temporal Correlation Learning for Generalizable RF Sensing

author.name: Jing Wang, Zhu Wang, Changlong Cheng, Yifan Guo, Yin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified encoder for heterogeneous radio-frequency sensing that models feature-structure, spatial-set and hierarchical temporal correlations so one backbone transfers across devices, environments and RF modalities. Only the feature configuration and task head change between tasks.

entry.title: Enhancing Scientific Named Entity Recognition via Large Language Models: A Type-driven Multi-task Learning Approach

author.name: Tong Bao, Yi Zhao, Heng Zhang, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: Addresses the failure of LLMs to handle long candidate type lists in scientific named entity recognition by proposing a type-driven multi-task approach that narrows and structures the type space before extraction. Targets information extraction from scientific literature.

entry.title: Agentic Anomaly Detection with ORCA-Style Dynamic Inductive Bias Adaptation in Multimodal Wearable Time Series Data

author.name: Anushka Roy, Jyotirmoy Singh, Shreea Bose, Chittaranjan Hota

entry.summary: Proposes an agentically controlled anomaly detection framework for wearable physiological time series that adapts the temporal receptive field at inference using lightweight signal statistics, instead of fixing context length per dataset. Targets nonstationary body-area-network signals under tight compute budgets.

entry.title: LoRA-based Adaptation Alone Is Not Enough: Understanding the Limits of Foundation Models for Face Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Peter Lorenz, Anjith George, Marcel S\'ebastien

entry.summary: Evaluates whether parameter-efficient adaptation of diverse vision foundation models solves the cross-dataset generalization failure of face presentation attack detection, moving beyond the CLIP-centric focus of prior work. Concludes that low-rank adaptation alone is insufficient, with performance still degrading sharply across sensors and lighting conditions.

entry.title: Reading Cognition as Decisions Unfold in Words: A Factorized Inverse Decision Model

author.name: Jiawen Kang, Dongrui Han, Xixin Wu, Helen Meng

entry.summary: Proposes a factorized inverse decision model that splits an individual's task-execution likelihood into an action factor and an effort factor with separate person-specific parameters, using a language model to turn raw verbal transcripts into structured execution traces. Evaluated on 400 older adults performing a grocery-shopping dialog task for cognitive assessment.

entry.title: Learning Structural Illumination for Unsupervised Low-light Enhancement

author.name: Tianle Du, Peiyuan He, Hainuo Wang, Tianxiu Yu, Xiaojie Guo

entry.summary: RISE separates the spatially varying relative illumination pattern from absolute exposure level in unsupervised low-light enhancement, inferring structure from reliable bright regions rather than from noisy dark ones. This avoids scene-agnostic fixed exposure targets and yields more interpretable adaptation across lighting conditions.

entry.title: EndoMD-SLAM: Endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM under Optical Degradation with Memory and Static-Transient Decomposition

author.name: Nuo Chen, Kangqi Ni, Lulin Liu, Joga Ivatury, Ying Ding, Farshid Alambeigi, Tianlong Chen, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: Presents a Gaussian splatting reconstruction framework that works directly from unposed event streams, aiming to combine the speed of feed-forward pose estimation with the fidelity normally requiring expensive SLAM-style joint optimization. It targets the accuracy-versus-cost trade-off in event-based dense 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Model the Edit, Not the Image: Visual Autoregressive Editing from a Source-Centric Perspective

author.name: Hongyi Fang, Chuwen Xie, Benjia Zhou, Yu-Xuan Qiu, Chenggong Hu, Zhibin Wang, Chao Chen, Jianbin Qin, Rui Mao

entry.summary: Reconsiders text-guided editing with next-scale visual autoregressive models from a source-centric view: rather than regenerating the target conditioned on the source, it exploits the multiscale encoding of the source image directly, avoiding inversion, test-time optimization, or user masks. This targets training-free editing efficiency.

entry.title: Right Answer, Wrong Heat: Explanation-Aware Evaluation and Thermal-Grounded Feedback for MLLMs on Infrared Images

author.name: Yongsong Huang, Xiaofeng Liu, Tomo Miyazaki, Yaohou Fan, Shinichiro Omachi

entry.summary: Shows that multimodal language models scored only on answer accuracy for infrared images can be right for the wrong reasons, with explanations grounded in visible-light-like cues rather than thermal evidence. A dual-judge evaluation framework separates answer correctness, explanation groundedness, and true thermal grounding, and finds accuracy barely drops when the infrared image is withheld.

entry.title: RefineAny3D: Depth Refinement as Semantic Alignment for Monocular 3D Detection

author.name: Zhihao Zhang, Gengwei Zhang, Tianlong Chen, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: Finds that swapping in a state-of-the-art zero-shot depth foundation model actually degrades monocular 3D detection compared with a detector's own depth, because such models lack object-level metric precision. The authors therefore treat object-level depth refinement as a separate task solved by a vision-language model that corrects depth via semantic alignment.

entry.title: PatchHead: Learning Spatial Patch Evidence for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Shengbo Qi, Hongyi Fang, Benjia Zhou, Rui Mao

entry.summary: Argues that AI-generated image detectors built on the global class token of self-supervised vision backbones discard spatially distributed generation traces, and adds a lightweight spatial aggregation head over patch tokens with adapter tuning on a frozen backbone. The goal is better generalization to unseen generators and datasets.

entry.title: DH-VLM: Dual-Horizon Cooperative Latent Reasoning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Ziyi Song, Chen Xia, Hang Yu, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: DH-VLM enables asymmetric cooperation between roadside infrastructure and an ego vehicle, with the infrastructure aggregating a long-horizon semantic view and the vehicle performing short-horizon latent reasoning, to overcome occlusion and on-board compute limits. The design targets practical deployment constraints of large driving models.

entry.title: NL2SHACL-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for Natural Language to SHACL Translation

author.name: Yuchen Zhou, Niels Bobet, Maribel Acosta

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark suite for translating natural-language requirements into SHACL shape constraints for validating RDF knowledge graphs, together with semantics-aware evaluation that goes beyond string matching. Four frontier LLMs are evaluated, showing strong syntactic generation but weaker semantic fidelity.

entry.title: Guixu: Valuation-Driven Data Discovery for Autonomous AI Agents with On-Chain Attestation

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yuchen Peng, Jiaqi Chai, Yufei Qian, Xilin Li, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: Describes a data discovery system for autonomous agents that estimates task-specific dataset utility through proxy-label propagation, selects datasets under budget via multi-round knapsack optimization, and records usage feedback with on-chain attestation and agentic payment. It targets the gap between retrieval-oriented dataset search and value-aware acquisition.

entry.title: KGCache: Amortized Subgraph Retrieval for KG Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Uros Stanic, Changcheng Yuan, Sabuj Laskar, Ariful Azad

entry.summary: Observes that knowledge graph question answering systems repeatedly query the same one-hop neighborhoods across different questions and introduces an in-memory neighborhood cache placed between the QA engine and the graph backend. It is compatible with both iterative traversal and one-shot planning KGQA paradigms and is evaluated on standard KGQA datasets.

entry.title: VDGR-RAG: Vectors, Directories, Graphs, and Reflection Are All You Need for Unified Reasoning over Hierarchical Enterprise Knowledge

author.name: Wenqi Chen, Haofei Yang, Rui Yang, Fangming Li

entry.summary: Combines vector retrieval, directory-structure-driven reasoning, graph traversal, and iterative reflection into a unified agentic GraphRAG system for enterprise question answering over hierarchical product documentation. It targets poor domain routing and underuse of document hierarchy in existing RAG stacks.

entry.title: FitAQA: A Benchmark of Fitness Action Quality Assessment for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kaili Zheng, Kaiwen Wang, Xun Zhu, Qingyuan Yang, Chenyi Guo, Ji Wu

entry.summary: FitAQA evaluates multimodal LLMs on fitness action quality assessment with 2,219 videos and 5,512 question instances across 30 bodyweight exercises, using an expert-designed taxonomy of 38 recurring form errors across six quality dimensions. Unlike prior action-quality benchmarks it probes how models reason about form rather than just final scores. Reveals gaps in fine-grained temporal and biomechanical video understanding.

entry.title: PROSLEX: A Novel Dataset for Expert-Annotated Legal Statute Prediction for Indian Judiciary

author.name: Subinay Adhikary, Upal Bhattacharya, Vivek Kumar Singh, Anurag Sharma, Shubham Kumar Nigam, Suvasis Das, Shouvik Kumar Guha, Koustav Rudra, Kripabandhu Ghosh

entry.summary: PROSLEX is an expert-annotated dataset of 1,623 Indian legal documents for predicting applicable statutes along with the explanations justifying each prediction, moving beyond accuracy-only multi-label classification. The emphasis on justifiable reasoning reflects judicial requirements for explainability. Valuable resource for legal NLP in an underserved jurisdiction.

entry.title: Decoding Phenotypes: A Framework for Fusing Genomic Language Models and Neuroimaging

author.name: Tianli Tao, Ziyang Wang, Emma Robinson, Rachel Sparks, Le Zhang

entry.summary: GeneFuse fuses representations from pretrained genomic language models with neuroimaging features, using feature-wise modulation conditioned on genotype instead of encoding variants as hard labels that discard local sequence context. The goal is better multimodal diagnosis for nervous system diseases. It is a reasonable architectural contribution to imaging-genetics integration.

entry.title: CoRCi: Cross-Reconstruction of Coherent Interests Modeling in Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Qingtian Bian, Tieying Li, Marcus de Carvalho, Jiaxing Xu, Hui Fang, Yiping Ke

entry.summary: CoRCi tackles cross-domain sequential recommendation by reconstructing coherent user interests across domains rather than training separate encoders on mixed and per-domain sequences with aggregated losses, which the authors argue amplifies inter-domain discrepancy. Aims to preserve domain-invariant interest coherence.

entry.title: Cross-Model Humor Preference Modeling with Cards Against Humanity

author.name: Victor Winter, Farhan Lakhany

entry.summary: Tests whether one LLM can model another LLM's humor preferences in a Cards Against Humanity style binary selection task, using a stability procedure to isolate hands where two models deterministically disagree. Conditions escalate from generic instructions to showing prior selections with rationales, measuring whether preference modeling improves.

entry.title: FreSH: Frequency-Segmented Hierarchical Multi-Expert Framework for Multivariate Time Series Classification

author.name: Pingping Liu, Muyao Wang, Zijian Zhang, Tongshun Zhang, Hao Miao, Guorui Xie, Qingliang Li, Qiuzhan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes a frequency-segmented hierarchical mixture-of-experts architecture for multivariate time series classification that lets different experts specialise on different spectral bands and scales while a global module supplies context. Aims to handle class imbalance and efficiency constraints together.

entry.title: RAG-Based Auto-Configuration for Industrial Fieldbus Devices

author.name: Aadil Gani Ganie, Saad Ezzini, Naveed Farooz Marazi

entry.summary: Automates industrial device commissioning by retrieving parameters from heterogeneous PDF manuals with a hybrid dense-sparse index augmented by an industrial ontology graph, then having a local LLM emit ontology-aligned JSON-LD configurations with a repair loop. Covers four fieldbus protocols in a production-oriented pipeline.

entry.title: Two-Step MV-DeepONet: Probabilistic Operator Learning for Uncertainty Propagation Driven by Random Input Fields

author.name: Yupei Nie, Lei Wang, Jiasen Liu

entry.summary: Extends probabilistic DeepONet to capture cross-location conditional dependence by a two-step mean-variance training scheme, rather than assuming diagonal predictive covariance. Targets forward uncertainty propagation in physical systems driven by random input fields.

entry.title: GRASP: Granularity-Aware Region Alignment and Semantic Prototype Learning for Fine-Grained Cross-Modal Understanding in Drone Views

author.name: Jiahui Cui, Yan Zhao, Kan Wei, Enze Zhu, Peirong Zhang, Lei Wang, Yiru Wang

entry.summary: GRASP tackles fine-grained drone-view vision-language grounding, where wide fields of view cause the model to match global scene similarity instead of the target object, and where candidates share near-identical geometry. It combines granularity-aware region alignment with semantic prototype learning.

entry.title: How Simple Can It Get? From Interpretable Equations to Readable Rules for Financial Decision Making

author.name: Adia Lumadjeng, Ilker Birbil, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Starts from an interpretable single-equation classifier and progressively simplifies it into pruned monomials, directional if-then rules, and integer scorecards of the kind finance already deploys, measuring exactly what accuracy each simplification costs. Across four financial datasets pruning is reported to be nearly free while further simplification degrades performance.

entry.title: Exact Rank-Space KL Projection for Shared-Marginal Low-Rank Factors: Application to Doubly Stochastic Clustering

author.name: Enliang Hu

entry.summary: Derives an exact Kullback-Leibler projection for nonnegative low-rank factorizations with fixed row marginals and a shared learned column marginal, reducing to a strictly convex dual with only r minus one variables and matrix-free Hessian products. Applies the geometry to doubly stochastic graph learning without ever materializing the dense affinity matrix.

entry.title: Multi-kernel spectral clustering: Entrywise eigenvector perturbation bounds and exact recovery

author.name: Zeqin Lin, Guangming Pan, Zhixiang Zhang, Yinbing Zhou

entry.summary: Analyzes kernel spectral clustering that aggregates multiple bandwidths chosen as empirical quantiles of pairwise distances, addressing data with several characteristic distance scales in high dimensions. The paper provides entrywise eigenvector perturbation bounds and exact recovery conditions under a heterogeneous multi-scale mixture model.

entry.title: Inductive Graph Layout with Implicit Neural Fields

author.name: Berfin Inal, Daniel Probst

entry.summary: Replaces the usual table of free node coordinates in graph drawing with a small neural network that maps landmark distances to plane positions, giving layouts a sample complexity and an extensible domain. This makes stress minimization tractable without materializing the quadratic distance matrix and allows new nodes to be placed inductively.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning in Network Interdiction Games

author.name: Luca M. Hartmann, Parinaz Naghizadeh

entry.summary: Shows a structural failure of decision-focused learning in shortest-path network interdiction games: many cost estimators achieve zero nominal decision loss yet break under interdiction, so the usual advantage over prediction-focused learning reverses. The paper characterizes this decision-equivalence class and proposes a remedy.

entry.title: Walk-on-Spheres Monte Carlo and deep neural network approximations of elliptic PDEs with drift and killing

author.name: Konrad Kleinberg, Thomas Kruse

entry.summary: Develops Monte Carlo estimators based on a modified walk-on-spheres scheme for linear elliptic PDEs with constant diffusion, drift, and killing, and proves uniform error bounds with sample complexity growing only polynomially in dimension and inverse accuracy. Also establishes a deep neural network approximation result for the same solutions.

entry.title: Financial Numerical Prediction and Allocation as Token Generation

author.name: Xu Ouyang, Moontae Lee

entry.summary: Tests whether a causal language model can emit financial forecasts and portfolio weights directly as constrained token sequences, removing task-specific regression or policy heads. The system generates volatility-standardized return tokens for stock forecasting and normalized long-only weights for a five-ETF allocation task, trained with ordinal, ranking, and policy-style objectives.

entry.title: Jako Tako or Fluent? Presenting PoVisLE: A Polish Vision-Language Evaluation

author.name: Anna Ko{\l}os, Grzegorz Statkiewicz, Karolina Seweryn, Katarzyna Kowol, Karolina Piosek, Wojciech Kusa

entry.summary: Presents a Polish monocultural vision-language benchmark designed to probe culturally grounded visual understanding, symbolic content, and pragmatic interpretation rather than surface-level object recognition. Aims to expose failures of English-centric VLMs on region-specific meaning.

entry.title: Security and Privacy Taxonomy Generation from Mobile App Reviews

author.name: Moghis Fereidouni, Vinaik Chhetri, Umar Farooq, A. B. Siddique

entry.summary: Filters over 600,000 mobile app reviews for privacy and security content and introduces a pipeline that constructs taxonomies at a scale where existing LLM and clustering methods, designed for a few thousand scientific documents, break down. Produces a continuously updatable taxonomy of user-reported privacy and security concerns.

entry.title: The Transparency Trap: How AI Disclaimers Create Overconfidence in High-Stakes Decisions

author.name: Neil Todkar

entry.summary: An experimental study of how AI disclaimer placement and persuasive framing affect trust and perceived accuracy across finance, medicine, and AI-generated content, using 378 stimulus responses from 52 participants. Advisory content was trusted even when disclaimers were shown, suggesting disclaimers may fail as risk communication.

entry.title: EvalConvoLearn: An Open-Source Framework for Evaluating Grounded Learner Simulations in Tutoring Conversations

author.name: Baptiste Moreau-Pernet

entry.summary: EvalConvoLearn is an open framework for judging whether LLM-simulated students reproduce real learner behavior, scoring both mastery outcomes and conversational features such as talk moves, error distributions, and turn length. It aims to validate simulated learners used to test tutors and teachable agents.

entry.title: VeriForge: Mitigating Latent Knowledge Gaps in Narrative Drafting via Mixed-Initiative Scaffolding

author.name: Ruqi Sun, Jiaping Li, Wenhui Tao, Ximing Zheng, Yuefeng Tan, Jiahao Wei, Yuxin Ma

entry.summary: VeriForge is a mixed-initiative writing tool that surfaces domain knowledge gaps fiction authors do not know how to query for, while leaving the actual prose to the writer. It is grounded in formative interviews with nine fiction writers and emphasizes preserving authorial voice and agency.

entry.title: Ghost Features and Spooky Transfer Learning for Hypercomplex-Valued Neural Networks

author.name: Guilherme Vieira Neto, Marcos Eduardo Valle

entry.summary: The paper builds hypercomplex-valued network layers whose real part reproduces a standard real-valued layer, so the extra imaginary components produce additional ghost features. These ghost features can be grafted into an already-trained network through a transfer procedure the authors call spooky transfer learning.

entry.title: LAD-COD: Language-Aligned Dense Perception for Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Shangye Song, Tianzhi Zhu, Syed Ariff Syed Hesham, Xin He, Yun Liu

entry.summary: LAD-COD improves camouflaged object detection by pushing language-conditioned semantics into the dense visual features rather than only into the mask decoder, so low-contrast cues are preserved. It builds on large multimodal segmentation systems that use instruction-derived target embeddings.

entry.title: PE-Mamba: Bidirectional Selective Layer Aggregation for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Kutub Uddin, Nusrat Tasnim, Khalid Malik

entry.summary: PE-Mamba detects AI-generated images by aggregating features across transformer layers with a bidirectional selective state-space module rather than a simple weighted sum, respecting the progression from shallow texture to deep semantics. It uses a pretrained vision encoder with lightweight LoRA adaptation.

entry.title: When Does An Extra View Help? Adapting Single-View 3D Reconstruction with Extra Imagery

author.name: Y Huynh, Duc Thanh Nguyen, Thao Minh Le, Mohamed Abdelrazek

entry.summary: ASV3D adapts a pretrained single-view 3D reconstruction model at test time when one extra image happens to be available, offering both a zero-shot scheme and an optimized adaptation variant. It addresses the absence of a mechanism to fold an additional view into single-view reconstruction pipelines.

entry.title: BAP-MOS: Bandit-Based Adaptive Prompting for Boundary-Sensitive Multi-Organ Segmentation

author.name: Satvik Praveen, Shengji Jin, Ahmed Lamidi, Xin Qian, Yi Sheng

entry.summary: BAP-MOS treats prompt selection for promptable multi-organ ultrasound segmentation as a per-organ multi-armed bandit over box, point, and combined prompts, wrapped in an outer hyperparameter search loop. The reward combines Dice with boundary-sensitive distance metrics to target localized errors that Dice alone hides.

entry.title: Linguistically-Aligned and Visually-Grounded Preference Optimization for Clinically-Augmented Medical Report Generation

author.name: Qiang Hu, Yuxuan Luo, Yingjie Guo, Hao Wang, Qimei Wang, Qiang Li, Zhiwei Wang

entry.summary: Improves preference optimization for medical report generation by constructing preference pairs that isolate clinical findings from irrelevant stylistic differences and by adding explicit visual grounding to the DPO objective. The aim is to reduce factual hallucination in generated radiology reports.

entry.title: ERF-GS: Reconstructing Fast Motion from Disjoint Event-RGB Viewpoints

author.name: Xiaoyang Bai, Zhenyang Li, Weiwei Xu, Edmund Y. Lam, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: Fuses event-camera data with RGB frames captured from separate, non-aligned viewpoints into a Gaussian splatting pipeline, injecting event evidence into both optimization and densification to reconstruct fast-moving objects. The disjoint-viewpoint setting relaxes the usual requirement for co-located hybrid sensors.

entry.title: LogiShot: Logically Coherent Cross-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Shuai Guo, Yuhang Yang, Zeyu Zhang, Pengfei Yu, Wei Zhai, Yang Cao, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: Addresses logical coherence across shots in multi-shot video generation, where individual clips look plausible but do not fit the overall narrative when instructions are underspecified. The framework establishes explicit cross-shot logical links alongside visual consistency preservation.

entry.title: Zero-shot 2D Grounding with Novel Affordance Types

author.name: Haomeng Zhang, Raymond A. Yeh

entry.summary: Defines a zero-shot task and benchmark for grounding affordance types never seen in training, and shows that a training-free method exploiting segmentation cues works well because affordance regions correlate strongly with object subparts. A trainable variant that learns to combine those cues improves results further.

entry.title: NBA_Streaming: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Fine-Grained Basketball Commentary Generation in Continuous Streams

author.name: Lifang Wu, Yuyang Wu, Yangdong Gao, Fengyu Liu, Ya Jing, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark of roughly 300 hours of basketball broadcast video with about 35 thousand temporally aligned events annotated for player identity, fine-grained action, event attributes, and event chains, aimed at online commentary generation in continuous streams. It stresses deciding when an event is observable enough to describe before the next one occurs.

entry.title: One Model to Magnify Them All: Efficient Scale-Invariant Histopathology via Conditional Normalization and Continuous Magnification Training

author.name: Agnieszka Florkowska, Henning M\"uller, Marek Wodzinski

entry.summary: The paper proposes Conditional Layer Normalization so that a single histopathology model can operate across continuously varying slide magnifications rather than the discrete resolutions used in training. This replaces ensembles of magnification-specific models with one lightweight conditioning mechanism.

entry.title: SC$^{2}$-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments

author.name: Xuan Yao, Yuze Zhu, Junyu Gao, Zongmeng Wang, Changsheng Xu

entry.summary: SC2-WM adds internal closed-loop feedback to vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments: world-model foresight is used to refine plans before actions execute, and the world model itself can be selectively updated at test time when feedback signals drift. It targets the lack of drift detection in open-loop navigation policies.

entry.title: SG-WAM: Text-Grounded and Spatial-aware Semantic Guidance for World-Action Models

author.name: Junjie He, Junfeng Li, Zhide Zhong, Haodong Yan, Ruixin Li, Yangyang Zheng, Jiaguan Zhu, Tianran Zhang, Yuqiao Du, Wen Chen, Shunbo Zhou, Haoang Li

entry.summary: SG-WAM uses a vision-language model as a semantic planner so that world-action models for manipulation ground their predicted futures in the language instruction rather than mainly in visual cues, adding spatial awareness to the guidance. The motivation is that off-the-shelf text encoders embed instructions independently of observations, causing instruction-video misalignment and worse actions.

entry.title: DiffSafeMerge: Mitigating Backdoor Inheritance in Diffusion Model Merging

author.name: Jiayang Zhang, Ji Guo, Jiachen Li, Wenshu Fan, Wenbo Jiang

entry.summary: DiffSafeMerge mitigates inheritance of dormant backdoors when merging unconditional diffusion checkpoints, using a small clean unlabeled set and attack-agnostic stress probes to score and attenuate suspicious blocks toward a trusted reference under a clean-loss budget. It is evaluated across four attacks, two datasets and 21 target conditions.

entry.title: FactorDrive: Adaptive Multi-Step Reasoning Driven by Planning-Critical Factors for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Guolei Huang, Tengfei She, Yuxuan Lu, Yao Huang, Yuqi Ye, Yongjun Shen

entry.summary: FactorDrive is an end-to-end driving framework in which a vision-language model performs adaptive multi-step reasoning conditioned on planning-critical factors, following large-scale driving instruction tuning and post-training that optimizes the reasoning path for planning quality. It targets weak integration of spatial-physical evidence and coarse reasoning adaptation in existing VLM drivers.

entry.title: Hierarchical Topology-Aware Planning and Control of Underwater Vehicle-Manipulator Systems in Confined Environments

author.name: Mohamed Abdelwahab, Ruggero Carli, Damiano Varagnolo, Alberto Dalla Libera

entry.summary: MANTA is a three-layer planning and control stack for underwater vehicle-manipulator systems in confined spaces, reasoning first about corridor connectivity in a reduced base space, then jointly optimizing base and arm trajectories, then closing the loop during execution. It explicitly guards against entering unrecoverable regions in cluttered, partially known environments.

entry.title: UnsDrive: Towards Robust End-to-End Autonomous Driving in Unstructured Scenes

author.name: Nanxin Zeng, Ruiqi Song, Xiangyu Guo, Baiyong Ding, Yunfeng Ai

entry.summary: UnsDrive is an end-to-end driving planner for unstructured mining environments that builds an occupancy representation explicitly distinguishing occupied, free, and unknown space from multi-frame visibility cues, then conditions a flow-matching planner on it to generate multimodal trajectories. The emphasis is safe planning under heavy occlusion and degraded visibility.

entry.title: Ultra-Low-Impedance Robotic Gripper for High-Bandwidth and Transparent Physical Interaction

author.name: Joon Lee, Ari Choi, Seokhwan Jeong

entry.summary: Describes a nine-DOF three-fingered gripper using direct-drive motors with a low-ratio differential transmission, centralizing actuator mass at the base so moving links stay light while paired motors amplify flexion torque. The design achieves useful grasp force without high-friction gearing or external force sensors, enabling transparent high-bandwidth interaction.

entry.title: Entropic Partial Optimal Transport and Partial Gromov--Wasserstein Distance between Gaussian Mixtures

author.name: Toshiaki Yachimura, Xiaocheng Zou

entry.summary: Extends entropic partial optimal transport to Gaussian mixture models and defines a partial mixture Gromov-Wasserstein distance, proving existence and uniqueness of minimizers plus large-penalty estimates, with couplings inducing continuous transport plans via Gaussian optimal maps. Partial formulations tolerate outliers, missing parts, and only partially overlapping data.

entry.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: Models which LLM agents to activate and which communication edges to open as a cooperative game with task-conditioned utility minus activation and per-edge costs. Proposes a marginal-value activation rule, a greedy router, and Shapley-value estimates to predict which agents are worth contacting.

entry.title: A Structural Dynamics Graph World Model: Unified Modeling, Constrained Rollout, and Interpretable Calibration

author.name: Wei Wang, Yaosen Chen, Han Yang, Yuegen Liu, Mingli Luo, Xinxin Jiao, Xuming Wen, Ming Liu

entry.summary: SD-GWM is a graph world model that separates node self-dynamics, edge coupling, domain conservation constraints and a bounded learned residual, so mechanisms remain auditable and mature domain solvers can be reused. A global projection maps predicted states back into the feasible set to enforce constraints during rollout. Aimed at interpretable, constraint-respecting simulation of complex physical systems.

entry.title: From Prompt to Harness: Coderlet from Scratch

author.name: Mengfan Li

entry.summary: A design study of a minimal coding-agent harness, tracing a single request through context formation, model decision, environment action, observation return, and state continuation, and identifying model, execution, and state as the three key boundaries. Argues harness organization, not the model alone, determines agent behavior.

entry.title: Frequency-Domain Dual-Branch Fusion for Medical Visual Question Answering

author.name: Yusra Tariq, Rakesh Chandra Joshi

entry.summary: Adds a dual-branch fusion module for medical visual question answering that performs question-conditioned spectral filtering, selecting global low-frequency structure or fine high-frequency detail before returning to the spatial domain. Motivated by subtle lesion texture and boundary cues that spatial fusion may miss.

entry.title: Abstracted Away: Resisting Alienation and Ungrounded Abstraction in AI Research Communities

author.name: Vyoma Raman, Isabel O. Gallegos, Neha Srivathsa

entry.summary: A position and reflection piece in which three early-career critical AI researchers describe alienation produced by abstraction norms in computational AI research, where legitimacy standards detach from lived experience of harm and career incentives crowd out critique. Proposes resistance practices for grounding research in context.

entry.title: How Far Do Foundation Models Transfer to Infant Signals? A Cross-Dataset Transfer Audit with a Unified Need Ontology

author.name: Wu Hangyu

entry.summary: Audits cross-dataset transfer of frozen audio foundation-model encoders on infant cry classification under a unified five-class need ontology, with byte- and embedding-level leakage screening. Finds within-corpus scores swing wildly, cross-corpus transfer is negative on average, and hundreds of duplicate clip groups inflate reported performance.

entry.title: MARA: Flow-Matching-Guided Multi-Agent Resource Allocation for Computational Resource Efficient Learning

author.name: Hanye Zhao, Muning Wen, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: MARA allocates discrete compute nodes among concurrent training jobs with unknown effort requirements by forecasting loss trajectories with conditional flow matching and coordinating nodes via a cooperative multi-agent autoregressive policy. A potential-based progress reward shapes the sequential allocation decisions.

entry.title: Monotonicity-Guided Bottom-Up Petri Net Discovery: The SPECpp Framework

author.name: Leah Tacke genannt Unterberg, Lisa L. Mannel, Wil M. P. van der Aalst

entry.summary: Presents SPECpp, a bottom-up Petri net discovery framework that exploits monotonic properties of individual places to prune an exponential candidate space, letting concurrency, choice, and long-term dependencies emerge instead of assuming predefined constructs. Contrasts with top-down inductive mining approaches.

entry.title: Structure-Enhanced Features and Quality-Aware Dynamic Anchor Scoring for Robust Lane Detection

author.name: Weize Cai, Yongqi Dong, Zhida Shao, Yichen Liu, Zixin Fu

entry.summary: A lane detection method that adds gated horizontal-vertical token features to preserve structural continuity of partially occluded lane markings and rescoring of anchors by line-level localization quality rather than classification confidence alone. It keeps the inference pipeline of an existing anchor decomposition detector.

entry.title: Rethinking Learning-Based Influence Maximization: Simple Neural Surrogates and Native Discrete Search

author.name: Yiqiao Liao, Parinaz Naghizadeh

entry.summary: SIMBA argues that learning-based influence maximization does not need heavy neural machinery: it pairs uniformly anchored node embeddings and a two-layer GNN surrogate with batched multi-swap simulated annealing over discrete seed sets. Compute shifts from representation learning to direct combinatorial search.

entry.title: Approximation Rates for Metaplectic Neural Networks

author.name: Ahmed Abdeljawad, Marcello Carioni, Elena Cordero

entry.summary: Extends Barron space theory to dictionaries built from metaplectic operators, a symplectic generalization of the Fourier transform, and proves Monte-Carlo style approximation rates for shallow networks over these atoms. A deep architecture using metaplectic atoms as building blocks is proposed as validation.

entry.title: RAVEN: Frozen Random Graph Reservoirs with Physics-Informed Interaction Fingerprints for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction

author.name: Qingyang Zou, Jiaye Huang, Hangbo Xie, Jiayue Yin, Youyi Song, Jinfeng Liu

entry.summary: RAVEN predicts protein-ligand binding affinity using an ensemble of randomly initialized and completely frozen atomistic graph encoders as a reservoir, combined with a deterministic physicochemical interaction fingerprint. Avoiding end-to-end representation optimization is intended to counter small, heterogeneous and partition-sensitive structure-affinity data.

entry.title: Online Learning of Scale Parameters in Score-Driven Filters

author.name: Fabrizio Lillo, Giulia Livieri, Gianluca Palmari

entry.summary: Treats the gain that scales the likelihood score in score-driven time series filters as an online decision variable optimized against a Kullback-Leibler predictive objective. Shows that for a scalar unscaled gain, the negative product of consecutive scores is the stochastic gradient of this loss, giving a simple online update rule.

entry.title: Label Granularity Skew in Federated Learning with Hierarchical Image Classification

author.name: Jaeheon Kim, Hokeun Kim, Bong Jun Choi

entry.summary: Introduces label granularity skew, a form of federated heterogeneity where clients annotate at different levels of a shared class taxonomy rather than differing only in class distribution. Client-specific hierarchies are simulated with a probabilistic relational neighbor classifier and a WordNet-guided coarsening procedure.

entry.title: Flow-based conditional cardiac anatomy generation for virtual cohorts

author.name: Konstantinos Kevopoulos, Beatrice Moscoloni, Benjamin Alheit, Cameron Beeche, Julio A. Chirinos, Alexander Heinlein, Mathias Peirlinck

entry.summary: CAN-FLOW is a two-step conditional flow-based generator for cardiac anatomies that decouples representation learning from metadata conditioning, unlike conditional variational autoencoders that entangle both in a shared regularized latent prior. The goal is virtual patient cohorts that preserve realistic metadata-dependent anatomical variability for digital twin studies.

entry.title: Hierarchical rank-evolving representation for physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Ruoyang Su, Xi-Le Zhao, Kun Li, Liang Li

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical rank-evolving tensor representation for physics-informed neural networks that determines ranks automatically instead of relying on manually tuned pre-specified low-rank decompositions. This aims to capture the structure of multivariate PDE solutions more faithfully.

entry.title: Generalized Convexity and Smoothness via Conjugate Duality: Optimization Theory for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Binchuan Qi

entry.summary: Generalizes convexity and smoothness through Legendre functions and convex conjugation, introducing notions that cover convex and nonconvex, smooth and nonsmooth objectives in one formalism. The aim is an optimization theory that better explains why stochastic gradient descent works for deep network training.

entry.title: Recurrent Neural Networks Beyond Time: Learning from Multiple Ordered Projections

author.name: Vagan Terziyan, Artur Terziian, Oleksandra Vitko

entry.summary: Argues that recurrence is about ordering rather than time, and proposes training separate sequence models on multiple admissible orderings (projections) of the same data before fusing their representations. The claimed benefit is capturing structural dependencies that any single ordering hides.

entry.title: Fairness in Link Prediction Beyond Demographic Parity: A Reproducibility Study

author.name: Valentijn Oldenburg, Floris de Kam, Stef de Wildt, Jarno Nilson Balk

entry.summary: A reproducibility study confirming that demographic parity misses exposure bias in ranked link prediction because it ignores rank position, while a rank-aware normalized discounted KL divergence detects it. The authors also replicate a post-processing debiasing method and stress-test robustness on synthetic homophily settings.

entry.title: Exploiting chemical shift variability enables recovery of overlapping metabolites from 1H nuclear magnetic resonance spectra

author.name: Jesper L{\o}ve Hinrich, Pia Susan Mayer, Bekzod Khakimov, S{\o}ren Balling Engelsen, Morten M{\o}rup

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian shift-invariant non-negative matrix factorization that treats sample-dependent chemical shift variability in proton NMR spectra as informative rather than as noise. It recovers overlapping metabolite signals missed by existing pipelines across simulations, lab-created mixtures, and a large urine cohort.

entry.title: Stochastic gradient descent with discontinuity across a manifold

author.name: Vivek S. Borkar

entry.summary: Analyzes stochastic gradient descent when the loss is discontinuous across lower-dimensional manifolds, using the differential-equation (stochastic approximation) limit. This addresses a regime where standard smoothness-based SGD theory does not apply.

entry.title: Embedding Initialization for Unseen Low-resource Languages in Multilingual NMT: A Case Study on Limbum-English Translation

author.name: Samiratu Ntohsi, Neza David Tuyishimire, Anesu Kafesu, Marvin Ogore, Samuel Oluwajunwonlo Babalola, Oche Ankeli

entry.summary: Addresses how to pick or build a language token when adapting a massively multilingual translation model to an unseen language, proposing initialization by averaging embeddings of typologically related languages. The case study is Limbum-to-English with fewer than 9,000 parallel sentences.

entry.title: Classical $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Models Match or Exceed Shallow Variational Quantum Circuits on Vision Benchmarks

author.name: Christopher Fulton, Irene Tsapara, Lawrence Fulton

entry.summary: Compares real-valued, quaternion-valued, and variational quantum classification heads on identical frozen features across three vision benchmarks. Quaternion networks nearly match real-valued baselines and outperform shallow product-state quantum circuits, undercutting claims of quantum advantage from SU(2) structure alone.

entry.title: MotionCraft: Latent World Modeling with Sparse Attention for Visual Upscaling

author.name: Rong Fu, Chunlei Meng, Yangchen Zeng, Xiaowen Ma, Yongtai Liu, Wangyu Wu, Shuo Yin, Zijian Zhang, Sicheng Li, Yingrui Ji, Chenhao Wang, Simon Fong

entry.summary: MotionCraft approaches video super-resolution as latent world modeling with sparse attention, aiming to reconcile local detail fidelity, long-range spatio-temporal coherence, perceptual realism, and compute cost. It positions itself against convolutional alignment, transformer, and diffusion-based upscalers.

entry.title: PreGress: Ranking-Native Pre-training and Prompting for Graph Node Ranking

author.name: Lujie Ban, Jiasheng shi, Yingli Zhou, Kaiwen Xue, Daiyin Wang, Xubin Li, Shuanghua Li, Chenhao Ma

entry.summary: PreGress introduces ranking-native pre-training and prompting for graph node ranking, arguing that existing graph pre-training objectives are misaligned with ranking and that GNN rankers must be retrained per criterion. The aim is transferable approximation of expensive ranking measures across tasks without retraining.

entry.title: Gated Spatial Redundancy Projection for Pathology Transformer Attentions

author.name: Zhiyuan Yang, Jiahao Cheng, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: Identifies local spatial redundancy in whole-slide pathology images as a specific failure mode of self-attention, where near-identical neighbouring patches wash out subtle diagnostic signals. The authors add a lightweight gated projection module that removes the local redundancy direction from attention outputs, usable as a drop-in fix in existing pathology transformers.

entry.title: Goal-oriented Navigation Instruction Generation with Tour Video Priors

author.name: Fangdi Li, Juncheng Liao, Changxu Cheng, Jiazhi Wang, Senda Chen, Tao Wang, Wuyue Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a goal-oriented task in which navigation instructions must be generated from an egocentric tour video, an initial observation, and a goal, without access to the intermediate route. This requires genuine spatial reasoning rather than captioning a demonstrated trajectory.

entry.title: IDATA: Scalable Invertible Diffusion for Unrestricted Adversarial Transfer Attack

author.name: Yi Pan, Jun-Jie Huang, Tianrui Liu, Zihan Chen, Lin Liu, Zhao Wentao

entry.summary: Proposes a memory-efficient diffusion-based unrestricted adversarial attack that replaces multi-step backpropagation through the sampler with an invertible formulation and constrains perturbations in the low-frequency band. It is aimed at stress-testing the black-box robustness of visual models.

entry.title: UniMoFlow: Grounding Instruction-Driven 3D Human Motion Editing in Generation

author.name: Yilei Hua, Beibei Jing, Ce Zheng, Hanyu Zhou, Yawei Luo, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Grounds instruction-driven 3D human motion editing inside text-to-motion generation across data, architecture, and inference, and contributes a large synthesized-and-verified editing dataset spanning body-part, amplitude, temporal, and action-level modifications. It targets precise spatiotemporal localization while preserving unedited motion content.

entry.title: OnEvoMemory: Evolving Memory through Online Robot Rollouts for Pretrained Robot Policies

author.name: Zhongxi Chen, Shenqi Zong

entry.summary: OnEvoMemory is a value-guided memory module for pretrained robot policies that keeps recent context, high-value experiences, and salient transitions, learning what to retain from trajectory outcomes and refining selection using online successes and failures. It helps long-horizon policies recognize stage transitions and avoid redoing completed subtasks.

entry.title: Beyond the Plane: Coupling Planar Vehicle Dynamics with Three-Dimensional Road Geometry

author.name: Simon Sagmeister, Phillip Pitschi, Nico Haja, Markus Lienkamp

entry.summary: Shows that three-dimensional road geometry can raise tire normal loads by well over half compared with nominal standstill values on a real speedway, and proposes a way to couple planar vehicle dynamics models with 3D road geometry without the cost of full 3D multibody simulation. This improves fidelity for localization and control development.

entry.title: Tether-Inertial Localization for Planetary Drones

author.name: Dielof van Loon, Anton Bredenbeck, Lennart Puck, Martin Azkarate, Salua Hamaza

entry.summary: Proposes localizing a tethered planetary drone relative to its base rover using tether length and angle measurements fused with inertial data, combining an efficient analytical catenary model with filtering. Tethering offloads power and compute to the rover while turning the cable into a non-drifting position reference.

entry.title: IntelliAudit: Using Large Language Models to Evaluate Audit Controls

author.name: Allison Wilson, Sina Moradi Sabet, Diar Shakimov, Panteha Shahrivar, Mohammad Reza Bagheri, Dean Konenkamp, Mohammad A. Tayebi

entry.summary: Describes a retrieval-grounded multi-agent system for IT audit that gathers evidence across policies and operational artifacts, generates an assessment, has an adversarial agent challenge adverse findings, adjudicates disagreements, and outputs cited recommendations. It targets evidentiary sufficiency judgments that keyword matching cannot handle.

entry.title: Exploring LLM Capabilities for Situational Understanding and COLREG compliance on real-world maritime navigation scenarios

author.name: Julius Wirbel, P. Nicholas Hansen, Line K. H. Clemmensen, Roberto Galeazzi

entry.summary: The authors build a 50-scenario dataset from real AIS ship traffic labeled with applicable collision regulation rules, recommended maneuvers and rationales, then test a range of LLMs on maritime situational understanding and good seamanship. Results probe whether models can combine codified rules with uncodified professional practice. It is an early, domain-grounded feasibility assessment rather than a deployable navigator.

entry.title: AirFlow: Context Preserving and Multi-Rate State Modeling for Air Quality Forecasting

author.name: Fan Yang, Nan Chen, Yijie Dong, Yuchen Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: AirFlow forecasts air quality with a pollutant-aware dual-stream design that avoids passing chemically different pollutant channels through one shared normalization and temporal backbone, modeling multi-rate dynamics and channel-specific distribution drift separately. Uses only station multivariate observations without extra inputs.

entry.title: Positioning Generative Artificial Intelligence in STEM Assessment: When to Require, Scaffold, or Restrict Its Use

author.name: Yizhu Gao, Zhongzhou Chen, Min Li, Xiaoming Zhai

entry.summary: Proposes a governance framework, grounded in Evidence Centered Design, for deciding when STEM assessments should restrict, scaffold, or require generative AI use. It supplies decision rules linking the construct being measured to the appropriate AI-use regime.

entry.title: Weather- and Location-Aware Agentic Dining Recommendation: Leveraging LLM World Knowledge for Region-Sensitive Contextual Reasoning

author.name: Kadharmoideen Fadurudeen

entry.summary: An agentic dining recommender that leverages LLM world knowledge to reason about weather, location, and culture jointly, rather than encoding weather-to-preference mappings as hand-crafted rules. Argues that culturally appropriate comfort food responses to weather are region-specific and unscalable to encode manually.

entry.title: Private Etymology: Designing Relational Reuse of Shared Symbols in Long-Term Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Miki Ueno

entry.summary: Proposes recording the provenance of dyad-specific expressions between a person and an AI, tracking how a shared symbol is proposed, negotiated, repaired, reused and revised so it can be safely invoked in later sessions. A concept and prototype for relational memory in long-term human-AI interaction.

entry.title: Eco-SoC: A Sustainable VLSI Architecture for Energy-Proportional Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Jatin Chopra

entry.summary: Proposes a system-on-chip architecture for sustainable edge AI whose dynamic precision-scaling logic adapts bit-width to real-time activation sparsity, reportedly cutting switching activity substantially. Frames sustainability as energy proportionality rather than static worst-case efficiency.

entry.title: LITEWAY: LIghtweight HAR via Temporal Efficient highWAY

author.name: Dominique Nshimyimana, Vitor Fortes Rey, Mengxi Liu, Bo Zhou, Paul Lukowicz

entry.summary: LITEWAY is a fully convolutional, modality-agnostic architecture for wearable human activity recognition that replaces recurrent temporal modeling with strided convolutions and convolution-attention pooling for parallelism and low latency. Evaluated across 16 HAR datasets.

entry.title: Learning to Modulate, Not to Cycle: Soft Actor---Critic Recovers Inverter-Style Heat-Pump Control

author.name: Faizan Ahmed, Aniket Dixit, James Brusey

entry.summary: Adds a compressor-wear cost to the reward for RL control of residential heat pumps and compares Soft Actor-Critic with PPO on the BOPTEST hydronic benchmark. SAC learns continuous modulation that keeps the compressor always engaged with zero daily start-ups, effectively rediscovering inverter-style control, while PPO degenerates into cycling.

entry.title: Tokenizer Generator Coupling in Medical Image Generation

author.name: Liam Chalcroft

entry.summary: Tests the common assumption that a tokenizer is neutral preprocessing for latent medical image generation, crossing discrete tokenizers, generator families, and sampler settings in a controlled small-resolution study. Rankings turn out to interact: the best quantizer depends on the generator, and sampler selection can flip apparent generator rankings.

entry.title: Conformal Calibration for Multi-Modal Regression with Missing Modalities

author.name: Ilia Azizi

entry.summary: Proposes a modality-aware conformal calibration layer for multi-modal regression, where a disagreement score across per-modality predictors modulates interval width and handles missing modalities. This avoids a single global quantile that averages over incompatible modality regimes.

entry.title: Population-Level Generative Modeling for Ranking Data

author.name: Zhaoyang Shi

entry.summary: Develops generative modeling for populations of rankings, enabling synthetic ranking data for privacy-preserving sharing, benchmark construction, and uncertainty quantification. The difficulty is that rankings are high-dimensional combinatorial objects with heterogeneous preference structures across a population.

entry.title: ARC: Augmented-Rank Conformalization for Changepoint Localization --- Finite-Sample Validity and Distribution-Robust Efficiency

author.name: Chenchen Peng, Mixia Wu, Qijing Yan, Zhiqi Shen, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: ARC builds conformal confidence sets for changepoint location using scores that depend on the data only through within-segment ranks, including rank-CUSUM channels and a frozen lightweight neural score. Rank-based construction preserves finite-sample coverage for any weight configuration while improving interval length under heavy tails and distribution shift.

entry.title: Contrastive Mask Fidelity: Reference-Free Auditing of Ground-Truth Masks in Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Shuaishuai Cao, Shuwei Peng, Meng Tang, Min Huang, Youjin Wang, Jie Chen, Jing Ouyang, Zhiwei Zhai

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free, reference-free metric that scores segmentation masks against image evidence by compositing keep-and-erase counterfactual views and asking a frozen vision-language model whether class evidence is concentrated inside the mask. Applied as an audit over roughly ten thousand image-class pairs across ten remote-sensing benchmarks, it exposes cases where high overlap scores reflect agreement with flawed labels rather than image faithfulness.

entry.title: Investigating Multimodal Informativity under Different Partner Visibility Conditions in Video-Mediated Dialogue

author.name: Esam Ghaleb, Hugh Mee Wong, Kristina Kobrock
